name: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) Screening By Culture
text:
Test code: 1302
Test name: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) Screening By Culture
Also known as: GBS;Streptococcus Screening For Pregnant Women;
Specimen: Rectal Swab,Vaginal Swab (VS)
Description: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) screening is a culture-based test performed to detect maternal colonization with Streptococcus agalactiae during pregnancy. The preferred specimen is a combined lower vaginal and rectal swab collected at 36 0/7 to 37 6/7 weeks' gestation. The specimen is cultured using selective enrichment media to maximize recovery of GBS, followed by organism identification and, where indicated, antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Detection of maternal GBS colonization identifies women who may benefit from intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis (IAP) to reduce the risk of early-onset neonatal GBS disease. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing is routinely performed only for GBS isolates from patients with a documented severe penicillin allergy when clindamycin susceptibility is required to guide prophylaxis. Recommended specimen: Combined lower vaginal and rectal swab (single or dual swab collection)
Tests included: High vaginal Swab ID, C & S, Rectal Swab ID C & S
Reported turnaround: After Three Days
Report date: 3-Days
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 7390.0

name: Lamotrigine
text:
Test code: 1103
Test name: Lamotrigine
Also known as: Lamictin; Lamictal
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect 3-5 mL of venous blood in a plain (red-top) tube or serum separator tube (SST). The sample should be drawn just before the next scheduled dose (trough level) to obtain an accurate assessment of steady-state concentration. After collection, allow the sample to clot, centrifuge, and separate serum promptly. Avoid hemolyzed or lipemic samples. Clearly indicate the time of last dose and the time of sample collection on the request form to aid in accurate interpretation.
Description: The Lamotrigine test is used to measure and monitor the concentration of lamotrigine in a patients blood. Lamotrigine is an anticonvulsant medication commonly prescribed for the management of epilepsy and bipolar disorder. Monitoring lamotrigine levels helps clinicians ensure therapeutic effectiveness while minimizing the risk of toxicity or subtherapeutic dosing. The test is particularly useful in cases of suspected non-compliance, drug interactions, dose adjustments, pregnancy, or when patients present with signs of toxicity such as dizziness, blurred vision, or skin rashes. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 10690.0

name: Osmolality (Urine)
text:
Test code: 1104
Test name: Osmolality (Urine)
Also known as: Urine Osmolality
Collection instructions: Collect a random urine sample in a clean, sterile, properly labeled container, ensuring no contamination during collection. The sample should be transported to the laboratory as soon as possible. If there is any delay, the specimen should be refrigerated at 2?8?C to preserve integrity. These conditions apply to urine organic acids, orotic acid, and urine osmolality testing. Clinical history should be provided to support interpretation, particularly for suspected metabolic disorders, renal concentrating defects, or polyuria-related conditions. Early or symptomatic collection may improve diagnostic yield where applicable.
Description: Urine Osmolality measures the concentration of solutes in urine and reflects the kidneys ability to concentrate or dilute urine. It is useful in assessing fluid balance, hydration status, and disorders of water regulation such as Diabetes Insipidus. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 3690.0

name: Oxalate (24 Hrs Urine)
text:
Test code: 1107
Test name: Oxalate (24 Hrs Urine)
Also known as: URINARY OXALATE
Specimen: 24 Hrs Urine
Collection instructions: Collect urine over 24 hours in a clean container pre-supplied with 10 mL of 6N HCl as preservative (do not discard). Discard the first morning urine, then collect all urine for the next 24 hours including the following mornings first sample. Keep the container tightly closed and refrigerated or in a cool place during the collection. Avoid spilling the acid and handle the container carefully; do not void directly into the container. Maintain adequate hydration and avoid high-oxalate foods (e.g., spinach, nuts, tea, chocolate) for at least 48 hours before and during collection unless otherwise advised.
Description: This test measures the total oxalate excretion in a 24-hour urine sample. Elevated levels may indicate primary or secondary hyperoxaluria, malabsorption syndromes, or increased risk of calcium oxalate kidney stones. It is particularly useful in the metabolic evaluation of patients with recurrent nephrolithiasis. Monitoring urinary oxalate can guide dietary modification and therapeutic interventions, and helps in assessing the effectiveness of stone-prevention strategies. Results should be interpreted alongside other metabolic urine parameters. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 6390.0

name: Potassium (24 Hrs Urine)
text:
Test code: 1120
Test name: Potassium (24 Hrs Urine)
Also known as: 24 hour K+ (URINE)
Specimen: 24 Hrs Urine
Collection instructions: Instructions for collection: Preferred start collection time is morning. Collect 24?hour urine without additives. Empty the bladder first thing in the morning or at the start time and discard this urine. Note the time as this is the start time of the 24 hours. For example 6:00 am Collect every drop of urine voided over the next 24 hours (i.e. upto the next morning e.g. 6:am on a Tuesday to 6:00 am Wednesday). Should one need to defecate and urinate at the same time, this urine should also be collected. Try as much as possible not to contaminate the urine with faeces. Keep the urine cold either on ice or refigerated. Stop time should be within 20 minutes of the start time the day before. E.g. if start time was 6:00 am Tuesday, stop time is between 5:50 am and 6:10 am Wednesday, during which time any urine passed must be collected. FOR SUBMITTING LABORATORIES /HOSPITALS If submitting an aliquot of the 24 hour urine, note the volume of 24 hour urine submited. Mix the sample well to a homogenous mixture and aliquote into a clean container. Submit the aliquot with clear documentation of the duration of collection and the volume of the 24 hour urine. Sample (Primary sample and alliquot) should be kept at 2?8 \'b0C
Description: 24 hour urine potassium is used to determine the cause of hypokalemia or hyperkalemia.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour
Standard price (KES): 790.0

name: Succinylacetone, Urine
text:
Test code: 1122
Test name: Succinylacetone, Urine
Specimen: Spot Urine
Collection instructions: Spot Urine: 10-15 ml of random (spot urine). Clinical History required including date of birth.
Description: The urine analysis demonstrates the presence of succinylacetone, a pathognomonic marker for tyrosinemia type I (fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase deficiency). Detection of this metabolite confirms a defect in the tyrosine catabolic pathway and supports the diagnosis of hereditary tyrosinemia type I. In the appropriate clinical context (hepatomegaly, coagulopathy, renal tubular dysfunction, or failure to thrive in infancy/childhood), this result warrants prompt initiation of disease-specific therapy (e.g., nitisinone) along with dietary management. Early treatment is critical to prevent progression to acute liver failure, renal impairment, or hepatocellular carcinoma. Correlation with plasma amino acid profile, liver function tests, renal function, and genetic confirmation is recommended. Family counseling and genetic testing may also\\~be\\~indicated. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 9390.0

name: Maternal Screen 2 (Double Marker) Free BHCG & PAPPA
text:
Test code: 1130
Test name: Maternal Screen 2 (Double Marker) Free BHCG & PAPPA
Also known as: Dual Down Screen; First-trimester Down Screen; Free BHCG / PAPPA
Specimen: Serum,EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Maternal Screen 2 (Double Marker) Free BHCG & PAPPA and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The Maternal Screen 2, or Dual Test, is a first-trimester maternal serum screening performed between 11-14 weeks' gestation. It measures free beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (free ß-hCG) and pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A (PAPP-A), and is typically combined with nuchal translucency (NT) measurement. The test assesses the risk of chromosomal abnormalities, primarily Trisomy 21 and Trisomy 18. Risk calculation incorporates maternal age, weight, gestational age, and other clinical factors. It is a screening tool; abnormal results should be followed by appropriate diagnostic procedures. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 7690.0

name: Maternal Screen 3 (Triple Screen)
text:
Test code: 1132
Test name: Maternal Screen 3 (Triple Screen)
Also known as: Triple Down Screen; Second-trimester Down Screen; AFP / hCG / E3
Specimen: Serum,EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Maternal Screen 3 (Triple Screen) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The Maternal Screen 3, also known as the Triple Test, is a second-trimester maternal serum screening performed between 15-20 weeks' gestation. It measures three biomarkers: alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), and unconjugated estriol (uE3). This test estimates the risk of fetal chromosomal abnormalities (such as Trisomy 21 and Trisomy 18) and neural tube defects. Results are interpreted in the context of maternal age, weight, gestational age, and other clinical factors. It is a non-diagnostic screening tool and abnormal results should prompt further diagnostic evaluation (e.g., ultrasound, amniocentesis). This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 9990.0

name: Diabetes CVD Risk Profile
text:
Test code: 1144
Test name: Diabetes CVD Risk Profile
Also known as: Diabetes CVS Risk Profile
Specimen: Serum,EDTA (Whole Blood)
Description: The Diabetes CVD (Cardiovascular Disease) Risk Profile is a comprehensive panel designed to assess both glycemic control and cardiovascular risk in patients with diabetes or suspected metabolic syndrome. It includes HbA1c for long-term glucose regulation, proBNP as a marker of cardiac strain and heart failure risk, and Troponin I for early detection of myocardial injury. Together, these markers provide valuable insight into the interplay between diabetes and cardiovascular health. This panel is recommended for diabetic patients during routine monitoring or when assessing cardiovascular risk. The addition of a Lipid Profile (total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, and triglycerides) helps identify atherogenic dyslipidemia commonly associated with diabetes, guiding both risk stratification and therapeutic interventions.
Tests included: Lipid Profile, HbA1C (Glycosylated Hemoglobin) A1C, Troponin I , pro-BNP (NT Pro BNP)
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 10990.0

Test name: Succinylacetone, Blood
Specimen: Newborn Screen Card
Collection instructions: Dried blood spot (DBS) heel prick or finger prick blood on special filter paper DBS card. DOB and clinical history required
Description: Blood succinylacetone testing demonstrates elevated succinylacetone, which is diagnostic for hereditary tyrosinemia type I due to fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase deficiency. The presence of succinylacetone in blood is highly specific and can be detected even in the newborn period, making it a reliable screening and confirmatory marker. This finding indicates a block in tyrosine catabolism, leading to accumulation of toxic metabolites that cause progressive liver, renal, and systemic complications. In the clinical setting, this result necessitates urgent initiation of targeted therapy with nitisinone and dietary restriction of tyrosine and phenylalanine, as early treatment dramatically improves prognosis and reduces the risk of liver failure or hepatocellular carcinoma. Correlation with urine succinylacetone, plasma amino acids, liver and renal function, and confirmatory molecular genetic testing is advised. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 10990.0

name: AH50 (Alternative Complement Pathway Function)
text:
Test code: 1207
Test name: AH50 (Alternative Complement Pathway Function)
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for AH50 (Alternative Complement Pathway Function) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The AH50 test evaluates the function of the alternative complement pathway by measuring serum-mediated lysis of rabbit erythrocytes. It helps detect deficiencies or dysfunction of factors B, D, properdin, C3C9, and is complementary to the CH50 test, which assesses the classical pathway. Clinically, it is used in patients with recurrent infections (especially meningococcal), or in disorders of complement regulation such as atypical HUS and C3 glomerulopathy. Low or absent AH50 suggests an alternative pathway defect, while normal results usually exclude complete\\~deficiency. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Red Cell Antibody Indentification (RBC ID Panel / Monospecific DAT)
text:
Test code: 1213
Test name: Red Cell Antibody Indentification (RBC ID Panel / Monospecific DAT)
Also known as: RBC Antibody Panel x11 markers; Alloantibody Identification Panel; Monospecific DAT
Specimen: Clotted,EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood and any other listed specimens for Red Cell Antibody Identification (RBC ID Panel). Fast only if the request or a component test requires it. Label all containers with patient and collection details.
Description: Red Blood Cell (RBC) Antibody Identification Panel or Monospecific DAT is a confirmatory immunohematology test used to identify and characterize unexpected red cell alloantibodies detected following a positive antibody screening test. Patient plasma or serum is tested against a panel of reagent red cells with known antigen profiles using the Indirect Antiglobulin Test (IAT) (gel card, column agglutination, or tube method). The reaction pattern allows identification of specific clinically significant antibodies such as Anti-D, Anti-C, Anti-E, Anti-c, Anti-K, Anti-Fya, or Anti-Jka, and detection of multiple antibodies where present. The test is essential for safe transfusion practice, antenatal care, and investigation of transfusion reactions. Identified clinically significant antibodies guide the selection of antigen-negative, crossmatch-compatible blood units and help prevent hemolytic transfusion reactions and hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN). Results are reported with antibody specificity, autocontrol status, and interpretive comments, and the antibody history should be permanently recorded in the patients transfusion record. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 1 week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 9690.0

name: Cysticercosis IgG (Taenia Solium IgG) CSF
text:
Test code: 1222
Test name: Cysticercosis IgG (Taenia Solium IgG) CSF
Also known as: Cysticercus IgG Antibodies Test: Pig Tapeworm Antibodies Test
Specimen: CSF
Collection instructions: CSF 3-5 mL
Description: The Cysticercosis IgG antibody test is a serologic assay used to support the diagnosis of cysticercosis, especially neurocysticercosis, caused by Taenia solium larvae. It detects IgG antibodies in serum or CSF. A positive result suggests prior or active infection but must be interpreted alongside clinical findings and neuroimaging, as it cannot distinguish between active and past infection. False positives may occur due to cross-reactivity with other parasitic infections, while false negatives are possible in cases of localized lesions, early infection, or immunosuppression. The test is most useful in patients from endemic regions who present with unexplained seizures or intracranial cystic/ring-enhancing lesions. However, it is not suitable as a screening tool in asymptomatic individuals due to high background seroprevalence. Negative results do not rule out disease, especially in cases with single or calcified lesions. A positive test should prompt further diagnostic evaluation including brain imaging and possible CSF analysis, with management guided by a multidisciplinary team. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 3690.0

name: HMGCR Antibody (Anti–3-Hydroxy-3-Methylglutaryl-CoA Reductase Antibodies)
text:
Test code: 1235
Test name: HMGCR Antibody (Anti–3-Hydroxy-3-Methylglutaryl-CoA Reductase Antibodies)
Also known as: HMGCR Ab (Anti–3-Hydroxy-3-Methylglutaryl-CoA Reductase Ab)
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for HMGCR Antibody (Anti?3-Hydroxy-3-Methylglutaryl-CoA Reductase Antibodies) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The HMGCR antibody test detects autoantibodies directed against 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase, the key enzyme in cholesterol synthesis. The presence of these antibodies is strongly associated with immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM), particularly in patients with prior statin exposure, though cases also occur in statin-naïve individuals, especially younger patients. Clinically, affected patients typically present with progressive proximal muscle weakness, markedly elevated creatine kinase (CK) levels, and muscle fiber necrosis with minimal inflammation on biopsy. Unlike statin-related toxic myopathy, HMGCR antibodyassociated IMNM usually persists or progresses despite statin withdrawal and often requires immunosuppressive therapy. A positive test supports the diagnosis of HMGCR-associated IMNM, while a negative result does not exclude other inflammatory or necrotizing myopathies such as SRP-positive IMNM or paraneoplastic forms. The antibody may remain detectable despite clinical improvement and is not reliable for disease monitoring. Interpretation should always be integrated with the clinical picture, CK levels, muscle biopsy findings, and other myositis-specific antibody\\~results. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 13390.0

Description: The diphtheria antibody test measures circulating IgG antibodies against Corynebacterium diphtheriae toxin, helping assess immunity status following vaccination or infection. It is primarily used to determine whether a patient has protective immunity, guide booster vaccination decisions, or evaluate immune response after immunization. The test is especially useful in individuals with uncertain vaccination history, immunocompromised patients, or before travel to areas with diphtheria risk. Results should be interpreted in the context of vaccination records, clinical history, and other immunological\\~assessments. text:
Test code: 1321
Test name: Hepatitis B (HBV) Genotyping (reflex test on recent HBV Viral Load)
Also known as: HBV Genotype Reflex Testing

Collection instructions: Sample Type: EDTA Plasma (preferred), Serum (acceptable) Collection & Handling: Performed on an already submitted sample; no additional collection required NOTE: This is a REFLEX TEST performed on samples with a recent detectable HBV viral load Adequate viral load is required for successful genotyping (typically =1,000 IU/mL); lower levels may result in amplification failure The existing HBV DNA result will be utilized for this analysis
Description: This assay performs molecular genotyping of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) using PCR-based sequencing methods to determine the viral genotype (AJ). It is conducted as a reflex test on samples with a recent detectable HBV viral load. HBV genotyping provides clinically relevant information for guiding antiviral therapy selection, predicting treatment response (e.g., interferon sensitivity), and offering prognostic insight into disease progression, including the risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Successful analysis requires sufficient circulating viral DNA; low viral loads may lead to test failure. This test is intended for use in patients with confirmed HBV infection and detectable viremia. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Protein C
text:
Test code: 1348
Test name: Protein C
Also known as: PROTEIN-C
Specimen: Citrated
Description: Protein C is a natural anticoagulant that plays a key role in controlling blood clot formation by inactivating factors Va and VIIIa. This test measures the functional activity of Protein C in plasma to help identify deficiencies that may predispose individuals to an increased risk of venous thromboembolism. It is commonly used in the evaluation of patients with unexplained or recurrent blood clots, a family history of thrombophilia, or as part of a thrombophilia workup. The test may also be useful in assessing liver function and in cases of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC).

Description: Antithrombin (also known as Antithrombin III) is a key inhibitor of several activated coagulation factors, particularly thrombin and factor Xa. Antithrombin deficiency can be inherited or acquired (e.g., due to liver disease, nephrotic syndrome, or disseminated intravascular coagulation) and is an important part of a thrombophilia workup in patients with unexplained or recurrent venous thrombosis.

name: Bilirubin Direct
text:
Test code: 1502
Test name: Bilirubin Direct
Also known as: Conjugated Bilirubin
Specimen: Serum,Lithium Heparin
Collection instructions: Venous blood collected in a plain red-top or serum separator tube (SST). Allow the blood to clot and centrifuge promptly to separate serum. Avoid hemolysis and exposure to light, as bilirubin is light-sensitive. Transport serum in an amber-colored tube or wrap the tube in foil to protect from light. Protect from light during collection, storage and shipment. Allow serum tube to clot completely at room temperature. Separate serum or plasma from cells within 2 hours of collection.
Description: Verdana; ;; The Direct Bilirubin test measures the level of conjugated (direct) bilirubin in the blood. Direct bilirubin is formed in the liver when unconjugated bilirubin is processed for excretion. This test helps evaluate liver function, detect bile duct obstruction, and differentiate types of jaundice. Elevated direct bilirubin levels may indicate hepatocellular disease or cholestasis. It is often used alongside total and indirect bilirubin tests to provide a complete picture of bilirubin metabolism. Used for the diagnosis of hyperbilirubinemia in the evaluation of jaundice, suspected liver and haemolytic disease.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour

name: ALT Alanine Aminotransferase
text:
Test code: 1503
Test name: ALT Alanine Aminotransferase
Also known as: SGPT;Alanine Aminotransferase
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: The preferred specimen is serum or plasma collected in a serum separator tube (SST) or green-top tube (sodium or lithium heparin). Allow the specimen to clot at room temperature, separate from cells within 2 hours, and transfer 2 mL (minimum 1 mL) to a transport tube. Samples should be stored and transported refrigerated (2-8\'b0C); freeze if analysis is delayed. Allow serum tube to clot completely at room temperature. Separate serum or plasma from cells within 2 hours of collection.
Description: Verdana; ;; ALT (Alanine Aminotransferase) is a liver-specific enzyme released into the bloodstream when liver cells are damaged. It is a key marker for detecting and monitoring liver conditions such as acute and chronic viral hepatitis, nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), alcohol-related liver disease, ischemic hepatopathy, autoimmune hepatitis, cholestasis, and suspected malignant liver infiltration. ALT is more specific for liver injury than AST, as it is found primarily in the liver and has a longer half-life, while AST is present in multiple organs. ALT elevations are rarely seen outside of liver disease and persist longer than AST in cases of hepatic injury. Quantitative determination of ALT is used in the diagnosis and follow-up of acute and chronic liver injury .
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour
Standard price (KES): 790.0

Description: ;; AST (Aspartate Aminotransferase) is an enzyme found in the liver, heart, skeletal muscle, kidneys, brain, and red blood cells. AST is used to diagnose and monitor liver diseases such as viral hepatitis, NAFLD, alcohol-related liver disease, ischemic hepatopathy, autoimmune hepatitis, cholestasis, and malignant infiltration. Though less liver-specific than ALT, AST may be more sensitive in alcohol-related and autoimmune liver conditions. Elevated AST may also indicate cardiac or muscle injury, Quantitative determination of AST is used in the diagnosis and monitoring of acute and chronic liver injury.

name: ALP Alkaline Phosphatase
text:
Test code: 1505
Test name: ALP Alkaline Phosphatase
Also known as: ALP;Alkaline Phosphatase
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Allow the specimen to clot at room temperature, separate from cells within 2 hours, and transfer 2 mL (minimum 1 mL) to a transport tube. Samples should be stored and transported refrigerated (2 8\'b0C); freeze if analysis is delayed.
Description: ALP (Alkaline Phosphatase) is an enzyme found mainly in the liver and bones and is used to detect and monitor liver and bone diseases. In the liver, ALP rises with cholestasis and biliary obstruction, especially in obstructive jaundice. In the bones, it increases with osteoblastic activity, seen in conditions like Paget s disease, rickets, osteomalacia, fractures, and bone tumors. Levels may be naturally higher in growing children. Low ALP is rare but may occur in hypophosphatasia, growth hormone deficiency, or multiple myeloma. Though not liver-specific, ALP is a key marker for biliary and bone disorders.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour

Description: Gamma-glutamyltransferase (GGT) is an enzyme measured in serum or plasma to aid in the diagnosis and monitoring of hepatobiliary diseases and serves as a screening tool for alcohol abuse. Although present in multiple tissues, serum GGT primarily reflects liver activity. GGT testing is often performed alongside ALT, AST, ALP, bilirubin, and albumin during liver function assessment. Elevated levels are associated with among others liver disease, excessive alcohol intake, obesity, and the use of certain drugs. It is one of the most sensitive markers for alcohol-related liver damage.

name: Ammonia (NH3)
text:
Test code: 1710
Test name: Ammonia (NH3)
Also known as: AMMONIA; NH3
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Tubes should be filled completely and kept tightly stoppered at all times. Sample stability is 30 minutes at 15-25 \'b0C, otherwise centrifuge to separate plasma and place immediately on ice and transport to the lab at 2?8 \'b0C. Test analysis should be ideally performed within 60 minutes of venipuncture if the plasma is not frozen, or else freeze separated plasma immediately and transport to the lab soonest possible.
Description: Quantitative determination of Ammonia is useful in evaluation of the status of existing liver disease and diagnosis and follow up of in- born errors of metabolism. Ammonia is produced in the gastrointestinal tract during the breakdown of nitrogen-containing compounds. It is normally converted to urea in the liver through the urea cycle and then excreted. High ammonia levels (hyperammonemia) can be toxic to the brain and may indicate liver dysfunction. In infants, it can result from inherited urea cycle disorders or Reye s syndrome. In adults, elevated ammonia is often seen in liver failure or hepatic encephalopathy caused by cirrhosis or severe hepatitis.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour
Standard price (KES): 2390.0

name: CK-MB
text:
Test code: 1802
Test name: CK-MB
Also known as: Creatine Kinase MB CPK-MBCreatine PhosphokinaseCKMB
Specimen: Serum,Lithium Heparin
Collection instructions: CK?MB is temperature-sensitive. To prevent inaccurate results, avoid keeping the sample at or above 32?\'b0C.
Description: CK-MB is the muscle-brain isoenzyme of creatine kinase and serves as a key biomarker for diagnosing acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and other cardiac injuries such as myocarditis and heart failure. It becomes detectable in serum within 3-8 hours after symptom onset and remains elevated depending on disease progression. Though cardiac troponins are now the preferred and more specific markers for myocardial injury, CK-MB remains a valuable alternative when troponin assays are unavailable, particularly when measured using mass assays. CK-MB may also rise in non-cardiac conditions like rhabdomyolysis and stroke, so it is often interpreted alongside other markers such as total CK, myoglobin, and troponin.

Description: Cardiac Troponin T (cTnT) is a protein found in the heart and is released into the blood when the heart muscle is damaged. It is a highly specific and sensitive marker for heart attacks (both STEMI and NSTEMI). High-sensitivity tests (cTnT-hs) can detect even small amounts of heart injury within 1 to 3 hours of symptom onset. Elevated levels, together with symptoms and ECG changes, help confirm or rule out a heart attack. cTnT may also rise in other conditions like heart failure, kidney disease, or severe infections. Ongoing elevations can indicate long-term heart stress. The test is also useful for monitoring heart health, guiding treatment, and assessing risk in various heart-related conditions

Levels above 1.7 mmol/L (150 mg/dL) increase cardiovascular risk, while levels above 2.3 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) indicate high risk. Testing is useful in evaluating conditions such as diabetes, liver disease, kidney disorders, and endocrine abnormalities.

name: Rhesus (Rh) Anti-D Antibody Titre
text:
Test code: 2222
Test name: Rhesus (Rh) Anti-D Antibody Titre
Also known as: Rh Antibodies; Antenatal Screen for Rh Antibodies
Specimen: Serum,Whole Blood
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Rhesus (Rh) Anti-D Antibody Titre and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: Rhesus (Rh) antibody titre testing is performed to detect and quantify maternal alloantibodies, particularly anti-D antibodies, in Rh-negative pregnant women. This test helps assess the risk of hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN). A rising titre, especially above a critical threshold (commonly 1:16 or 1:32 depending on the laboratory), indicates increased risk of fetal hemolysis and necessitates closer monitoring, including ultrasound for signs of fetal anemia and possible referral for middle cerebral artery Doppler studies or intrauterine transfusion. Clinicians should order Rh antibody titres early in pregnancy for all Rh-negative women and repeat at intervals if antibodies are detected. It is essential to differentiate passive anti-D from prophylactic Rh immunoglobulin (RhIg) administration versus active immunization due to sensitization. Documentation of antibody specificity and monitoring of titre trends is vital for management decisions. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 3390.0

text:

Specimen: Fluids
Description: "The Lactate (Fluid) test measures the concentration of lactate in body fluids such as pleural, peritoneal, or synovial fluid. Lactate is a byproduct of anaerobic metabolism and serves as a sensitive marker of local tissue hypoxia, inflammation, or infection within the fluid compartment. Elevated lactate levels in body fluids may indicate bacterial peritonitis, empyema, intestinal ischemia, or septic arthritis, and can aid in differentiating infectious from non-infectious causes of effusion. This test is especially useful in critically ill patients or when evaluating unexplained fluid accumulation. Proper collection into sterile containers and rapid transport to the lab (ideally on ice) are essential, as lactate is metabolically active and may degrade if delayed"

text:
Test code: 2707

Also known as: Pancreatic alpha amylasePancreatic amylaseAlpha amylaseAmylase alpha
Description: The Amylase (Fluid) test measures the concentration of amylase enzyme in body fluids such as peritoneal, pleural, or pericardial fluid. Amylase is primarily produced by the pancreas and salivary glands and plays a key role in the digestion of carbohydrates. Elevated amylase levels in non-blood fluids may indicate conditions such as pancreatitis, pancreatic duct leakage, intestinal perforation, or inflammation involving adjacent organs. This test is particularly useful for evaluating abdominal effusions or pleural fluid in patients with suspected pancreatic disease, ruptured viscera, or salivary gland pathology. Amylase levels in fluid are interpreted alongside serum amylase, fluid protein, LDH, and cell count to support differential diagnosis. Proper sample collection, handling, and transport are essential, and the fluid should be collected in a sterile container and analyzed promptly to avoid enzymatic degradation.

This test is particularly useful for evaluating abdominal effusions or pleural fluid in patients with suspected pancreatic disease, ruptured viscera, or salivary gland pathology. Amylase levels in fluid are interpreted alongside serum amylase, fluid protein, LDH, and cell count to support differential diagnosis. Proper sample collection, handling, and transport are essential, and the fluid should be collected in a sterile container and analyzed promptly to avoid enzymatic degradation.

name: IGHV Mutation Status by NGS
text:
Test code: 2802
Test name: IGHV Mutation Status by NGS
Also known as: IGHV Mutation for CLL
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Description: IGHV Mutation Status by NGS is a molecular assay used in the diagnostic and prognostic work-up of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). Using next-generation sequencing, the test analyzes the immunoglobulin heavy chain variable (IGHV) gene rearrangement in leukemic B cells and compares it with the closest germline IGHV sequence to determine the degree of somatic hypermutation. Cases with <98% identity are reported as mutated IGHV, while those with ?98% identity are unmutated IGHV, in line with iwCLL/WHO/ICC recommendations. IGHV status is a stable, disease-defining biomarker with major clinical impact: mutated IGHV is associated with indolent disease and longer progression-free and overall survival, whereas unmutated IGHV predicts more aggressive behavior and earlier need for therapy. Results inform risk stratification at diagnosis and may influence treatment selection (e.g., likelihood of durable response to chemo-immunotherapy versus preference for targeted agents). The test requires peripheral blood or bone marrow with adequate tumor burden and is typically performed once, as IGHV status does not change over the disease course.
Reported turnaround: 2-3 Weeks
Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: TUE & FRI
Standard price (KES): 49690.0

name: IGHV Mutation Status by Sanger Sequencing
text:
Test code: 2803
Test name: IGHV Mutation Status by Sanger Sequencing
Also known as: IGHV Mutation Status by Sanger Sequencing for CLL
Description: IGHV Mutation Status by Sanger Sequencing is a molecular assay used in the diagnostic and prognostic evaluation of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). The test involves PCR amplification of the rearranged immunoglobulin heavy chain variable (IGHV) gene from leukemic B cells, followed by Sanger sequencing and comparison with the closest germline IGHV sequence in international databases (e.g., IMGT). A sequence identity of <98% defines mutated IGHV, while ?98% defines unmutated IGHV, in accordance with iwCLL, WHO, and ICC criteria. IGHV mutation status is a robust, stable prognostic biomarker in CLL: mutated IGHV is associated with more indolent disease and prolonged survival, whereas unmutated IGHV correlates with aggressive disease and earlier treatment requirement. Results support baseline risk stratification and may guide therapeutic decisions, including the expected durability of response to chemo-immunotherapy versus targeted agents. The assay is typically performed once per patient, as IGHV status remains stable over time, and requires peripheral blood or bone marrow with sufficient clonal B-cell burden.
Reported turnaround: 3-4 Weeks
Report date: 4-Weeks
Testing days: TUE & FRI
Standard price (KES): 27690.0

name: Calcium (24 Hrs Urine)
text:
Test code: 3508
Test name: Calcium (24 Hrs Urine)
Also known as: URINARY CALCIUM
Specimen: 24 Hrs Urine
Collection instructions: Preferred start collection time is morning Collect in 24 hour urine container with 20?30 mL of 6 mol/L HCl to prevent calcium salt precipitation. Addition of HCl after collection may not completely dissolve precipitated calcium and is therefore discouraged. Empty the bladder first thing in the morning or at the start time and discard this urine. Note the time as this is the start time of the 24 hours. For example 6:00 am Collect every drop of urine voided over the next 24 hours (i.e. upto the next morning e.g. 6:am on a Tuesday to 6:00 am Wednesday). Should one need to defecate and urinate at the same time, this urine should also be collected. Try as much as possible not to contaminate the urine with faeces. Keep the urine cold either on ice or refigerated. Stop time should be within 20 minutes of the start time the day before. E.g. if start time was 6:00 am Tuesday, stop time is between 5:50 am and 6:10 am during which time any urine passed must be collected. FOR SUBMITTING LABORATORIES /HOSPITALS If submitting an aliquot of the 24 hour urine, note the volume of 24 hour urine submited. Mix the sample well to a homogenous mixture and aliquote into a clean container. Submit the aliquot with clear documentation of the duration of collection and the volume of the 24 hour urine. Sample (Primary sample and alliquot) should be kept at 2?8 \'b0C
Description: Determination of 24 hour urine calcium is useful in the evaluation of nephrolithiasis, renal disease, hyperparathyroidism, hyper/hypocalcaemia and hypercalciuria.

text:
Test code: 3513

Collection instructions: General instructions Preferred start collection time is morning. Collect in detergent?free container. Note the time as this is the start time of the 24 hours. For example 6:00 am Collect every drop of urine voided over the next 24 hours (i.e. upto the next morning e.g. 6:am on a Tuesday to 6:00 am Wednesday). Should one need to defecate and urinate at the same time, this urine should also be collected. Try as much as possible not to contaminate the urine with faeces. Keep the urine cold either on ice or refigerated. Stop time should be within 20 minutes of the start time the day before. Mix the sample well to a homogenous mixture and aliquote into a clean container. Submit the aliquot with clear documentation of the duration of collection

name: Water Microbiological Analysis (Total Coliforms/Total Viable Count)
text:
Test code: 3881
Test name: Water Microbiological Analysis (Total Coliforms/Total Viable Count)
Also known as: Faecal Coliforms
Specimen: Fluids
Collection instructions: To test water for Total Coliforms and Total Viable Count (TVC), collect the sample in a sterile, sealable bottle-preferably one containing sodium thiosulfate if the water is chlorinated. Choose a clean, representative sampling point, disinfect the outlet (by flaming or using alcohol), and allow the water to flow for 2-3 minutes before collecting. Fill the bottle without touching the inside, leaving a small air gap, and seal it immediately. Label the sample clearly with the source, date, and time, and transport it in a cool box at ~4?C to the lab within 6 hours, ensuring analysis is done within 24 hours. Include a completed submission form or chain of custody with test details. Proper sampling is critical for accurate microbiological assessment, especially for compliance or public health monitoring.
Description: Total Coliforms, Faecal Coliforms/ E.coli, Total Viable Count This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days

Description: Luteinizing hormone (LH) is a glycoprotein hormone produced by the anterior pituitary, acting alongside FSH to regulate the growth and function of the ovaries and testes. In women, LH surges mid-cycle to trigger ovulation and support corpus luteum formation. In men, LH stimulates testosterone production in Leydig cells. Measurement of LH is used to assess disorders in the hypothalamus-pituitary-gonadal axis and is helpful in diagnosing conditions like polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), amenorrhea, menopausal status, and gonadal insufficiency. When combined with FSH testing, it aids in evaluating reproductive and endocrine function.

name: FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) - Endocrine
text:
Test code: 4105
Test name: FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) - Endocrine
Also known as: FSH;Follicle Stimulating Hormone
Specimen: Serum,Lithium Heparin
Collection instructions: Serum collected using standard sampling tubes or tubes containing separating gel. Li?heparin, K2?EDTA and K3?EDTA plasma.
Description: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) is hormone produced by the anterior pituitary. Acting together with luteinizing hormone (LH), it stimulates the growth and function of the gonads. In women, it promotes follicular development and the production of estrogen, with levels peaking around mid-cycle and rising significantly during menopause due to reduced estrogen feedback. In men, FSH supports spermatogenesis by acting on the seminiferous tubules. Measurement of FSH levels, often in conjunction with LH, is useful in evaluating conditions such as menstrual irregularities, polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), menopausal status, infertility, and gonadal dysfunction. Low FSH levels in men may be associated with azoospermia.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour

name: Progesterone
text:
Test code: 4108
Test name: Progesterone
Specimen: Serum
Description: The Progesterone test the quantitatively measures progesterone levels in human serum or plasma. Progesterone is a steroid hormone primarily produced by the corpus luteum and placenta during pregnancy. It plays a key role in preparing the endometrium for implantation, supporting early pregnancy, and inhibiting uterine contractions. Clinically, this test is valuable in assessing ovulation, luteal phase adequacy, and progesterone-related disorders such as infertility or ectopic pregnancy. Elevated levels are expected in the luteal phase and throughout pregnancy, while low levels may suggest ovulatory dysfunction or luteal phase defects.

Description: The Folate test is a quantitatively measures folate (vitamin B9) levels in the human serum, aiding in the diagnosis and management of anemia and nutritional deficiencies. name: Growth Hormone
text:
Test code: 4115
Test name: Growth Hormone
Also known as: Human Growth Hormone;HGH
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Serum collected using standard sampling tubes or tubes containing separating gel. Li?heparin, K2?EDTA and K3?EDTA plasma.
Description: This assay quantitatively measures human growth hormone in serum and plasma. hGH, secreted by the pituitary gland, plays a vital role in stimulating growth, especially bone elongation, through the production of IGF-1 in the liver. Its secretion is pulsatile and regulated by factors such as GHRH, somatostatin, sleep, exercise, and glucose levels. hGH levels vary by age, sex, and physiological state, peaking in adolescence and declining with age. Excess hGH can lead to gigantism (in children) or acromegaly (in adults), often caused by pituitary adenomas, while deficiency can cause growth retardation in children and metabolic disturbances in adults. Accurate diagnosis relies on stimulation or suppression tests due to the hormone s variability throughout the day.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour
Standard price (KES): 3390.0

name: ACTH - Adrenocorticotropic Hormone
text:
Test code: 4119
Test name: ACTH - Adrenocorticotropic Hormone
Also known as: ACTH Adrenocorticotropic Hormone
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: ;; Collect in K2?EDTA and K3?EDTA plasma. Only use pre-cooled sampling vials . After drawing the blood, put the vials immediately on ice . Use a cooled centrifuge to separate the plasma. Measure samples immediately or freeze them at -20 C
Description: The ACTH test measures the level of adrenocorticotropic hormone in the blood. ACTH is produced by the pituitary gland and stimulates the adrenal glands to release cortisol, a hormone essential for stress response, metabolism, and immune function. This test helps evaluate adrenal and pituitary gland function and is often used to diagnose conditions such as Cushing s syndrome, Addison s disease, and secondary adrenal insufficiency. Low ACTH levels usually suggest that the pituitary gland isn t producing enough hormone, often due to high cortisol levels from conditions like Cushing s syndrome or long-term steroid use. High ACTH levels may indicate that the adrenal glands aren t producing enough cortisol, as seen in Addison s disease, or may result from overproduction by a pituitary or ectopic tumor. ACTH results should always be considered alongside cortisol levels for accurate diagnosis. ACTH is used in the assessment of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis (HPA axis or HTPA axis) disorders.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour
Standard price (KES): 3990.0

name: DHEA-S (Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulphate)
text:
Test code: 4120
Test name: DHEA-S (Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulphate)
Also known as: DHEASDehydroepiandrosterone Sulfate Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulphate
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Serum. Plasma: Li?heparin, K2?EDTA and K3?EDTA plasma.
Description: The DHEA-S test measures the level of dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate, a hormone produced mainly by the adrenal glands. DHEA-S serves as a precursor to male and female sex hormones (androgens and estrogens) and plays a role in puberty, reproductive function, and overall hormonal balance. This test is often used to evaluate adrenal gland function and investigate symptoms of hormone imbalances such as excessive hair growth (hirsutism), irregular menstrual cycles, infertility, or early or delayed puberty. Low levels of DHEA-S may indicate underactive adrenal glands (adrenal insufficiency), aging, or pituitary dysfunction that reduces hormone production. They can also occur due to chronic illness or long-term use of corticosteroids. On the other hand, high DHEA-S levels are often linked to conditions that cause excessive androgen production, such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), adrenal tumors, or congenital adrenal hyperplasia. In rare cases, elevated levels may suggest an adrenal cancer. Because DHEA-S is produced almost exclusively by the adrenal glands, abnormal levels can provide important insight into adrenal health and hormonal balance. Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour

Dietary foods and several medicines can affect results, so collection preparation and interpretation with symptoms and imaging are important. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: ACE Angiotensin Converting Enzyme (Serum)
text:
Test code: 4123
Test name: ACE Angiotensin Converting Enzyme (Serum)
Also known as: A.C.E.
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: History of patient using Angiotensin Converting Enzyme Inhibitor therapy should be ruled out.
Description: ACE is an enzyme involved in the renin-angiotensin system, playing a key role in blood pressure regulation by converting angiotensin I to angiotensin II. Measurement of serum ACE levels is primarily used as a biochemical marker in the diagnosis and monitoring of sarcoidosis, a multisystem granulomatous disease. Elevated ACE levels may also be observed in other conditions such as Gaucher s disease, leprosy, and certain liver disorders, while reduced levels may be associated with ACE inhibitor therapy. The test is useful for supporting clinical suspicion and monitoring response to treatment in patients with sarcoidosis.

name: Testosterone (Total)
text:
Test code: 4124
Test name: Testosterone (Total)
Also known as: Total TestosteroneTestosterone
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Serum. Plasma: Li?heparin, K2?EDTA and K3?EDTA plasma.
Description: The Total Testosterone test measures the overall level of testosterone in the blood, including both the hormone bound to proteins and the small amount that circulates freely. Testosterone is a key sex hormone involved in the development of male reproductive tissues, muscle mass, bone density, and body hair, though it is also present in females in smaller amounts. This test helps evaluate symptoms such as infertility, low sex drive, erectile dysfunction, irregular menstrual cycles, or signs of hormonal imbalance. It is commonly used to assess conditions like hypogonadism, polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), and certain adrenal or pituitary disorders. Low total testosterone levels can be a sign of hypogonadism, where the body doesn t produce enough testosterone. In men, this may lead to symptoms like fatigue, reduced libido, erectile dysfunction, loss of muscle mass, and mood changes. It can result from aging, pituitary gland disorders, testicular injury, or chronic illnesses. In women, low testosterone is less common but may contribute to low libido and fatigue. Conversely, high testosterone levels in men may be due to testosterone supplementation, anabolic steroid use, or certain tumors. In women, high levels are often linked to conditions like polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), leading to symptoms such as excessive hair growth, acne, and irregular periods.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 2990.0

name: Parathyroid Hormone Intact (PTH)
text:
Test code: 4125
Test name: Parathyroid Hormone Intact (PTH)
Also known as: Intact Parathyroid Hormone (iPTH);Parathormone
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood),Serum
Collection instructions: EDTA plasma sample is preferred as PTH is stable for >24 hours at room temperature in whole blood anticoagulated with EDTA. Serum collected using standard sampling tube (SST) should be centrifuged immediately because of instability of PTH in unseparated serum, and the sample should be kept at 2-8 degrees when transported to the lab within 2 days of collection.
Description: ;; The Parathyroid Hormone Intact (PTH) test measures the level of parathyroid hormone in the blood to assess how well the parathyroid glands are functioning. PTH plays a key role in regulating calcium, phosphorus, and vitamin D levels in the body. This test is often ordered to help diagnose the cause of abnormal calcium levels. Low parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels typically suggest hypoparathyroidism, a condition where the parathyroid glands produce too little hormone. This can lead to low blood calcium levels, causing symptoms like muscle cramps, tingling, or even seizures. It may result from autoimmune disease, neck surgery, or certain genetic conditions. On the other hand, high PTH levels often indicate hyperparathyroidism, where one or more parathyroid glands produce too much hormone. This can lead to high calcium levels in the blood and symptoms such as bone pain, kidney stones, fatigue, and abdominal discomfort. Elevated PTH can also occur in response to low calcium or vitamin D levels, especially in chronic kidney disease. The test provides valuable information about bone metabolism and overall mineral balance. Quantitative determination of PTH in serum in the evaluation of Chronic Kidney disease- Mineral Bone disorder (CKD -MBD), Calcium and phosphate disorders and primary Parathyroid disease.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 3390.0

name: Insulin Autoantibodies (IAA)
text:
Test code: 4137
Test name: Insulin Autoantibodies (IAA)
Also known as: IAA; Insulin Autoantibodies Anti-Insulin Antibodies
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Insulin Autoantibodies (IAA) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The Insulin Autoantibody (IAA) test detects antibodies directed against endogenous insulin and is primarily used in the evaluation of autoimmune Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM), particularly in young children. IAA is often the first autoantibody to appear in genetically susceptible individuals and is most commonly seen in children under five years old with new-onset T1DM. The presence of IAA indicates an autoimmune response targeting insulin-producing ß-cells. A positive IAA result supports the diagnosis of autoimmune T1DM, especially when detected alongside other antibodies such as GAD65, IA-2, and ZNT8. Its diagnostic utility decreases with age and in individuals who have been treated with exogenous insulin, as this can induce antibody formation. A negative IAA result does not rule out T1DM, and the test should be interpreted in the clinical context along with other autoantibody and metabolic markers. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 7390.0

Description: Qunatitative determination of Haptoglobin is used to detect and assess hemolysis. Haptoglobin is a liver-derived glycoprotein that binds free hemoglobin released during red blood cell destruction, forming complexes cleared by the liver. Its levels drop in hemolytic anemia or liver dysfunction due to rapid consumption, while they increase during inflammation as it is an acute phase reactant. Therefore, haptoglobin measurement in serum or plasma helps diagnose and monitor hemolysis, inflammation, and liver conditions. Low levels can also occur in cirrhosis, splenomegaly, or malnutrition, while elevated levels may be seen in infections, cancer, or tissue damage.

name: Lead (Blood)
text:
Test code: 4154
Test name: Lead (Blood)
Also known as: Lead
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Lead (Blood) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: Blood lead level (BLL) testing is the gold standard for diagnosing lead exposure and toxicity. It reflects recent or ongoing exposure and is used for both screening and monitoring, particularly in children, pregnant women, and workers in high-risk occupations. BLL is reported in micrograms per deciliter (µg/dL), with any detectable level considered abnormal in children, as no safe threshold has been established. Elevated BLLs should prompt evaluation of exposure sources, clinical assessment for toxicity, and possible environmental or occupational interventions. In symptomatic individuals or those with very high levels, further evaluation including renal function, hemoglobin, and chelation eligibility may be necessary. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: BRCA 1 and BRCA 2 Germline
text:
Test code: 4156
Test name: BRCA 1 and BRCA 2 Germline
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Description: Symbol; The BRCA germline mutation test is a DNA analysis hHereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome is a type of familial cancer, and is linked to mutations in two genes called BRCA1 and BRCA2 . BRCA1 and BRCA2 are known as tumour suppressor genes - they prevent cells from growing too rapidly or in an uncontrolled way. Thousands of mutations have been found in these genes, but only some have been linked to an increased risk of cancer. Women with a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation are at increased risk of cancer of the fallopian tubes, pancreas, and peritoneum (the membrane that lines the abdomen and the organs in the abdomen). Men with a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation are at increased risk of cancer of the breast, prostate and pancreas. BRCA gene mutation testing is recommended if you have any of the following: -360 1. A personal or family history of breast and/or ovarian cancer. -360 2. If you were younger than 50 years of age when breast cancer was diagnosed. 3. If you have had breast cancer diagnosed more than once (in the same breast or in both breasts). 4. If you are a man and diagnosed with breast cancer at any age. 5. If you have a close relative with a known BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation.
Reported turnaround: 3-4 Weeks
Report date: 4-Weeks
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 44990.0

name: Insulin (Fasting)
text:
Test code: 4160
Test name: Insulin (Fasting)
Also known as: Fasting Insulin (Serum)

Collection instructions: The preferred sample type for insulin is a fasted sample collected after 8 - 12 hours of fasting. Insulin may be collected at other times if carried out as part of a dynamic study or in the investigation of acute hypoglycemia. The reference ranges apply for fasting insulin.
Description: Quantitative determination of Insulin is carried out in the evaluation of disorders of carbohydrate deficiency and hypoglycemia. The fasting insulin test measures the amount of insulin in the bloodstream after a period of not eating, typically for 8-12 hours. Insulin is a hormone produced by the pancreas that helps regulate blood sugar levels by allowing glucose to enter cells. This test is used to evaluate insulin production and sensitivity, helping to assess conditions like insulin resistance, metabolic syndrome, prediabetes, and type 2 diabetes. It may also be used to investigate causes of low blood sugar or monitor insulin-secreting tumors. Elevated or decreased insulin levels can provide valuable insights into metabolic and endocrine function.

name: LKM-1 Liver Kidney Microsomal Antibodies
text:
Test code: 4170
Test name: LKM-1 Liver Kidney Microsomal Antibodies
Also known as: ANTI L.K.M-1Liver kidney Microsomal Abs
Specimen: Serum
Description: The LKM-1 (Liver Kidney Microsomes type 1) test quantitatively detects IgG antibodies against LKM-1 in human serum or plasma, serving as an aid in diagnosing type 2 Autoimmune Hepatitis (AIH). AIH is a chronic autoimmune liver disease, often seen in females, characterized by elevated gamma globulins, specific autoantibodies, and histological liver changes. It is classified into three types based on antibody profiles: type 1 (ANA and SMA), type 2 (LKM-1), and type 3 (anti-SLA/LP). LKM-1 antibodies target cytochrome P4502D6 and are detected in about 90% of type 2 AIH cases, making them a key diagnostic marker. However, they can also appear in 5-10% of chronic hepatitis C patients, though the epitopes differ from those in AIH. Detecting LKM-1 antibodies is crucial for distinguishing type 2 AIH from other liver diseases and autoimmune conditions.
Reported turnaround: Three Hours
Report date: 3-h
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 4390.0

name: Hepatitis B Surface Antibody (Anti-HBs)
text:
Test code: 4203
Test name: Hepatitis B Surface Antibody (Anti-HBs)
Also known as: ANTI HBsAnti Hepatitis B Surface Antibody
Specimen: Serum
Description: The Hepatitis B Surface Antibody (Anti-HBs) test measures the presence and level of antibodies against the hepatitis B surface antigen, reflecting immunity status. A positive Anti-HBs result indicates immunity to hepatitis B virus (HBV), either from past infection or successful vaccination. Levels ?10 mIU/mL are generally considered protective. In patients post-vaccination, Anti-HBs testing can confirm adequate immune response, especially in high-risk individuals (e.g., healthcare workers, immunocompromised patients). A negative result (Anti-HBs <10 mIU/mL) suggests susceptibility to HBV infection, warranting vaccination if not previously done or revaccination in non-responders. Anti-HBs testing should be interpreted alongside other hepatitis B markers (e.g., HBsAg, Anti-HBc) for a comprehensive assessment of HBV status.

name: HIV PCR Qualitative RNA Detection
text:
Test code: 4222 Test name: HIV PCR Qualitative RNA Detection Also known as: HIV 1/2 Qualitative;HIV 1/2 PCR Specimen: Serum,EDTA (Whole Blood) Description:

The cobas® HIV-1/HIV-2 Qualitative assay uses real-time reverse transcription PCR to detect and distinguish HIV-1 and HIV-2. It detects viral RNA in serum or EDTA plasma. Dried blood spots (DBS) may also be tested when the laboratory uses the assay version that includes DBS in its intended use. The test aids diagnosis in adults and children, including infants with perinatal HIV exposure. name: BCR-ABL Tyrosine Kinase Domain (TKD) Mutation Analysis by NGS
text:
Test code: 4311
Test name: BCR-ABL Tyrosine Kinase Domain (TKD) Mutation Analysis by NGS
Also known as: BCR-ABL Mutation Testing for TKI Resistance in CML;BCR-ABL1 tyrosine kinase domain mutation testing
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Description: BCR-ABL1 kinase domain (TKD) mutation analysis by next-generation sequencing (NGS) is performed in patients with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) or Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL) who show loss of molecular response, suboptimal response, or disease progression on tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. TKD mutations are a major mechanism of TKI resistance, and NGS enables sensitive detection (typically down to ~1-3% variant allele frequency) of both dominant and low-level mutations, including multiple coexisting ( compound ) mutations. Identifying the specific mutation helps guide selection of the most appropriate TKI, as certain variants confer resistance to specific agents (e.g., T315I is resistant to imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, and bosutinib, but sensitive to ponatinib). The report should be interpreted in conjunction with BCR-ABL1 transcript monitoring, cytogenetic findings, and clinical features. Higher VAF mutations are generally more clinically relevant, but emerging low-level mutations may still predict future resistance. Absence of detectable mutations does not rule out TKI resistance from other mechanisms. When mutations are found, results should prompt multidisciplinary review to optimize therapy per current guidelines, and repeat testing is advised if further loss of response occurs.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 33990.0

text:

Also known as: Cyclosporin; CSA
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect EDTA whole blood at the clinician-specified time, usually immediately before the next dose. Record the dose, date and time of the last dose, and collection time.
Description: Cyclosporine is an immunosuppressant medication that is primarily used to prevent organ rejection following organ transplants (such as kidney, liver, and heart transplants). It works by suppressing the immune system, specifically targeting T-cells, which are part of the body's immune response that can attack transplanted organs. By inhibiting the activity of these immune cells, cyclosporine helps prevent the body from rejecting the new organ.The dosage needs to be carefully monitored, as cyclosporine can have serious side effects, including kidney damage, high blood pressure, and increased risk of infections. Regular blood tests are necessary to ensure the drug is at the correct level in the body. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: HPV DNA PCR on Tissue Sample
text:
Test code: 4612
Test name: HPV DNA PCR on Tissue Sample
Also known as: Human Pappiiloma Virus
Specimen: BLOCKS
Collection instructions: Submit representative tumour tissue or the specified molecular specimen for HPV DNA PCR on Tissue Sample, with diagnosis and estimated tumour content where relevant. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: HPV is a viral infection that causes common skin and mucous membrane warts. Certain high-risk strains are known to progress cancer. It is now well-established that a persistent infection with a high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) genotype is the main cause of cervical cancer. It is possible to have an HPV infection without any cytologic abnormalities. Checking for HR-HPV genotypes is a reliable and accurate primary screening tool for cervical cancer in women between 25 and 65 years without need for Pap smear while those under 25 years are recommended to have Pap smear. Detection of one or more high risk genotypes is associated with an increased risk of development of cervical cancer. The HPV DNA PCR test at Dr. Kalebi Labs (DKL) has been performed using the FDA approved Cobas 5800 assay which automatically detects 14 HR - HPV genotypes (16, 18, 31, 33, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66 and 68) with individual typing of HPV 16 and HPV 18 simultaneously. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 3 Weeks
Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 6990.0

text:
Test code: 4703
Test name: Toxoplasma IgG
Also known as: TOXOPLASMA IgGTOXO IgG
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Serum collected using standard sampling tubes or tubes containing separating gel. Li?heparin, K2?EDTA and K3?EDTA plasma.
Description: "The Toxo IgG Antibody Test detects Immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies specific to Toxoplasma gondii, the parasite responsible for toxoplasmosis. This infection is typically acquired through consumption of undercooked meat containing tissue cysts or food and water contaminated with oocysts from infected cats. In most healthy individuals, infection is mild or asymptomatic and followed by a lifelong latent phase. The presence of Toxo IgG antibodies indicates previous exposure to T. gondii and suggests either a latent or past infection, or occasionally an ongoing one. While harmless in most people, toxoplasmosis poses significant risks to immunocompromised individuals, such as those with HIV/AIDS, cancer, or organ transplants, in whom reactivation can cause severe complications, particularly brain lesions. The test is especially important in the context of pregnancy, as a newly acquired infection can cross the placenta and affect the fetus. While many congenitally infected infants show no symptoms at birth, serious complications including chorioretinitis, intellectual disability, psychomotor delay, and hearing or vision loss can appear later in life. The likelihood of transmission increases with gestational age, but earlier infections pose a higher risk of severe outcomes.Toxo IgG testing is commonly used to assess immune status before or during pregnancy, to guide management in immunosuppressed patients, and in combination with Toxo IgM testing to distinguish between acute, recent, and past infections. A diagnosis of acute toxoplasmosis is typically confirmed by seroconversion or a significant rise in IgG and/or IgM levels in paired samples over time."

Description: "The Toxo IgM Antibody Test detects Immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibodies specific to Toxoplasma gondii, the protozoan parasite responsible for toxoplasmosis. This infection is commonly acquired through ingestion of undercooked meat containing tissue cysts or food and water contaminated with oocysts shed by infected cats.In healthy individuals, toxoplasmosis is usually mild or asymptomatic and results in a lifelong latent infection. However, reactivation can occur in immunocompromised individuals-such as organ transplant recipients or people living with HIV/AIDS-and may lead to serious complications like meningoencephalitis. Description: "The Cytomegalovirus (CMV) IgM Antibody Test is a qualitative test used to detect IgM antibodies against CMV in human serum or plasma. The presence of CMV-specific IgM antibodies typically indicates a recent or current infection, as IgM is the first antibody produced by the immune system in response to CMV exposure.This test is commonly used in pregnant women, organ transplant candidates or recipients, and patients with unexplained mononucleosis-like symptoms, where identifying active or primary CMV infection is clinically important. A positive CMV IgM result may suggest a primary CMV infection, reactivation of latent infection, or, in some cases, false positives due to cross-reactivity with other viruses. name: Herpes IgG (HSV1)
text:
Test code: 4707
Test name: Herpes IgG (HSV1)
Also known as: HERPES 1 IgGHSV1 IgG
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Serum collected using standard sampling tubes or tubes containing separating gel. Li?heparin, K2?EDTA and K3?EDTA plasma.
Description: "The Herpes Simplex Virus Type 1 (HSV-1) IgG Antibody Test detects IgG antibodies specific to HSV-1, a virus most commonly associated with oral herpes. HSV-1 is highly prevalent worldwide, with most people acquiring the infection in childhood through non-sexual contact. It typically causes cold sores or fever blisters around the mouth but can also be responsible for genital infections, especially through oral-genital contact.This test helps determine whether an individual has been previously exposed to HSV-1, even if they have never experienced noticeable symptoms. IgG antibodies usually appear within a few weeks after infection and remain in the body for life, making this test useful for detecting past or silent infections. The HSV-1 IgG test is particularly helpful in cases where clinical symptoms are unclear, when screening individuals who may be at risk of transmitting the virus, and in evaluating exposure in pregnant women to support perinatal care. It can also be used to distinguish HSV-1 from HSV-2 when both types are possible causes of infection.By identifying long-term immunity or prior infection, the HSV-1 IgG Antibody Test supports accurate diagnosis, patient counseling, and appropriate management of herpes-related conditions."
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour
Standard price (KES): 3390.0

name: Herpes IgG(HSV2)
text:
Test code: 4708

Also known as: HERPES 2 IgGHSV2 IgG
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Serum collected using standard sampling tubes or tubes containing separating gel. Li?heparin, K2?EDTA and K3?EDTA plasma.
Description: "The Herpes Simplex Virus Type 2 (HSV-2) IgG Antibody Test is used to detect IgG antibodies specific to HSV-2, the virus most commonly associated with genital herpes. HSV-2 is a lifelong viral infection that often goes unrecognized, as many individuals may have mild or no symptoms. Despite the absence of symptoms, the virus can still be transmitted through subclinical viral shedding, making serologic testing important for diagnosis, screening, and management. This test identifies past exposure to HSV-2 by detecting IgG antibodies, which typically develop within a few weeks of infection and remain in the bloodstream for life. As such, the HSV-2 IgG test is useful for confirming prior infection, even in asymptomatic individuals or those with non-specific symptoms. The test is particularly valuable in evaluating patients with unexplained genital ulcers or recurrent symptoms, screening sexual partners of individuals with confirmed HSV-2, and assessing risk in pregnant women to help reduce the chance of neonatal herpes. It is also helpful in guiding patient counseling and treatment decisions. Because it is type-specific, this test can distinguish HSV-2 from HSV-1, enhancing diagnostic accuracy.Overall, the HSV-2 IgG Antibody Test provides a reliable method for detecting silent or past infections and plays a critical role in comprehensive sexual health care"

"The Alpha-1 Antitrypsin (A1AT) test measures the level of A1AT, a protein produced by the liver that protects the lungs and other tissues from damage caused by enzyme activity during inflammation. It is the body s primary inhibitor of serine proteases, particularly neutrophil elastase, and plays a key role in controlling tissue breakdown and immune regulation. This test is commonly used to screen for or confirm Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency, a hereditary condition that can lead to early-onset emphysema, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and liver disease, including cirrhosis and neonatal hepatitis. Elevated A1AT levels may also be seen in inflammatory conditions, infections, and certain cancers, as it acts as a positive acute-phase reactant. The A1AT test is valuable in diagnosing unexplained liver or lung conditions, assessing disease progression, and supporting treatment decisions. "

name: Von Willebrand Factor Activity
text:
Test code: 5014
Test name: Von Willebrand Factor Activity
Also known as: VWF Activity; Functional VWF assay; VWF:GPIb activity
Specimen: Citrated
Collection instructions: Collect blood into a correctly filled light blue top tube maintaining the 9:1 blood-to-anticoagulant ratio. Mix gently by inversion and centrifuge promptly to obtain platelet-poor plasma. Avoid hemolyzed, clotted, or underfilled specimens. Transport refrigerated at 2-8?C; if testing is delayed beyond 4 hours, separate plasma and freeze at -20?C or lower.
Description: This assay measures the functional activity of von Willebrand factor and evaluates its ability to mediate platelet adhesion through interaction with platelet glycoprotein Ib. It is a key investigation in patients with mucocutaneous bleeding, easy bruising, menorrhagia, epistaxis, or a suspected inherited or acquired von Willebrand disorder. Results should be interpreted together with the von Willebrand factor antigen level and, where indicated, ristocetin cofactor activity and factor VIII levels. A reduced activity-to-antigen ratio may suggest a qualitative von Willebrand factor defect, while proportional reductions in both activity and antigen are more consistent with a quantitative deficiency. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Transmission occurs mainly through respiratory droplets or direct contact, with symptoms such as fever, malaise, headache, abdominal pain, and a characteristic vesicular rash. Complications may include bacterial super-infections, pneumonia, CNS disorders, and long-term sequelae. IgM antibodies appear within 3 days of symptom onset, peak during acute infection, and wane within a few months, while IgG antibodies persist for years. The test is valuable for confirming acute infection or reactivation when interpreted alongside IgG results and clinical findings.
