VZV, also called Human Herpes Virus-3 (HHV-3), is the causative agent of chickenpox and can remain dormant in the body, later reactivating as herpes zoster (shingles), particularly in the elderly or immunocompromised. Transmission occurs mainly through respiratory droplets or direct contact, with symptoms such as fever, malaise, headache, abdominal pain, and a characteristic vesicular rash. Complications may include bacterial super-infections, pneumonia, CNS disorders, and long-term sequelae. IgM antibodies appear within 3 days of symptom onset, peak during acute infection, and wane within a few months, while IgG antibodies persist for years. The test is valuable for confirming acute infection or reactivation when interpreted alongside IgG results and clinical findings. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: C-ANCA, PR3-II (Proteinase 3)
text:
Test code: 5017
Test name: C-ANCA, PR3-II (Proteinase 3)
Also known as: ANCA - C, PR3-II (Proteinase 3)
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Performed on serum or plasma(EDTA or Sodium Citrate)
Description: The c-ANCA (cytoplasmic Antineutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibody) test measures IgG antibodies which target proteinase 3 in the cytoplasm of neytrophils.It is used in diagnosing and monitoring disease progression in patient with autoimmune vasculitides especially Wegener's granulomatosis.This test was perfomed using Euroimmun chemoliminescence(ChLIA) assay on the IDS-iSYS platform. The PR3 II test quantitatively detect IgG antibodies against proteinase 3 (PR3) in human serum or plasma, aiding in the evaluation of ANCA-associated vasculitides (AAVs), particularly Wegener s granulomatosis (WG). Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) are key markers for necrotizing vasculitides affecting small- and medium-sized blood vessels, including WG, microscopic polyangiitis (MPA), pauci-immune necrotizing glomerulonephritis (PING), and Churg-Strauss syndrome (CSS). PR3, a serine protease in granulocytes and monocytes, contributes to antimicrobial activity but can cause tissue damage when uncontrolled. c-ANCA patterns are typically associated with PR3 antibodies, while p-ANCA patterns often involve MPO antibodies. ANCA titres often correlate with disease activity, making quantitative PR3 testing valuable for monitoring patients. While PR3-ANCA is strongly associated with WG, it cannot differentiate between all AAV subtypes. A positive result must be interpreted alongside clinical findings due to possible ANCA positivity in other conditions, such as infections or bacterial endocarditis, and a negative result does not entirely rule out AAV in symptomatic patients.
Reported turnaround: Two Hours
Report date: 2-Hours
Testing days: DAILY-0

name: Lactate Level (Blood)
text:
Test code: 5023
Test name: Lactate Level (Blood)
Also known as: LACTATE LEVEL
Specimen: Flouride
Collection instructions: Specimen Instructions - Lactate (Roche cobas c503) The patient should be at complete rest for at least 15-30 minutes prior to specimen collection and should avoid exercise or repeated use of the arm or hand before and during phlebotomy. Where clinically feasible, a fasting sample is preferred. Blood should be drawn without the use of a tourniquet where possible, or within three minutes of tourniquet application, while avoiding fist clenching and excessive venous stasis. The specimen should be centrifuged and plasma separated as soon as possible, preferably within 15-30 minutes of collection. If immediate processing is not possible, the specimen should be maintained at 2-8 degrees centigrade and transported promptly. Rapid processing and proper handling are essential to minimize falsely elevated lactate results caused by ongoing cellular metabolism.
Description: Lactate is produced during anaerobic metabolism and is an important marker of tissue hypoxia and impaired oxidative metabolism. Measurement of blood lactate is primarily used in the evaluation and monitoring of sepsis, shock, hypoxia, and metabolic acidosis, and may also assist in the investigation of mitochondrial disorders and inborn errors of metabolism. Serial lactate measurements are useful for assessing disease severity and response to treatment in critically ill patients. Testing is performed on the Roche cobas c503 analyzer using an enzymatic method. Accurate results require proper patient preparation and prompt specimen processing, as prolonged venous stasis or delayed plasma separation may lead to falsely elevated lactate levels.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour
Standard price (KES): 2690.0

name: Lupus Anticoagulant
text:
Test code: 5026
Test name: Lupus Anticoagulant
Also known as: LUPUS ANTICOAGULANT abs
Specimen: Citrated
Collection instructions: Collect 2.7 mL of venous blood into a 3.2% sodium citrate (blue top) tube, ensuring the correct 9:1 blood-to-anticoagulant ratio. The tube should be properly filled as underfilling or overfilling may affect results. Immediately after collection, gently invert the tube 3-4 times to mix and avoid clot formation; do not shake vigorously. The sample should be free from hemolysis and clots. Transport the specimen to the laboratory as soon as possible and process promptly after plasma separation. If the patient is on anticoagulant therapy such as heparin, warfarin, or DOACs, this should be clearly indicated as it may affect interpretation.
Description: The Lupus Anticoagulant test is used to detect the presence of antiphospholipid antibodies that interfere with phospholipid-dependent coagulation assays. Despite the name, these antibodies are associated with an increased risk of thrombosis (both venous and arterial) and pregnancy-related complications rather than bleeding. This test is primarily used in the evaluation of suspected Antiphospholipid Syndrome and may also be requested in patients with unexplained prolonged clotting times (e.g., APTT), recurrent miscarriages, or thrombosis at a young age. It is often performed as part of an antiphospholipid antibody panel alongside anticardiolipin and anti-ß2 glycoprotein I antibodies. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 8390.0

Also known as: SHBG
Specimen: Serum,Serum
Collection instructions: DO NOT use EDTA plasma.
Description: The SHBG test measures the level of sex hormone-binding globulin, a protein produced mainly by the liver that binds tightly to sex hormones like testosterone and estradiol. By regulating the amount of free, biologically active hormones in the bloodstream, SHBG plays a key role in hormone balance. This test is often used to investigate symptoms of hormone excess or deficiency, especially in conditions such as polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), hirsutism, infertility, or suspected androgen disorders. SHBG levels can be affected by factors such as age, sex, liver function, thyroid status, and medications like oral contraceptives.

name: Nickel (Urine)
text:
Test code: 5034
Test name: Nickel (Urine)
Also known as: Nickel
Specimen: Spot Urine
Collection instructions: Collect urine for Nickel (Urine) in a clean, leak-proof laboratory container. Avoid contamination with faeces or toilet water. Follow any midstream, first-morning, or timed instruction on the request. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: The urine nickel test assesses recent exposure to nickel by measuring its concentration in urine, typically reflecting exposure over the past few days. It is primarily used in evaluating occupational or environmental exposure, particularly in individuals working in industries like electroplating, welding, battery production, or mining. Results from spot urine samples should ideally be corrected for creatinine to account for urine concentration variability, while 24-hour urine collections may offer greater accuracy in certain situations. Interpretation requires correlation with exposure history and clinical findings, as mild elevations can also occur due to dietary sources or nickel-containing medical devices. Clinically, elevated urine nickel levels should be assessed alongside potential symptoms such as dermatitis, respiratory irritation, or systemic toxicity in significant exposures. Persistently high levels warrant investigation for ongoing exposure and may require referral to occupational health or toxicology specialists. Reference intervals differ across laboratories, and results should be interpreted within the appropriate regulatory and clinical context. No special patient preparation is needed prior to testing. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Nickel (Serum)
text:
Test code: 5035
Test name: Nickel (Serum)
Also known as: Nickel
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Nickel (Serum) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The serum nickel test measures the concentration of nickel circulating in the bloodstream, providing an indication of recent or ongoing systemic exposure. It is typically requested when significant acute exposure is suspected, such as in industrial accidents, ingestion of nickel-containing substances, or complications from nickel-containing implants or prosthetic devices. Unlike urine testing, serum nickel reflects circulating levels at the time of sampling but does not directly correlate with total body burden. Reference values vary, and interpretation should consider local reference ranges, exposure history, and clinical presentation. Elevated serum nickel may be associated with systemic symptoms like allergic reactions, respiratory issues, gastrointestinal irritation, or in rare cases, systemic toxicity. Persistently elevated serum levels suggest ongoing exposure or accumulation, particularly from internal sources like implants. The test is not routinely used for occupational monitoring but may aid in acute exposure assessment or medical device surveillance. No specific patient preparation is required before sample collection. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Lactate Level (CSF)
text:
Test code: 5045
Test name: Lactate Level (CSF)
Also known as: CSF FOR LACTATE LEVEL
Specimen: CSF
Description: The CSF (cerebrospinal fluid) lactate test measures the concentration of lactate in the cerebrospinal fluid, which surrounds the brain and spinal cord. It is primarily used to help differentiate between bacterial and viral meningitis, as lactate levels tend to be significantly higher in bacterial infections. Elevated CSF lactate may also indicate other conditions such as brain hypoxia, mitochondrial disorders, or central nervous system trauma. It provides valuable information about metabolic activity and oxygen utilization in the brain.

text:
Test code: 5050
Test name: Vitamin D 25-OH
Also known as: 25-OH VITAMIN D;Vitamin D;25-Hydroxy Cholecalciferol
Specimen: Serum
Description: The Vitamin D 25-hydroxy (25-OH) test measures the level of 25-hydroxyvitamin D, the major circulating form of vitamin D in the body. It is the most accurate indicator of vitamin D status and is used to assess whether a person has too little or too much vitamin D. This test helps in diagnosing vitamin D deficiency or insufficiency, which can lead to bone disorders such as rickets or osteomalacia, and may also play a role in immune function and chronic disease risk. It is commonly ordered when there are symptoms of bone weakness, or to monitor supplementation and overall health

name: EBV DNA PCR (Quantitative Viral Load) by RT-PCR
text:
Test code: 5055
Test name: EBV DNA PCR (Quantitative Viral Load) by RT-PCR
Also known as: PCR for EBV DNA; (Quantitative Viral Load) by RT
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood or named specimen for EBV DNA PCR (Quantitative Viral Load) by RT-PCR. Send with the clinical indication and any prior molecular results. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) DNA Quantitative PCR test is a molecular diagnostic assay used to detect and quantify EBV DNA in clinical specimens such as whole blood, plasma, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), or tissue. Using real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR), this test provides an accurate measurement of EBV viral load. It is highly sensitive and specific, allowing for early detection of viral replication even before clinical symptoms appear. This test is primarily used to monitor EBV infection in immunocompromised patients, particularly transplant recipients at risk for post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD), and in the evaluation of EBV-associated malignancies or chronic active EBV infection. Quantitative PCR enables serial monitoring of viral load over time, aiding in diagnosis, prognosis, and response to therapy. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings and other laboratory tests. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 17690.0

name: Thyroid Peroxidase Antibodies (Anti TPO)
text:
Test code: 5057
Test name: Thyroid Peroxidase Antibodies (Anti TPO)
Also known as: Anti-Thyroid Peroxidase TPO TPOAnti-TPOAnti TPO
Specimen: Serum
Description: Thyroid peroxidase (TPO) is the key enzyme in synthesis of thyroid hormones.This test is used for detection and follow up of individuals with TPO autoimmune thyroid disease-graves disease and Hashimoto thyroiditis. This test is not recommended for initial thyroid screening disorders. The Anti-TPO test detects antibodies against thyroid peroxidase (TPO), an essential enzyme in the production of thyroid hormones. The presence of these antibodies indicates an autoimmune reaction against the thyroid and is commonly associated with autoimmune thyroid diseases such as Hashimoto s thyroiditis and Graves disease. Elevated anti-TPO levels are found in up to 90% of Hashimoto s cases and around 70% of Graves cases. The test provides high clinical specificity and consistency, particularly when using purified or recombinant TPO antigens

name: Porphobilinogen (PBG) Qualitative Screen, Spot Urine
text:
Test code: 5069
Test name: Porphobilinogen (PBG) Qualitative Screen, Spot Urine
Also known as: Urine for porphobilinogen, spot/random urine
Specimen: Spot Urine
Collection instructions: Spot urine to be collected in dark coloured bottle with 3-5ml of 6M HCL added as preservative. Urine must be protected from light; At least 30ml of the urine to be submitted to the lab in a dark coloured bottle or wrapped urine container protected from light.
Description: Porphobilinogen (PBG) urine test measures the amount of PBG, a porphyrin precursor, in a urine sample to help diagnose or monitor conditions like acute porphyrias, particularly acute intermittent porphyria (AIP). PBG is a porphyrin precursor, a substance involved in the synthesis of heme, a component of hemoglobin in red blood cells. Porphyrins are normally found in small amounts in the body and are excreted through urine or stool. Elevated levels of PBG in urine can be a sign of a porphyria, a group of inherited or acquired disorders that affect the body's ability to produce heme. A positive qualitative test result should be confirmed by quantitative PBG test in 24-hour urine. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: CALR Mutation (Calreticulin Exon 9) by PCR
text:
Test code: 5070
Test name: CALR Mutation (Calreticulin Exon 9) by PCR
Also known as: CALR exon 9 mutation; Calreticulin mutation; CALR mutation PCR; CARL Mutation By PCR
Specimen: Whole Blood,Bone Marrow Aspirate
Collection instructions: Collect 3?5 mL peripheral blood in an EDTA tube; a minimum of 1 mL may be acceptable. Alternatively, submit 1?2 mL bone marrow aspirate in EDTA. Clearly identify the specimen type and provide relevant clinical information. Do not centrifuge. Avoid heparinised, clotted, leaking or improperly labelled specimens. Transport promptly according to the referral laboratory's current requirements; do not freeze.
Description: This test detects somatic insertion and deletion mutations involving exon 9 of the CALR gene using a PCR-based method. CALR mutations are recurrent driver mutations in BCR::ABL1-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms and are most commonly associated with essential thrombocythaemia and primary myelofibrosis. The test is particularly useful in patients with suspected myeloproliferative neoplasms in whom the JAK2 V617F mutation is not detected. Results should be interpreted together with the clinical findings, full blood count, peripheral blood film, bone marrow morphology and other relevant molecular results, including JAK2, MPL and BCR:ABL1 where indicated. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

Description: Cholinesterase (CHE), primarily produced in the liver and found in serum/plasma, heart, pancreas, and brain, is measured to assess liver synthetic function, detect organophosphate (insecticide) poisoning, and identify individuals with atypical enzyme variants at risk of prolonged paralysis after certain muscle relaxants (like succinylcholine). Decreased CHE may reflect liver failure, enzyme genetic variants (A, F, S, K), or exposure to inhibitors, while phenotyping (e.g., dibucaine test) helps characterize variant risk. name: Zinc Transporter 8 Antibodies (ZNT8)
text:
Test code: 5074
Test name: Zinc Transporter 8 Antibodies (ZNT8)
Also known as: ZnT8; Zinc Transporter 8 Autoantibodies
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Zinc Transporter 8 Antibodies (ZNT8) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The Zinc Transporter 8 (ZNT8) antibody test is used to support the diagnosis of autoimmune Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM). ZNT8 is a \'df-cell-specific protein, and the presence of autoantibodies against it indicates immune-mediated destruction of pancreatic \'df-cells. The test is especially useful in distinguishing T1DM from Type 2 or monogenic diabetes in cases with atypical features or adult-onset diabetes. It is typically used in conjunction with other autoimmune markers such as GAD65, IA-2, and insulin autoantibodies to increase diagnostic sensitivity. A positive ZNT8 result supports a diagnosis of autoimmune T1DM and may also help assess the risk of disease development in first-degree relatives of T1DM patients. However, a negative result does not exclude the diagnosis, especially in long-standing cases where antibody levels may have declined. The test is performed on serum samples, and results should always be interpreted in the clinical context. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 8990.0

name: Autoimmune Liver Hepatitis Profile x5 Markers
text:
Test code: 4850
Test name: Autoimmune Liver Hepatitis Profile x5 Markers
Also known as: Autommune Liver profile 2
Specimen: Serum
Description: The Liver Profile 2 (EUROLINE immunoblot) is a targeted autoantibody panel designed to aid in the diagnosis of autoimmune liver diseases, particularly Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC) and Autoimmune Hepatitis (AIH). It detects five key antibodies: AMA-M2 and M2-3E, which are highly specific for PBC and present in the vast majority of cases; LKM-1 and LC-1, which are associated with AIH type 2, most commonly seen in children and young adults; and SLA/LP, a highly specific marker for AIH type 1 that is often linked to a more aggressive disease course or tendency to relapse. A positive AMA strongly supports a diagnosis of PBC in the right clinical setting, while the presence of LKM-1, LC-1, or SLA/LP supports the diagnosis of AIH and helps in distinguishing between its subtypes. Negative results, however, do not completely rule out autoimmune liver disease, as some patients may have seronegative AIH. The test is best interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings, liver function tests, immunoglobulin levels, imaging, and histology. In cases of diagnostic uncertainty when the 5 Ag test is negative and overlap syndromes are suspected, a broader panel including other additional markers such as Sp100, gp210, and Ro-52 may be considered for more comprehensive coverage. ASMA is a key diagnostic marker for Type 1 AIH, present in most cases, but its specificity is limited since it can occur in other conditions. It is ordered separately as a standalone marker tather than being part of the panel.
Tests included: Antimitochondrial antIbody (AMA-M2), LC-1 antibody, LKM-1 antibody, M2-3 antibody, SLA/LP antibodies
Reported turnaround: Next Day
Report date: 1-Day
Testing days: 9Am & 1Pm
Standard price (KES): 15390.0

name: Von Willebrand Factor Ristocetin Cofactor Assay
text:
Test code: 7005
Test name: Von Willebrand Factor Ristocetin Cofactor Assay
Also known as: VWF:RCo; Ristocetin Cofactor Assay; Ristocetin-induced Platelet Agglutination Cofactor Activity
Specimen: Citrated
Collection instructions: Fill the light blue-top citrate tube to the correct fill line (must be exactly 9 parts blood to 1 part anticoagulant) Gently invert the tube 3-5 times.Do not shake. Keep the sample at room temperature if the sample is to be analysed within 4 hours. If analysis will occur after 4 hours, plasma should be separated by centrifugation (within 1 hour) and shipped frozen in dry ice at -20 degrees.
Description: This assay assesses the ability of von Willebrand factor to bind platelet glycoprotein Ib in the presence of ristocetin and is used to evaluate the platelet-binding function of VWF. It is particularly useful in the investigation and subtyping of von Willebrand disease, especially when a qualitative defect is suspected. The ristocetin cofactor activity should be interpreted alongside VWF antigen and other coagulation studies. A disproportionately low ristocetin cofactor activity relative to the antigen level may indicate a qualitative VWF abnormality such as type 2 von Willebrand disease, whereas parallel reductions in both measurements suggest a quantitative deficiency. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 11990.0

Collection instructions: General instructions : Preferred start collection time is morning. Collect urine in a 24 hour metal free urine container. Urine is acidified to pH 1 with concentrated HCl to prevent precipitation of magnesium ammonium phosphate. Empty the bladder first thing in the morning or at the start time and discard this urine. Note the time, as this is the start time of the 24 hours. (For example 6:00 am) Collect every drop of urine voided over the next 24 hours (e.g. 6:am on a Tuesday to 6:00 am Wednesday). Should one need to defecate and urinate at the same time, this urine should also be collected. Try as much as possible not to contaminate the urine with faeces. Keep the urine cold either on ice or refigerated. Stop time should be within 20 minutes of the start time the day before. E.g. if start time was 6:00 am Tuesday, stop time is between 5:50 am and 6:10 am during which time any urine passed must be collected. FOR SUBMITTING LABORATORIES /HOSPITALS If submitting an aliquot of the 24 hour urine, note the volume of 24 hour urine submited. Mix the sample well to a homogenous mixture and aliquote into a clean container. Submit the aliquot with clear documentation of the duration of collection and the volume of the 24 hour urine.
Description: 24 hour urine is used to distinguish between renal and GIT losses of Magnesium in hypomagnesemia.

name: TB PCR (MTB) with RIF/INH Sensitivity - Sputum
text:
Test code: 1152
Test name: TB PCR (MTB) with RIF/INH Sensitivity - Sputum
Also known as: Mycobacterium Tuberculosis PCR with Rifampicin and Isoniazid Sensitivity;Similar PCR to GeneXpert with additional sensitivity for INH in addition to RIF
Specimen: SPUTUM
Description: The TB PCR with INH and RIF Sensitivity (Molecular Drug Resistance Testing) assay detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) DNA in sputum and simultaneously screens for common mutations associated with resistance to Rifampicin (RIF) and Isoniazid (INH)-the two most important first-line anti-TB drugs. It provides rapid results that can guide early treatment decisions, particularly in settings where multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) is a concern. However, molecular assays detect only the most frequent resistance-conferring mutations, so phenotypic culture-based drug susceptibility testing remains essential to confirm results and identify resistance to other drugs. A negative PCR does not exclude TB, and results must be interpreted alongside histology, culture, and clinical findings.
Tests included: INH, MTB, RIF1, RIF2, RIF3
Reported turnaround: After Three Days
Report date: 3-Days
Testing days: 11Am & 5Pm
Standard price (KES): 7990.0

Description: Amyloid A immunohistochemistry is an immunohistochemical (IHC) test used on tissue biopsy sections to detect Serum Amyloid A (SAA) protein within amyloid deposits. name: Porphobilinogen (PBG) Quantitative, 24-Hr Urine
text:
Test code: 5087
Test name: Porphobilinogen (PBG) Quantitative, 24-Hr Urine
Also known as: Urine for porphobilinogen, 24-hr
Specimen: 24 Hrs Urine
Collection instructions: 24-hour urine to be collected in dark coloured bottle with 10ml of 6M HCL as preservative. Urine must be protected from light; At least 30 ml of urine from the 24-hr urine container to be submitted to the lab in a dark coloured bottle or wrapped urine container protected from light.
Description: Porphobilinogen (PBG) urine test measures the amount of PBG, a porphyrin precursor, in a urine sample to help diagnose or monitor conditions like acute porphyrias, particularly acute intermittent porphyria (AIP). PBG is a porphyrin precursor, a substance involved in the synthesis of heme, a component of hemoglobin in red blood cells. Porphyrins are normally found in small amounts in the body and are excreted through urine or stool. Elevated levels of PBG in urine can be a sign of a porphyria, a group of inherited or acquired disorders that affect the body's ability to produce heme. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: MRD B-Lymphoblastic Leukemia (B-ALL) by Multiparametric Flow Cytometry
text:
Test code: 1159
Test name: MRD B-Lymphoblastic Leukemia (B-ALL) by Multiparametric Flow Cytometry
Also known as: B-ALL MRD by Flow Cytometry;Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) B-ALL; Measurable Residual Disease (MRD) B-ALL;Residual B-ALL Detection by Flow Cytometry;Post-treatment B-ALL Flow Cytometry; Leukemia MRD Panel B-ALL;
Specimen: Bone Marrow Aspirate
Description: T-Lymphoblastic Leukemia / Lymphoma Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) by Multiparametric Flow Cytometry is a high-sensitivity assay used for detection and quantification of residual leukemic T-lymphoblasts following therapy in patients with T-acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (T-ALL/LBL). The assay utilizes advanced multicolor flow cytometry to identify aberrant leukemia-associated immunophenotypes (LAIP) and/or abnormal immature T-cell populations that differ from normal thymic or regenerating T-cell precursors using both leukemia-associated and different-from-normal analytical approaches. This test is primarily performed for post-induction, consolidation, maintenance, relapse assessment, and treatment response monitoring in T-ALL. MRD status is a major independent prognostic marker and is widely used for risk stratification, evaluation of therapeutic response, transplant decision-making, and relapse prediction. Analytical sensitivity typically ranges from 10^4m to 10^5 depending on specimen quality, cellularity, and assay design. Fresh bone marrow aspirate is the preferred specimen. Concurrent review of prior diagnostic immunophenotyping and treatment history is strongly recommended for accurate interpretation.
Reported turnaround: Same Day
Report date: 8-Hours
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 19990.0

text:
Test code: 6082

Specimen: Serum

Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: This highly sensitive test is used to detect and characterize donor-specific anti-HLA antibodies (DSAs) against both Class I (HLA-A, -B, -C) and Class II (HLA-DR, -DQ, -DP) molecules. Using a Luminex-based single antigen bead technology, the assay provides precise antibody identification and semi-quantitative measurement (mean fluorescence intensity), enabling detailed risk stratification in transplantation. It is significantly more sensitive than conventional crossmatch methods, detecting even low-level antibodies that may impact graft survival. Clinically, this test is essential for pre-transplant risk assessment, monitoring sensitized patients, evaluating antibody-mediated rejection, and guiding immunosuppressive therapy. The extended subclass analysis provides additional insight into the antibody profile, helping transplant teams make informed decisions about donor compatibility, rejection risk, and post-transplant management. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: JC virus (JCV) PCR Test {CSF}
text:
Test code: 6086
Test name: JC virus (JCV) PCR Test {CSF}
Also known as: JCV; PCR for JC virus (JCV); Test {CSF}
Collection instructions: Collect cerebrospinal fluid aseptically into the laboratory-approved sterile tubes and label the tube sequence if more than one tube is taken. Submit immediately with collection time and the clinical indication. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: The JC virus (JCV) PCR test on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is used in the evaluation of patients with suspected progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), a demyelinating CNS infection seen in immunocompromised individuals such as those with advanced HIV, post-transplant immunosuppression, or on monoclonal antibody therapies like natalizumab or rituximab. The assay detects JCV DNA by real-time PCR, offering high specificity and good sensitivity, though detection depends on viral load and disease stage. A positive result in the appropriate clinical and radiological setting strongly supports a diagnosis of PML, while a negative result does not fully exclude the disease, particularly early on or in patients with low viral burden. If suspicion remains high, repeat CSF testing or brain biopsy may be indicated. Interpretation should always be made in correlation with neurological findings and MRI features of multifocal non-enhancing white matter lesions. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Mitochondrial DNA Genome Sequencing (mtDNA)
text:
Test code: 6117
Test name: Mitochondrial DNA Genome Sequencing (mtDNA)
Also known as: Whole Mitochondrial Genome sequencing (mtDNA sequencing)
Collection instructions: Sample Types: Peripheral Blood in EDTA, Amniotic Fluid, Chorionic Villi
Description: Mitochondrial DNA sequencing is a molecular diagnostic test that evaluates the entire mitochondrial genome or targeted regions to detect pathogenic variants associated with mitochondrial disorders. It is indicated in patients with unexplained multi-systemic presentations such as progressive myopathy, encephalopathy, lactic acidosis, stroke-like episodes, optic neuropathy, hearing loss, cardiomyopathy, or maternal inheritance patterns of disease. The test can identify point mutations, small insertions/deletions, and heteroplasmy (the proportion of mutant vs wild-type mtDNA), which is a critical factor influencing disease severity and penetrance. Results should be interpreted in the context of clinical presentation, biochemical findings (e.g., elevated lactate), and additional nuclear gene testing, since many mitochondrial disorders arise from nuclear-encoded genes that affect mitochondrial function. A positive result confirming a pathogenic mtDNA variant provides a definitive diagnosis, guides management, and enables genetic counseling regarding maternal transmission risk. Negative or inconclusive results do not exclude a mitochondrial disorder, and further nuclear DNA sequencing or functional studies may be warranted. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 5 Weeks
Report date: 5-w
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Homologous Recombination Deficiency (HRD) Assay
text:
Test code: 6145 Test name: Homologous Recombination Deficiency (HRD) Assay Also known as: HRD Molecular Profiling Specimen: BLOCKS Description:

HRD testing assesses defects in the homologous recombination DNA repair pathway in tumour cells, which may predict sensitivity to platinum-based chemotherapy and PARP inhibitors. Comprehensive HRD testing evaluates genomic instability markers, including loss of heterozygosity (LOH), telomeric allelic imbalance (TAI), and large-scale state transitions (LST), often alongside BRCA1/2 mutation analysis.

Unlike Homologous Recombination Repair (HRR) gene panel testing, which identifies mutations in DNA repair genes, comprehensive HRD testing assesses the genomic consequences of defective DNA repair and may identify HRD-positive tumours even without detectable BRCA1/2 mutations. An HRR gene panel alone does not establish HRD status.

name: SRY GENE BY FISH
text:
Test code: 7010
Test name: SRY GENE BY FISH
Specimen: Sodium Heparin
Collection instructions: Collect the specimen specified for cytogenetic analysis in the approved anticoagulant. Do not refrigerate or freeze unless the receiving laboratory instructs otherwise. Provide the clinical indication and submit promptly. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: FISH for Y-chromosome sequences (SRY GENE BY FISH) is a molecular cytogenetic test that detects the presence of Y-chromosome DNA in cells using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). In this technique, fluorescently labeled DNA probes designed to bind to specific Y-chromosome regions-commonly including the SRY gene or Y-centromeric sequences-are applied to patient cells (such as peripheral blood, amniotic fluid, or tissue samples). If Y-chromosome material is present, the probes hybridize to the target DNA and produce visible fluorescent signals under a fluorescence microscope. Clinically, this test is used to determine whether Y-chromosome material is present or absent, particularly in the evaluation of disorders of sex development (DSD), suspected Y-chromosome mosaicism, Turner syndrome with possible hidden Y material, and prenatal sex determination. Detection of Y-chromosome sequences can have important diagnostic and management implications, for example identifying patients at risk of gonadoblastoma when Y-chromosome material is present in individuals with gonadal dysgenesis or Turner syndrome. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Orotic Acid, Urine
text:
Test code: 1429
Test name: Orotic Acid, Urine
Also known as: Oritic Acid in Urine
Specimen: Urine
Collection instructions: Collect 15-20 mL of a random urine sample in a sterile, preservative-free container; first morning or timed collections may be used if clinically indicated. Keep refrigerated if transport is delayed, and samples should be transported refrigerated (preferred). Avoid contaminated specimens. Indicate relevant clinical details, such as hyperammonemia or suspected urea cycle disorder, to assist interpretation.
Description: The urinary orotic acid test measures levels of orotic acid, a byproduct of pyrimidine metabolism, to aid in the evaluation of urea cycle disorders-particularly ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency-as well as certain metabolic conditions like hereditary orotic aciduria. Elevated orotic acid in the presence of hyperammonemia suggests OTC deficiency, while persistent elevation without hyperammonemia may indicate defects in pyrimidine synthesis. The test is typically performed via quantitative mass spectrometry on a random or timed urine sample. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: ADAMTS13 Activity Test
text:
Test code: 8064
Test name: ADAMTS13 Activity Test
Specimen: Citrated
Collection instructions: d- 3ml of whole blood in blue top (sodium citrate) tube. - Fill tube completely to ensure correct blood-to-anticoagulant ratio. - Gently invert tube 5-10 times to mix. If submitting to the lab will take more than 1 hour, process as follows: - Centrifuge at 1500 x g for 15 minutes at room temperature. - Transfer supernatant plasma into a plastic, screw-cap vial. - Freeze immediately at -20?C or colder - Ship frozen plasma to the lab
Description: The ADAMTS13 activity assay measures the activity of the ADAMTS13 enzyme, which is responsible for cleaving von Willebrand factor (vWF). This test is essential for diagnosing thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), a rare but potentially life-threatening condition. ADAMTS13 activty at <10% indicates severe deficiency which is highly suggestive of TTP, which requires ADAMTS13 inhibitor assay to assess for autoantibodies for confirmation. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

Also known as: POC - MICROARRAY; Products of Conception Microarray, peripheral blood micro-array High resolution Micro-array CMA POC Chromosomal Microarray
Collection instructions: For chromosomal microarray (CMA) testing on products of conception (POC), submit fresh fetal tissue-preferably chorionic villi or fetal parts-in sterile saline or transport media, avoiding maternal decidua and blood clots. Ensure the sample is properly labeled and accompanied by a completed requisition form and relevant clinical history, including gestational age and any notable findings. Keep the specimen refrigerated (not frozen) and deliver to the lab within 24-48 hours. If fresh tissue is unavailable, FFPE blocks may be submitted, though DNA quality may be limited. Maternal cell contamination testing may be performed to confirm fetal origin.
Description: Chromosomal microarray (CMA) testing for products of conception (POC) is a high-resolution genetic test used to detect chromosomal abnormalities, including aneuploidies and submicroscopic copy number variants, that may have contributed to pregnancy loss. It offers greater diagnostic yield compared to conventional karyotyping and does not require viable cells, making it suitable for both fresh and formalin-fixed tissue. CMA helps provide insight into the genetic causes of miscarriage, guides counseling for recurrence risk, and informs future pregnancy management. The 750K chromosomal microarray offers higher resolution and broader genomic coverage compared to the 315K array, allowing for more sensitive detection of smaller copy number variants (CNVs) and subtle chromosomal abnormalities. While both platforms are effective for identifying aneuploidies and large CNVs, the 750K array provides greater diagnostic yield, especially in complex cases such as recurrent pregnancy loss or when detailed genomic analysis is needed. Previous research indicates that more than 60% of first trimester miscarriages occurred due to chromosomal anomalies including aneuploidies, triploidy, uniparental disomy (UPD), etc. Traditional cytogenetic analysis of these samples is challenging due to high degrees of maternal cell contamination and culture failure, results in long turn-around time. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 32990.0

name: Cysticercosis IgG (Taenia Solium IgG) Serum
text:
Test code: 8066
Test name: Cysticercosis IgG (Taenia Solium IgG) Serum
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Serum 3-5mL
Description: The Cysticercosis IgG antibody test is a serologic assay used to support the diagnosis of cysticercosis, especially neurocysticercosis, caused by Taenia solium larvae. It detects IgG antibodies in serum or CSF. A positive result suggests prior or active infection but must be interpreted alongside clinical findings and neuroimaging, as it cannot distinguish between active and past infection. False positives may occur due to cross-reactivity with other parasitic infections, while false negatives are possible in cases of localized lesions, early infection, or immunosuppression. The test is most useful in patients from endemic regions who present with unexplained seizures or intracranial cystic/ring-enhancing lesions. However, it is not suitable as a screening tool in asymptomatic individuals due to high background seroprevalence. Negative results do not rule out disease, especially in cases with single or calcified lesions. A positive test should prompt further diagnostic evaluation including brain imaging and possible CSF analysis, with management guided by a multidisciplinary team. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 4390.0

name: Mpox
text:
Test code: 9016
Test name: Mpox
Also known as: Monkey POX
Specimen: Swab
Collection instructions: The preferred specimen is skin lesion material. Gently clean the lesion with sterile saline, then vigorously swab vesicular, pustular, or ulcerative lesions using a synthetic fibre swab (Dacron/polyester/nylon) with a rigid plastic shaft. Where possible, collect from 2-3 lesions at different sites or stages. Vigorous swabbing may naturally unroof the lesion; do not intentionally unroof or incise lesions, and do not use scalpels, needles, or other sharp instruments. Do not use cotton or wooden-shafted swabs. An oropharyngeal (throat) swab may be collected as a supplementary specimen when skin lesions are absent or limited. Place the swab in a sterile, leak-proof, screw-cap tube (dry or in VTM/UTM as per laboratory protocol). Clearly label each specimen with at least two patient identifiers and ensure the details match the request form. Securely seal and transport using triple packaging (UN3373 - Biological Substance, Category B) at 2-8?C. For prolonged storage, store at -70?C and avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles. IMPORTANT: Do not open the specimen container during accessioning or routine sample reception. Keep the specimen sealed and forward it directly to the designated testing area for processing under appropriate biosafety precautions.
Description: This assay detects Monkeypox virus (MPXV) DNA by real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) from clinical specimens and is the preferred laboratory method for confirming suspected mpox infection. Skin lesion material (vesicle, pustule or crust/lesion swabs) is the specimen of choice and provides the highest diagnostic sensitivity. Oropharyngeal swabs may be submitted as supplementary specimens where clinically indicated but have lower sensitivity than lesion specimens. A positive result confirms the presence of MPXV DNA in the submitted specimen and should be interpreted in conjunction with the patients clinical presentation and epidemiological risk factors. A negative result does not completely exclude mpox, particularly if specimen collection is suboptimal, sampling is performed very early or late in the course of illness, or viral DNA is below the assays limit of detection. Appropriate infection prevention and public health measures should be followed in accordance with national guidelines. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Days
Report date: 47-Hours
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 3690.0

name: MRD Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) by Multiparametric Flow Cytometry
text:
Test code: 2820
Test name: MRD Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) by Multiparametric Flow Cytometry
Also known as: AML MRD by Flow Cytometry;Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) AML; Measurable Residual Disease (MRD) AML; Residual AML Detection by Flow Cytometry; Post-treatment AML Flow Cytometry; Leukemia MRD Panel AML;
Specimen: Bone Marrow Aspirate
Description: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) by Multiparametric Flow Cytometry is a high-sensitivity assay used for detection and quantification of residual leukemic myeloid blasts following therapy in patients with AML. The assay utilizes advanced multicolor flow cytometry to identify aberrant leukemia-associated immunophenotypes (LAIP) and/or abnormal immature myeloid blast populations that differ from normal regenerating myeloid precursors using both leukemia-associated and different-from-normal analytical approaches. This test is primarily performed for post-induction, consolidation, maintenance, relapse assessment, and treatment response monitoring in AML. MRD status is a major independent prognostic marker and is widely used for risk stratification, evaluation of therapeutic response, transplant decision-making, and relapse prediction. Analytical sensitivity typically ranges from 10^4 to 10^5 depending on specimen quality, cellularity, and assay design. Fresh bone marrow aspirate is the preferred specimen. Concurrent review of prior diagnostic immunophenotyping, cytogenetic/molecular findings, and treatment history is strongly recommended for accurate interpretation.
Reported turnaround: Same Day
Report date: 8-Hours
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 22990.0

name: Very Long Chain Fatty Acids (VLCFA)
text:
Test code: 2005
Test name: Very Long Chain Fatty Acids (VLCFA)
Also known as: Very long-chain fatty acids; VLCFA; X-ALD screen; VLCFA Fatty Acids With Very Long Chains
Specimen: Plasma
Collection instructions: Collect 3?5 mL venous blood in an EDTA (purple-top) or lithium-heparin (green-top) tube. Mix gently to avoid clotting. Centrifuge promptly, separate plasma into a clean labelled cryovial, and freeze the plasma. Keep frozen during storage and transport. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: The VLCFA test measures fatty acids with chain lengths of 22 carbons or more in plasma. Abnormal accumulation is a biochemical marker of peroxisomal disorders, most notably X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD) and related conditions. Elevated VLCFA levels indicate impaired peroxisomal ß-oxidation. The assay supports confirmation of a suspected diagnosis in patients with adrenal insufficiency, progressive neurological symptoms, or unexplained leukodystrophy, and may be used for at-risk male relatives of patients with X-ALD and for carrier detection in females. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 4 Weeks
Report date: 4-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Measles IgM Antibodies
text:
Test code: 5003
Test name: Measles IgM Antibodies
Also known as: MEASELES IgM Abs
Specimen: Serum
Description: The Measles IgM test quantitatively detect IgM antibodies against the measles virus in serum or plasma, aiding in the diagnosis of recent or ongoing infection. Measles is a highly contagious viral disease caused by the Morbillivirus of the Paramyxoviridae family, transmitted via respiratory droplets or direct contact with secretions. It presents with fever, cough, conjunctivitis, Koplik s spots, and a generalized rash, with complications such as pneumonia, diarrhea, and rarely subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE). IgM antibodies typically appear at the onset of the rash, persist for 3-6 weeks, and are the preferred marker for diagnosing acute measles, whereas IgG antibodies indicate past infection or vaccination but require paired serum samples for confirmation.

Testing days: DAILY-0

metadata.name: Measles IgM Antibodies
metadata.description: The Measles IgM test quantitatively detect IgM antibodies against the measles virus in serum or plasma, aiding in the diagnosis of recent or ongoing infection. Measles is a highly contagious viral disease caused by the Morbillivirus of the Paramyxoviridae family, transmitted via respiratory droplets or direct contact with secretions. It presents with fever, cough, conjunctivitis, Koplik s spots, and a generalized rash, with complications such as pneumonia, diarrhea, and rarely subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE). IgM antibodies typically appear at the onset of the rash, persist for 3-6 weeks, and are the preferred marker for diagnosing acute measles, whereas IgG antibodies indicate past infection or vaccination but require paired serum samples for confirmation.

name: Varicella Zoster Virus (Chicken Pox) IgG
text:
Test code: 5005
Test name: Varicella Zoster Virus (Chicken Pox) IgG
Also known as: Varicella Zoster Virus (Chicken Pox) IgG Abs
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Varicella Zoster Virus (Chicken Pox) IgG and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The IDS VZV IgG test quantitatively detect IgG antibodies against Varicella-Zoster Virus (VZV) in serum or plasma, aiding in assessing immunity or past infection. VZV, also known as Human Herpes Virus-3 (HHV-3), is the cause of varicella (chickenpox) and can remain latent, later reactivating as herpes zoster (shingles), especially in the elderly or immunocompromised individuals. Transmission occurs via respiratory droplets or direct skin contact, with symptoms including fever, malaise, and characteristic vesicular rashes. Complications can include bacterial infections, pneumonia, and CNS issues. IgG antibodies appear within days of symptom onset, persist for years, and rise sharply during reactivation, making this test useful for evaluating immunity, guiding vaccination decisions, and confirming infections when combined with IgM results. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: Three Hours
Report date: 3-h
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 3390.0

name: Tryptase (Mast Cell ) Allergy Test
text:
Test code: 4648
Test name: Tryptase (Mast Cell ) Allergy Test
Also known as: Mast Cell Tryptase
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect serum for Tryptase (Mast Cell ) Allergy Test. No allergen avoidance is required immediately before sampling unless the clinician advises otherwise. Record the suspected allergen.
Description: The tryptase test is used to support the diagnosis of anaphylaxis and mast cell disorders by measuring serum tryptase, a marker of mast cell activation. Elevated tryptase levels within 1-4 hours of symptom onset suggest anaphylaxis, while persistently elevated levels may indicate systemic mastocytosis. The test should be interpreted in the context of clinical findings, and a follow-up baseline sample 24-48 hours later may help confirm transient versus persistent elevation. Prompt sampling after the onset of symptoms is essential for accurate assessment. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Mumps IgM Antibodies
text:
Test code: 5307
Test name: Mumps IgM Antibodies
Specimen: Serum
Description: The Mumps IgM test detects recent mumps infection by identifying IgM antibodies in serum or plasma. Mumps, caused by the Rubulavirus, spreads via respiratory droplets and often causes parotid gland swelling, though many cases are mild or asymptomatic. IgM antibodies appear 3-4 days after symptoms, peak within a week, and persist for up to 12 weeks, while IgG antibodies develop later and confer lifelong immunity. Diagnosis is confirmed by detecting IgM or a rise in IgG titers, especially in atypical or vaccinated cases.

name: CYP11B1 / CYP11B2 Chimeric Gene by PCR
text:
Test code: 3528
Test name: CYP11B1 / CYP11B2 Chimeric Gene by PCR
Also known as: CYP11B1 / CYP11B2 Molecular Assay for Glucocorticoid-Remediable Aldosteronism;Familial Hyperaldosteronism Type I
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Description: This PCR-based assay detects the presence of a CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimeric gene, the characteristic genetic abnormality in familial hyperaldosteronism type I (FH-I), also known as glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism (GRA). The test is performed on peripheral blood DNA and targets the hybrid gene formed by unequal crossover between the 11\'e2-hydroxylase and aldosterone synthase genes, resulting in ACTH-regulated aldosterone overproduction. It is indicated in patients with early-onset or familial hypertension, suppressed renin with inappropriately normal or elevated aldosterone, and in children or young adults with suspected primary aldosteronism. A positive result confirms FH-I and enables targeted management with low-dose glucocorticoids and/or mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists and facilitates family cascade testing. A negative result excludes FH-I but does not rule out other causes of primary aldosteronism, including sporadic aldosterone-producing adenomas, bilateral adrenal hyperplasia, and other familial subtypes. Where clinical suspicion remains high despite a negative PCR result, next-generation sequencing (NGS) -based clinical exome seuqncing (CES) targeting genes implicated in primary aldosteronism (e.g., KCNJ5, CACNA1D, CACNA1H, ATP1A1, ATP2B3) may be used as an alternative or complementary approach to detect point mutations, small insertions/deletions, or atypical rearrangements that are not detectable by conventional PCR
Reported turnaround: 3-4 Weeks
Report date: 4-Weeks
Testing days: TUE & FRI
Standard price (KES): 40690.0

name: Unconjugated Estriol (uE3)
text:
Test code: 9082
Test name: Unconjugated Estriol (uE3)
Also known as: Free Estriol; Maternal Serum Estriol
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Unconjugated Estriol (uE3) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: Unconjugated Estriol (uE3) is an estrogen produced by the placenta from precursors supplied by the fetal adrenal gland and liver. In maternal serum screening (triple/quadruple test), low uE3 is associated with fetal chromosomal abnormalities, particularly trisomy 18 and, less specifically, trisomy 21. Very low or undetectable levels may also indicate rare fetal steroid metabolism disorders such as SmithLemliOpitz syndrome or steroid sulfatase deficiency, and may reflect placental insufficiency, intrauterine growth restriction, or fetal demise. uE3 rises progressively during pregnancy, and interpretation should always consider gestational age, maternal demographics, and other serum markers. Isolated low uE3 is not diagnostic but signals the need for further evaluation with ultrasound and possibly genetic testing. Abnormal results should be communicated as part of an integrated risk assessment and followed up in a multidisciplinary\\~setting This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 1 week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 4390.0

name: MRD Mature B-Cell Neoplasm / CLL by Multiparametric Flow Cytometry
text:
Test code: 8106
Test name: MRD Mature B-Cell Neoplasm / CLL by Multiparametric Flow Cytometry
Also known as: Mature B-Cell Neoplasm MRD by Flow Cytometry; B-Cell Lymphoma MRD by Flow Cytometry; Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) MRD by Flow Cytometry; Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) Mature B-Cell Neoplasm; Measurable Residual Disease (MRD) B-Cell Lymphoma; Residual B-Cell Neoplasm Detection by Flow Cytometry; Post-treatment B-Cell Neoplasm Flow Cytometry;
Specimen: Bone Marrow Aspirate,PERIPHERAL BLOOD
Description: Mature B-Cell Neoplasm Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) by Multiparametric Flow Cytometry is a high-sensitivity assay used for detection and quantification of residual clonal mature B-cell populations following therapy in patients with mature B-cell lymphoproliferative disorders including chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), mantle cell lymphoma, follicular lymphoma, hairy cell leukemia, lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, and other mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas with peripheral blood and/or bone marrow involvement. The assay utilizes advanced multicolor flow cytometry to identify persistent abnormal B-cell populations based on aberrant antigen expression patterns and light-chain restriction. This test is primarily performed for post-treatment response assessment, remission monitoring, relapse detection, and therapeutic response evaluation in mature B-cell neoplasms. MRD assessment is increasingly used for prognostication, treatment stratification, evaluation of depth of remission, and monitoring response to targeted therapies and stem cell transplantation. Analytical sensitivity typically ranges from 10^4 to 10^5 depending on specimen quality, cellularity, and assay design. Bone marrow aspirate is generally preferred for highest sensitivity, although peripheral blood may be acceptable in selected disorders such as CLL. Concurrent review of prior diagnostic immunophenotyping, molecular/cytogenetic findings, and treatment history is strongly recommended for accurate interpretation.
Reported turnaround: Same Day
Report date: 8-Hours
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 19990.0

name: APOE Genotyping ( Apolipoprotein E e2/e3/e4 )
text:
Test code: 7906 Test name: APOE Genotyping ( Apolipoprotein E e2/e3/e4 ) Also known as: APOE Alzheimer Risk Genotyping; ApoE Genotype; APOE e4 Allele Testing; Apolipoprotein E Genotyping Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood) Collection instructions:

Mix gently by inversion immediately after collection. Send whole blood; do not separate. Provide relevant clinical history and indication for testing. Follow the reference laboratory’s requirements for genetic consent, storage and transport.

Description:

APOE genotyping identifies the common apolipoprotein E alleles e2, e3 and e4, reporting the allele pair and e4 carrier status as non-carrier, heterozygous or homozygous. The e4 allele is associated with increased susceptibility to late-onset Alzheimer’s disease, with greater risk generally associated with two copies than one. APOE genotype also informs assessment of the risk of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA), including cerebral oedema and haemorrhage, in patients being considered for anti-amyloid therapy.

This is a susceptibility test and does not independently diagnose Alzheimer’s disease or predict or exclude its future development. Routine predictive testing in asymptomatic individuals is generally not recommended because of limited predictive value. Results should be interpreted alongside clinical findings, family history and relevant diagnostic investigations, with appropriate genetic counselling.

This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks Report date: 2-Weeks Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU Standard price (KES): 33990.0

name: CPK-MM Fraction Test
text:
Test code: 9151
Test name: CPK-MM Fraction Test
Also known as: Creatine Kinase MM
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for CPK-MM Fraction Test and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The creatine phosphokinase (CPK) enzyme has three isoenzymes: CPK-MM (muscle), CPK-MB (cardiac), and CPK-BB (brain). The CPK-MM fraction test checks for the predominant form found in skeletal muscle and to a lesser extent in cardiac muscle. Elevated CPK-MM levels indicate skeletal muscle injury, breakdown, or disease. Common causes include trauma, strenuous exercise, muscular dystrophies, myositis, rhabdomyolysis, and certain drug/toxin exposures. Clinically, CPK-MM helps differentiate muscle-derived enzyme elevation from cardiac (CPK-MB) or neurologic (CPK-BB) sources. Persistently high levels warrant evaluation for ongoing muscle damage, while correlation with clinical history, physical findings, and additional tests (e.g., renal function, urine myoglobin, EMG, biopsy) is important for accurate diagnosis\\~and\\~management. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: LP-PLA2 (Lipoprotein-associated Phospholipase A2) Activity test
text:
Test code: 9153
Test name: LP-PLA2 (Lipoprotein-associated Phospholipase A2) Activity test
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for LP-PLA2 (Lipoprotein-associated Phospholipase A2) Activity Test and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: LP-PLA2 (Lipoprotein-associated Phospholipase A2) Activity test is an LDL-associated enzyme produced by inflammatory cells within atherosclerotic plaques. Elevated activity reflects vascular-specific inflammation and plaque instability, and has been shown to independently predict coronary heart disease, ischemic stroke, and cardiovascular mortality. It may be useful in refining ASCVD risk stratification, particularly in patients with intermediate risk or when preventive treatment decisions are uncertain. High LP-PLA2 activity suggests increased atherothrombotic risk, while low/normal levels indicate lower vascular inflammatory burden. Results should be interpreted alongside lipids, hs-CRP, and overall ASCVD risk profile. Although not recommended for routine screening, it can provide added value in select clinical contexts. Statins and lifestyle modification can lower LP-PLA2 activity, though no specific inhibitors are in\\~clinical\\~use. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Description: CA 27.29 is a serum tumor marker associated with the MUC1 glycoprotein, primarily used for monitoring breast cancer rather than for diagnosis or screening. It is most useful for assessing treatment response and detecting recurrence in patients with known breast carcinoma, as levels often correlate with disease burden. Serial measurements should be performed using the same assay method to ensure consistency. Elevated CA 27.29 may also be seen in other epithelial malignancies (such as ovarian, lung, pancreatic, or colorectal cancers) and occasionally in benign liver or breast conditions, so results must be interpreted in clinical context. Falling levels generally suggest therapeutic response, while rising levels may indicate progression or relapse, warranting correlation with imaging and clinical findings. text:
Test code: 9171
Test name: CIDP Paranodal Antibodies / Autoimmune Nodopathy Antibody Panel
Also known as: Autoimmune Nodopathy Antibody Panel; Paranodal Antibody Panel; Nodal-Paranodal Antibody Panel; Autoimmune Neuropathy Nodopathy Panel; Neurofascin/Contactin/CASPR1 Antibody Panel
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood and any other listed specimens for CIDP Paranodal Antibodies / Autoimmune Nodopathy Antibody Panel. Fast only if the request or a component test requires it. Label all containers with patient and collection details.
Description: Autoimmune Nodopathy / Paranodal Antibody Panel is a serum autoantibody panel used in the evaluation of suspected autoimmune nodopathies (paranodopathies), a distinct group of immune-mediated neuropies within the CIDP spectrum associated with antibodies directed against nodal and paranodal proteins of peripheral nerves. The panel typically includes Neurofascin-155 (NF155), Neurofascin-186 (NF186), Contactin-1 (CNTN1), and CASPR1 antibodies, usually detected using cell-based assay (CBA) methodologies. These antibodies are associated with atypical or treatment-refractory demyelinating neuropathies presenting with features such as progressive weakness, sensory ataxia, tremor, distal neuropathy, cranial nerve involvement, or acute/subacute inflammatory neuropathy. Identification of specific nodal/paranodal antibodies may help refine diagnosis, prognostication, and therapeutic selection, particularly in patients with poor response to standard IVIg therapy and possible responsiveness to B-cell-directed therapies such as rituximab. Preferred specimen is serum. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Filarial PCR
text:
Test code: 9172
Test name: Filarial PCR
Also known as: Filaria DNA PCR; Filariasis PCR; Lymphatic Filariasis PCR; Wuchereria bancrofti PCR; Brugia malayi PCR
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect 3?5 mL peripheral venous blood in a sterile EDTA tube and gently invert to mix. Avoid haemolysis and clot formation. For suspected Wuchereria bancrofti or Brugia infection, document collection time and consider nocturnal collection where clinically appropriate. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen, timing and transport requirements.
Description: This test is a molecular qualitative PCR assay used for the detection of filarial parasite DNA in clinical specimens for the diagnosis of filariasis. Depending on assay design and laboratory capability, the test may detect and/or differentiate major human pathogenic filarial species including Wuchereria bancrofti, Brugia malayi, and occasionally other filarial nematodes. PCR offers high analytical sensitivity and specificity and may be useful in cases with low microfilarial burden, occult infection, atypical presentations, partially treated disease, or when smear microscopy is negative despite strong clinical suspicion. The test is primarily used as an adjunctive or confirmatory investigation and does not replace routine conventional methods such as peripheral blood smear microscopy, circulating filarial antigen (CFA) assays, or filarial antibody testing, which remain the standard frontline diagnostic approaches in most clinical settings. name: B Cell Phenotyping
text:
Test code: 9181
Test name: B Cell Phenotyping
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect fresh whole blood in an adequately filled EDTA tube and label with patient and collection details. Do not centrifuge, aliquot or freeze. Submit as soon as possible because cell viability and marker expression deteriorate with delay; include the clinical indication and relevant immunoglobulin/lymphocyte results. Description: B-cell phenotyping by flow cytometry characterises circulating B-cell populations and, depending on the configured panel, may distinguish naïve, memory and class-switched or non-switched subsets. Interpret with the absolute B-cell count, immunoglobulin concentrations, vaccine-specific antibody responses, treatment history and the clinical phenotype.

name: Taenia Solium (Pork Tapeworm) PCR
text:
Test code: 9183
Test name: Taenia Solium (Pork Tapeworm) PCR
Also known as: Taenia solium Molecular Detection; T. solium PCR; Pork Tapeworm PCR
Specimen: CSF,STOOL
Collection instructions: Submit 2 mL of CSF or ocular fluid in a sterile, leak-proof container, or submit a fresh stool sample in a clean, sterile, leak-proof stool container. Stool should not be contaminated with urine, water or disinfectant.
Description: Species-specific molecular detection of Taenia solium DNA in clinical specimens, including CSF, ocular fluid and stool. The assay may support diagnosis of T. solium infection and, in appropriate clinical settings, investigation of suspected cysticercosis/neurocysticercosis or ocular cysticercosis. In stool specimens, molecular testing provides species-specific identification of intestinal Taenia infection. This is particularly useful because the ova of T. solium and T. saginata are morphologically indistinguishable on routine stool microscopy and therefore cannot be reliably speciated by ova morphology alone. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 11990.0

name: PLA2R Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
text:
Test code: 9184
Test name: PLA2R Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
Also known as: PLA2R IHC; Phospholipase A2 Receptor IHC; Anti-PLA2R Tissue Stain;
Specimen: FFPE tumour tissue block
Collection instructions: Submit a representative formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) renal tissue block. Where a block cannot be submitted, appropriately prepared unstained positively charged slides may be accepted subject to laboratory requirements. Relevant histopathology report and clinical information should accompany the specimen where available .
Description: PLA2R1 immunohistochemistry is performed on FFPE renal tissue to assess glomerular expression of phospholipase A2 receptor 1 (PLA2R1), a major target antigen associated with membranous nephropathy. Granular capillary-wall staining supports PLA2R-associated membranous nephropathy when interpreted in conjunction with renal biopsy morphology, immunofluorescence findings and the clinical/serological context. Tissue PLA2R1 staining is particularly useful in the pathological classification of membranous nephropathy and may complement serum anti-PLA2R antibody testing. A negative result does not exclude membranous nephropathy, as other target antigens and secondary disease associations may be involved.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 6990.0

name: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis Precipitins IgG Panel
text:
Test code: 9187
Test name: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis Precipitins IgG Panel
Also known as: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis Antibody Panel; HP Precipitins; Farmer’s Lung/Bird Fancier’s Lung Antibody Panel
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood and any other listed specimens for Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis Precipitins IgG Panel. Fast only if the request or a component test requires it. Label all containers with patient and collection details.
Description: The Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis (HP) IgG Panel is a serological assay that detects IgG antibodies against a range of inhaled environmental antigens associated with hypersensitivity pneumonitis (extrinsic allergic alveolitis), an immune-mediated interstitial lung disease. The test provides evidence of immune sensitisation to potential causative antigens such as moulds, fungi, avian proteins and other occupational or environmental exposures, and is intended to support the diagnostic evaluation of patients with suspected hypersensitivity pneumonitis. Results should always be interpreted in conjunction with the patients exposure history, clinical presentation, high-resolution CT findings, pulmonary function tests and, where appropriate, bronchoalveolar lavage and/or lung biopsy findings. A positive result indicates prior sensitisation to the relevant antigen but does not, by itself, establish the diagnosis of hypersensitivity pneumonitis. A negative result does not exclude the disease, particularly if the causative antigen is not represented within the testing panel. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 17990.0

name: Taenia Saginata (Beef Tapeworm) PCR
text:
Test code: 9188
Test name: Taenia Saginata (Beef Tapeworm) PCR
Also known as: Taenia saginata Molecular Detection; T. saginata PCR; Beef Tapeworm PCR
Specimen: CSF,STOOL,TISSUE
Collection instructions: Submit 2 mL of CSF or ocular fluid in a sterile, leak-proof container, or submit a fresh stool sample in a clean, sterile, leak-proof stool container. Stool should not be contaminated with urine, water or disinfectant.
Description: Species-specific molecular detection of Taenia saginata DNA in submitted clinical specimens. The assay is primarily useful for confirmation and species-level identification of T. saginata infection where taeniasis is clinically or microscopically suspected. In stool specimens, molecular testing differentiates T. saginata from T. solium, whose ova are morphologically indistinguishable by routine microscopy. Detection of T. saginata DNA therefore enables definitive species identification when conventional stool examination can report only Taenia species. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Immunophenotyping
text:
Test code: 9189
Test name: Immunophenotyping
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Submit fresh peripheral blood or bone marrow aspirate in a dedicated EDTA tube. CSF, pleural, ascitic and other body fluids should be collected into a sterile, leak-proof container and clearly labelled with the specimen source. Send specimens promptly to preserve cell viability; do not centrifuge, freeze or fix specimens intended for flow cytometry. For lymph-node or other tissue samples, contact the laboratory before collection for the appropriate transport medium and do not place flow-cytometry tissue in formalin. Include the clinical indication, provisional diagnosis, treatment history and recent FBC or morphology findings.
Description: Flow cytometric immunophenotyping evaluates cell-surface and intracellular antigen expression to detect and characterise abnormal haematolymphoid cell populations. It supports the diagnosis and classification of acute leukaemias, lymphomas, chronic lymphoproliferative disorders and related haematological malignancies. Results should be correlated with the clinical findings, FBC, morphology and relevant cytogenetic or molecular studies. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Report date: 3-Weeks

name: Membranous Nephropathy IHC Panel
text:
Test code: 9200
Test name: Membranous Nephropathy IHC Panel
Also known as: Membranous Nephropathy Immunohistochemistry Panel; MN Antigen Panel; Renal Membranous Nephropathy IHC Panel
Specimen: FFPE tumour tissue block
Collection instructions: Submit a representative formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) renal biopsy tissue block. If the block cannot be submitted, unstained positively charged sections may be accepted depending on laboratory requirements. The renal biopsy report, relevant immunofluorescence findings, serology and pertinent clinical information should accompany the specimen wherever possible.
Description: The Membranous Nephropathy IHC Panel comprises a panel of tissue immunohistochemical markers used in the evaluation and further classification of membranous nephropathy and selected associated renal pathological processes. The panel includes PLA2R1 and additional antigens associated with distinct membranous nephropathy phenotypes, together with ancillary markers as listed above. Panel Components: SV40 (PAb101), THSD7A, NELL-1, PCDH7, EXT1, EXT1 (Polyclonal), EXT2 (Polyclonal), PLA2R1 (IHC), Semaphorin and Amyloid A (RTU). Results should be interpreted in conjunction with light microscopy, immunofluorescence and, where available, electron microscopy, serum antibody studies and the clinical setting. Identification of a characteristic antigen-staining pattern may assist in distinguishing PLA2R-associated membranous nephropathy from other antigen-defined or potentially secondary forms and may guide further clinical investigation.

text:
Test code: 9201
Test name: Claudin 18.2 Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
Also known as: CLDN18.2 IHC
Specimen: BLOCKS
Collection instructions: For Claudin 18.2 Immunohistochemistry (IHC), submit representative tissue in approved fixative, or the specified paraffin block and slides. Label the anatomical site and provide relevant clinical, imaging, and previous pathology information. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: Claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2) Immunohistochemistry is performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor tissue to assess membranous expression of the tight junction protein CLDN18.2, a gastric lineage marker retained in a subset of malignancies, particularly gastric and gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinomas. This assay serves as a predictive biomarker to identify patients who may benefit from targeted therapy such as Zolbetuximab. Staining is interpreted based on the presence, intensity (weak/moderate/strong), and percentage of tumor cells demonstrating membranous positivity, using clinically validated scoring thresholds. Results should be integrated with histopathological findings and other relevant biomarkers (e.g., HER2, PD-L1) to guide therapeutic decision-making. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
