name: Folate Receptor Alpha (FOLR1) Expression – Semi-Quantitative (IHC)
text:
Test code: 9202
Test name: Folate Receptor Alpha (FOLR1) Expression – Semi-Quantitative (IHC)
Also known as: FOLR1 IHC; FRa IHC
Specimen: BLOCKS
Collection instructions: FFPE with >30% tumor tissue. The sample to be received at the lab by 1st of the month.
Description: Folate Receptor Alpha (FOLR1/FRá) is a glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored cell surface protein involved in folate transport and is overexpressed in several epithelial malignancies, most notably high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma and other subsets of epithelial cancers. This test evaluates FRá protein expression by immunohistochemistry (IHC) on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue sections. Expression is assessed in a semi-quantitative manner, incorporating the proportion of tumor cells demonstrating membranous staining and staining intensity, typically reported using a validated scoring system (e.g., percentage positivity and/or composite score). The assay is primarily indicated to identify patients eligible for FRá-targeted therapies (e.g., antibody-drug conjugates such as mirvetuximab soravtansine) and may also provide supportive diagnostic or prognostic information in selected tumor types. Interpretation should be performed in the context of tumor histology, clinical findings, and other relevant biomarkers. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 4 Weeks
Report date: 4-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Leishmania PCR
text:
Test code: 9203
Test name: Leishmania PCR
Also known as: PCR for Leishmania
Specimen: BLOCKS,Bone Marrow Aspirate,EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood or named specimen for Leishmania PCR. Send with the clinical indication and any prior molecular results. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: Leishmania spp. DNA Detection by Real-Time PCR (qPCR) is a highly sensitive and specific molecular assay used for the qualitative detection of Leishmania DNA in clinical specimens. The test employs nucleic acid extraction followed by real-time PCR amplification targeting conserved genomic regions (such as kinetoplast DNA or ribosomal DNA), enabling reliable detection even in cases with low parasite burden. It is applicable to a variety of specimen types including whole blood, bone marrow aspirate, tissue biopsies, and lesion aspirates, depending on the clinical presentation. This assay is indicated for the diagnosis and confirmation of suspected leishmaniasis (visceral, cutaneous, or mucocutaneous), particularly where conventional methods such as microscopy are inconclusive or insensitive. A Detected result supports the presence of active infection and should be interpreted in clinical context, while a Not Detected result does not fully exclude disease, especially in low-level or localized infection. The test is also useful for assessing suspected relapse. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 13990.0

name: Genome-wide DNA Methylation Profiling (CNS Tumor Classifier)
text:
Test code: 9208
Test name: Genome-wide DNA Methylation Profiling (CNS Tumor Classifier)
Also known as: CNS Tumor DNA Methylation Profiling; Brain Tumor DNA Methylation Array; Heidelberg CNS Tumor Classifier
Specimen: BLOCKS
Collection instructions: FFPE with > 30% tumor content
Description: Genome-wide DNA Methylation Profiling (CNS Tumor Classifier) is an advanced molecular diagnostic assay that analyzes genome-wide epigenetic patterns using an Illumina EPIC (850K) methylation array with validated classifier algorithms (e.g., Heidelberg CNS tumor classifier). This test enables objective, biology-based classification of central nervous system tumors by comparing the tumors methylation signature to a large reference dataset, thereby refining or resolving diagnoses that are morphologically and genetically ambiguous. This assay is particularly indicated in high-grade gliomas where there is overlap between adult-type glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) and pediatric-type high-grade glioma (H3-wildtype/IDH-wildtype). It allows definitive distinction between these entities and further subclassifies pediatric-type tumors into clinically relevant molecular subgroups (RTK1, RTK2, MYCN). The test complements histopathology and targeted NGS panels but is essential for accurate integrated diagnosis and risk stratification in such cases. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 5 Weeks
Report date: 5-w
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 169990.0

name: Carrier Screening - Expanded Panel (~2000 genes) including NGS and MLPA (SMA, CYP21A2)
text:
Test code: 9225
Test name: Carrier Screening - Expanded Panel (~2000 genes) including NGS and MLPA (SMA, CYP21A2)
Also known as: Carrier Screening – Comprehensive (sequencing + deletion/duplication analysis)
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: EDTA whole blood for both father & mother.
Description: The Expanded Carrier Screening Panel (~2000 Genes) NGS with MLPA/CNV Analysis is a comprehensive pan-ethnic expanded carrier screening assay designed to detect carrier status for a wide range of inherited genetic disorders. It utilizes high-depth next-generation sequencing (NGS) to identify single nucleotide variants and small insertions/deletions across approximately 2000 clinically relevant genes, with integrated copy number variation (CNV) analysis (via MLPA or validated NGS-based methods) for genes where deletions or duplications are a key disease mechanism. The panel covers autosomal recessive, X-linked, and selected dominant conditions relevant to reproductive risk assessment. Results are reported as carrier detected, no clinically significant variant detected (residual risk remains), or, where appropriate, variants of uncertain significance. This test is indicated for preconception and prenatal screening, with recommendation for partner testing and genetic counseling if a pathogenic variant is identified. Limitations include inability to detect all variant types (e.g., deep intronic or complex rearrangements), and a negative result does not eliminate carrier risk. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 5 Weeks
Report date: 5-w
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 133990.0

name: Liquid based Cytology (LBC) PAP Smear
text:
Test code: 9226
Test name: Liquid based Cytology (LBC) PAP Smear
Also known as: PAP Smear LBC; Gynae LBC
Collection instructions: Collect the cervical sample using the dedicated LBC cervical brush/broom, ensuring adequate sampling of the transformation zone. Insert the brush into the cervical os and rotate as per device instructions to obtain representative ectocervical and endocervical cells. Immediately place the brush into the LBC preservative vial-either by rinsing the head thoroughly or detaching it into the vial depending on the system-and secure the cap tightly. Ensure the sample is correctly labeled and accompanied by relevant clinical details. The liquid-based medium preserves cellular material, reduces obscuring artefacts, and allows for additional testing (e.g., HPV) from the same vial if required, in line with The Bethesda System.
Description: Liquid-Based Cytology (LBC) Pap smear is a cervical cancer screening test in which exfoliated cells from the transformation zone of the cervix are collected and preserved in a liquid medium, allowing for improved sample quality, standardized preparation, and enhanced detection of epithelial abnormalities. Compared to conventional smears, LBC reduces obscuring factors such as blood, mucus, and inflammation, and provides a more uniform cellular distribution, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy and adequacy rates. The residual sample also permits ancillary testing, including high-risk HPV DNA testing where indicated. Reporting is performed in accordance with the The Bethesda System. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings, prior cytology/HPV status, and current screening guidelines. Abnormal results may require further evaluation with HPV testing, colposcopy, or biopsy depending on the category and patient risk profile.
Reported turnaround: After Five Days
Report date: 5-Days
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 4690.0

name: FMR1 Premutation Test (Fragile X CGG Repeat Analysis)
text:
Test code: 9229
Test name: FMR1 Premutation Test (Fragile X CGG Repeat Analysis)
Also known as: FMR1 CGG Repeat Expansion Analysis; Fragile X DNA test
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: 4ml of EDTA whole blood. Clinical genetic history mandatory.
Description: FMR1 CGG Repeat Expansion Analysis (Fragile X Premutation Test) is a molecular assay that quantifies CGG repeat length in the FMR1 gene to identify normal, intermediate, premutation (55?200), and full mutation (>200) alleles. It is indicated in women with premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), unexplained infertility, or relevant family history. Testing is performed by TP-PCR with capillary electrophoresis, with reflex methods for large expansions if required. Detection of a premutation supports Fragile Xassociated POI (FXPOI) and has key reproductive implications, including risk of expansion in offspring. Results are reported as CGG repeat number with interpretation; genetic counseling is recommended for positive findings. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 23390.0

name: Strongyloidiasis IgG Serology (Serum)
text:
Test code: 9231
Test name: Strongyloidiasis IgG Serology (Serum)
Also known as: Strongyloidiasis IgG Serology
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Strongyloidiasis IgG Serology (Serum) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: Strongyloides serology detects IgG antibodies to Strongyloides stercoralis using ELISA and serves as the preferred initial screening test, particularly in patients with suspected chronic infection or low parasite burden where stool microscopy is frequently negative. It has high sensitivity (˜85?95%) and is especially valuable in pre-immunosuppression screening (e.g., prior to corticosteroids, chemotherapy, or transplantation), where missing infection carries a risk of life-threatening hyperinfection. A positive result supports exposure or infection and should be interpreted in clinical context, with consideration for confirmatory stool testing (agar plate culture or tissue) where feasible. However, serology cannot distinguish active from past infection and may show cross-reactivity with other helminths. A negative result does not fully exclude infection, particularly in immunocompromised patients, and further evaluation should be pursued if clinical suspicion remains high. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 5 Weeks
Report date: 5-w
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 14390.0

name: Oncotype DX Breast Recurrence Score Test (Insurance/billed account)
text:
Test code: 9233
Test name: Oncotype DX Breast Recurrence Score Test (Insurance/billed account)
Specimen: BLOCKS
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Oncotype DX Breast Recurrence Score Test (Insurance/Billed Account) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The Oncotype DX® Breast Recurrence Score is a quantitative RT-PCR-based genomic assay performed on formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor tissue from patients with early-stage, estrogen receptor (ER)-positive, HER2-negative invasive breast carcinoma. The test analyzes the expression of 21 genes (16 cancer-related genes and 5 reference genes) to generate a Recurrence Score® result ranging from 0-100. This score provides prognostic information regarding the risk of distant recurrence at 9-10 years and predicts the potential benefit of adjuvant chemotherapy when added to endocrine therapy. The assay is performed at a centralized reference laboratory (Exact Sciences) and requires submission of tumor tissue block with a completed requisition form. Results are reported as a numeric Recurrence Score with interpretive categories and clinical guidance based on established clinical trial validation studies (e.g., TAILORx). This test is intended for use in appropriately selected patients as part of multidisciplinary treatment planning. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 3 Weeks
Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 439990.0

name: SP100 Antibody Test for Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC)
text:

Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: SP100 antibody (IgG) is a highly specific antinuclear autoantibody associated with Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC). It is most commonly detected in patients with PBC who are AMA-negative, and supports the diagnosis in the appropriate clinical setting (cholestatic liver enzymes, pruritus, fatigue, and compatible imaging/biopsy findings). A positive SP100 antibody result strongly favors PBC and may be associated with more active autoimmune cholangitis. A negative result does not exclude PBC, and interpretation should be integrated with AMA (especially AMA-M2), GP210 antibody, liver biochemistry, and clinical findings. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Multiple Myeloma Panel by FISH
text:
Test code: 9246
Test name: Multiple Myeloma Panel by FISH
Also known as: Plasma Cell Myeloma Cytogenetics
Specimen: Sodium Heparin
Collection instructions: 4ml whole blood or 2ml Bone Marrow in SODIUM HEPARIN
Description: The Multiple Myeloma FISH Panel panel detects key cytogenetic abnormalities in plasma cell myeloma to support diagnosis, prognostic risk stratification, and treatment planning. It is performed on bone marrow aspirate (preferred) or plasma cell-enriched specimens and should be interpreted alongside morphology, flow cytometry, and serum/urine protein studies. Service parameters (targets) include 1q amplification/1p deletion, DLEU/12 centromere (13q deletion/trisomy 12), ATM deletion (11q deletion), TP53 deletion (17p deletion), IGH rearrangement, MYEOV::IGH t(11;14), FGFR3::IGH t(4;14), and MAF::IGH t(14;16). High-risk findings include del(17p)/TP53, t(4;14), t(14;16), and 1q gain/amplification, while t(11;14) may have therapeutic relevance. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days

Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Topiramate
text:
Test code: 9248
Test name: Topiramate
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Serum (Red top or Plain)
Description: Serum topiramate levels may be measured to support dose optimization in selected clinical situations, including inadequate seizure or migraine control, suspected non-adherence, potential drugdrug interactions (e.g., with enzyme-inducing antiepileptics), renal impairment, pregnancy, or dose-related adverse effects such as cognitive slowing, paresthesias, or metabolic acidosis. Levels are best interpreted at steady state, preferably using a trough sample. The clinical response and tolerability vary widely between patients. Concentrations below therapeutic reference range may be associated with reduced efficacy, while higher levels increase the risk of toxicity. text:

Description: MGMT Promoter Methylation Analysis (Tumor Tissue) assay detects methylation of the MGMT gene promoter in tumor DNA (typically from FFPE tissue) using PCR- or pyrosequencing-based methods. Promoter methylation leads to reduced MGMT expression and impaired DNA repair capacity. name: N-MYC (NMYCN) Amplification by FISH
text:
Test code: 9254
Test name: N-MYC (NMYCN) Amplification by FISH
Also known as: NMYCN
Specimen: BLOCKS
Collection instructions: Collect the specimen specified for cytogenetic analysis in the approved anticoagulant. Do not refrigerate or freeze unless the receiving laboratory instructs otherwise. Provide the clinical indication and submit promptly. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: N-MYC (MYCN) amplification analysis by fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is performed for prognostic risk stratification in neuroblastoma. The assay uses dual-color probes targeting the MYCN locus at chromosome 2p24 and a chromosome 2 reference probe, allowing assessment of MYCN gene copy number relative to chromosome 2 in interphase tumor nuclei from FFPE tissue or cytology specimens with adequate tumor cellularity. MYCN amplification is defined by a marked increase in MYCN signals relative to the chromosome 2 control (or the presence of MYCN signal clusters) and is a well-established adverse prognostic marker, associated with aggressive tumor biology and high-risk disease irrespective of age or stage. The result directly informs treatment intensity and clinical risk group assignment. Findings should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical stage, histology, DNA ploidy, and other genomic abnormalities (e.g., segmental chromosomal aberrations). This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: FLT3 ITD & TKD (D835Y) Mutations
text:
Test code: 9257
Test name: FLT3 ITD & TKD (D835Y) Mutations
Also known as: D835Y
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood or named specimen for FLT3 ITD & TKD (D835Y) Mutations. Send with the clinical indication and any prior molecular results. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: FLT3 mutation testing identifies activating alterations in the FLT3 receptor tyrosine kinase, a key prognostic and therapeutic biomarker in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The two clinically relevant mutations are FLT3-ITD (internal tandem duplication) involving the juxtamembrane domain, and FLT3-TKD mutations, most commonly D835Y, within the tyrosine kinase domain. Both result in constitutive FLT3 signaling and are associated with aggressive disease biology, high leukemic burden, and increased relapse risk, particularly for FLT3-ITD. Detection of FLT3 mutations informs risk stratification, treatment selection, and transplant planning. FLT3-ITD is generally associated with adverse risk (context-dependent), while FLT3-TKD confers intermediate risk. Identification of either mutation supports the use of FLT3 inhibitors (e.g., midostaurin in frontline therapy; gilteritinib in relapsed/refractory disease) and guides monitoring for acquired resistance, especially emergence of TKD mutations during therapy. Results should be interpreted alongside co-mutations (e.g., NPM1) and reported with variant allele frequency or allelic ratio where available. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: MI 2 (Anti-Mi-2 myositis-specific Ab)
text:
Test code: 9258
Test name: MI 2 (Anti-Mi-2 myositis-specific Ab)
Also known as: Dermatomyositis Antibody DM Ab
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for MI 2 (Anti-Mi-2 Myositis-Specific Ab) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: Anti-Mi-2 myositis-specific autoantibody is a highly specific serologic marker for dermatomyositis (DM). Its presence supports the diagnosis in patients with compatible clinical features such as proximal muscle weakness and characteristic cutaneous manifestations (e.g., Gottron papules, heliotrope rash). Anti-Mi-2 antibodies are most commonly detected in classic adult DM and are infrequently seen in polymyositis or other connective tissue diseases, enhancing their diagnostic utility. Clinically, Anti-Mi-2 positivity is associated with a more favorable prognosis, including good response to corticosteroids and immunosuppressive therapy, lower risk of interstitial lung disease, and reduced malignancy association compared with other myositis-specific antibodies. While titers are not routinely used for disease monitoring, results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings, muscle enzymes, imaging, and histopathology where indicated. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: NPM1 Gene Mutation Quantitative PCR
text:
Test code: 9259
Test name: NPM1 Gene Mutation Quantitative PCR
Also known as: PCR for NPM1 Gene Mutation Quantitative
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect EDTA whole blood or bone marrow aspirate as specified by the referral laboratory. Provide the AML diagnosis, NPM1 mutation type where known, treatment phase, prior molecular results and collection time.
Description: NPM1 Gene Mutation Quantitative PCR (qPCR) is a sensitive molecular test used to detect and quantify NPM1 gene mutations, most commonly seen in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). These mutations, typically involving exon 12 insertions, occur in about 30?35% of adult AML and define a biologically and prognostically distinct subgroup. The assay is mutation-specific and can detect very low levels of mutated transcripts, with analytical sensitivity reaching 10?4 to 10?5. The test is primarily used for measurable residual disease (MRD) monitoring. Serial measurement of NPM1-mutated transcript levels allows assessment of treatment response and early detection of molecular relapse, often before clinical or hematologic recurrence. Persistent or rising transcript levels are associated with increased relapse risk, while deep molecular remission correlates with favorable prognosis. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Oxcarbazepine (Trileptal)
text:
Test code: 9260
Test name: Oxcarbazepine (Trileptal)
Also known as: Trileptal
Specimen: Lithium Heparin,Serum
Collection instructions: Collect serum for Oxcarbazepine (Trileptal) therapeutic drug monitoring. Record the last dose time.
Description: Oxcarbazepine is an anticonvulsant used in the management of seizure disorders, and its therapeutic monitoring is performed by measuring the serum concentration of its active metabolite, 10-monohydroxy derivative (MHD). The usual therapeutic range for MHD is approximately 10?35 mcg/mL, though this may vary depending on the laboratory reference values. Measurement of MHD levels is clinically useful to evaluate medication adherence, adequacy of dosing, and risk of toxicity. Sub-therapeutic levels may explain breakthrough seizures or inadequate seizure control, whereas supra-therapeutic levels can be associated with adverse central nervous system effects such as dizziness, drowsiness, diplopia, and ataxia, as well as systemic complications like hyponatremia. Interpretation of the oxcarbazepine/MHD level should therefore be integrated with the patients clinical status, seizure frequency, reported side effects, and potential drug interactions. Dose adjustments or other therapeutic decisions should be guided by both the laboratory result and the overall clinical context. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Tests included: 10-hydroxycarbazepine, Oxcarbazepine

Test code: 9269
Test name: Celiac Disease IgA Panel (Tansglutaminase and GAF-3X)
Also known as: Coeliac disease IgA Panel (Immunoblot) x2 Parameters; Anti Tissue Glutaminase and AntiGliadin (GAF-3X) IgA
Description: The Celiac IgA Panel is a serological test used in the screening and diagnosis of celiac disease by detecting IgA antibodies directed against tissue transglutaminase (tTG IgA) and/or deamidated gliadin peptides (DGP IgA). These antibodies are produced in response to gluten exposure and are highly sensitive markers of gluten-induced intestinal injury. A positive result suggests active celiac disease when the patient is consuming a gluten-containing diet. This test is considered the preferred initial screening tool in individuals with normal IgA levels and may also be used to monitor response and adherence to a gluten-free diet.
Tests included: Anti-Gliadin (IgA), Anti-Tissue Transglutaminase (IgA)
Reported turnaround: Same Day
Report date: 8-Hours
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 8990.0

name: BCR-ABL by FISH
text:
Test code: 9274
Test name: BCR-ABL by FISH
Also known as: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) FISH; Philadelphia chromosome (Ph)
Specimen: Sodium Heparin
Description: BCR-ABL by FISH is a fluorescence in situ hybridization assay using dual-color, dual-fusion probes targeting the BCR (22q11.2) and ABL1 (9q34) loci to detect the t(9;22)(q34;q11.2) (Philadelphia chromosome). It is used for the diagnosis and classification of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL), and for identifying variant or complex rearrangements, using peripheral blood or bone marrow without the need for metaphase cells. Results are reported as positive or negative with the percentage of nuclei showing fusion signals; a positive result confirms a BCR-ABL1 rearrangement in the appropriate clinical context, while a negative result does not exclude low-level disease and should be correlated with morphology, immunophenotyping, cytogenetics, and RT-PCR, which is also required for transcript typing and MRD monitoring.
Reported turnaround: After One Week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: TUE & FRI
Standard price (KES): 15390.0

name: Atypical Haemolytic Uraemic Syndrome (aHUS) by MLPA
text:
Test code: 9281 Test name: Atypical Haemolytic Uraemic Syndrome (aHUS) by MLPA Also known as: Atypical HUS by MLPA, aHUS Copy-Number Analysis, Complement Gene Deletion/Duplication Analysis Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood) Collection instructions: Collect 4 mL of whole blood and mix gently by inversion. Label the tube with two patient identifiers. Include the clinical indication and attach any prior genetic report if requesting confirmation of an NGS finding. Description:

This assay uses Multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) to detect deletions and duplications in selected complement gene regions associated with atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome (aHUS). It can help investigate suspected complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy and confirm copy-number changes identified by sequencing, where the relevant regions are covered by the assay.

For the current referral, specify confirmation of the suspected homozygous deletion involving CFHR3 and CFHR1. Confirm with the reference laboratory that both genes are covered and that the assay distinguishes a one-copy deletion from a two-copy deletion.

Reported turnaround: 4 Weeks Report date: 4-Weeks Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU Standard price (KES): 36990.0

name: Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) Panel
text:
Test code: 9297
Test name: Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) Panel
Also known as: ELF
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood and any other listed specimens for Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) Panel. Fast only if the request or a component test requires it. Label all containers with patient and collection details.
Description: The Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) Panel is a non-invasive serum test that assesses the severity of liver fibrosis by measuring Hyaluronic Acid (HA), Amino-terminal Propeptide of Type III Procollagen (PIIINP), and Tissue Inhibitor of Metalloproteinases-1 (TIMP-1). These biomarkers reflect extracellular matrix turnover and fibrogenesis, and are combined into a calculated ELF score that correlates with fibrosis stage, aiding in the management of chronic liver diseases such as NAFLD/MASLD, viral hepatitis, alcohol-related liver disease, and autoimmune liver conditions. The ELF score helps suggest the degree of minimal fibrosis, minimum vs ndeterminate vs advanced fibrosis. While the test is useful for non-invasive fibrosis assessment and monitoring, it should be interpreted alongside clinical evaluation, imaging, and other investigations, as it cannot determine disease etiology and may be influenced by systemic fibrotic or inflammatory\\~conditions. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 10990.0

name: Karyotyping - POC
text:
Test code: 9329
Test name: Karyotyping - POC
Collection instructions: Sample Collection Instructions for POC Karyotyping Tissue Type: Submit chorionic villi or fetal tissue (preferably placental villi, not maternal decidua). Avoid blood clots and maternal tissue. Container: Use a sterile, screw-cap container. Transport Medium: Place the sample in sterile saline or transport medium (e.g., RPMI or Hanks Balanced Salt Solution). Do not use formalin or fixatives. Volume: A tissue piece about 2-4 cm³ is usually sufficient. Labeling: Clearly label the container with patient identifiers and indicate it is a POC specimen. Timing: Deliver to the lab as soon as possible (ideally within 24 hours) at room temperature or refrigerated (4-8?C). Do not freeze. Requisition: Include clinical details, gestational age, reason for testing (e.g., recurrent miscarriage), and contact information.
Description: Karyotyping of POC is a cytogenetic analysis used to detect chromosomal abnormalities that may underlie miscarriage or pregnancy loss. It helps identify aneuploidies (e.g., trisomy 13, 18, 21, monosomy X), polyploidies, and structural chromosomal anomalies. The test is most informative in recurrent pregnancy loss, second-trimester losses, or when fetal anomalies are suspected. Ideally, fresh tissue should be submitted promptly in sterile conditions to optimize cell culture success. Limitations include culture failure and maternal cell contamination. Molecular techniques (e.g., chromosomal microarray) may be considered where available for higher resolution and better diagnostic yield. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 3 Weeks
Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 13390.0

name: Thiopurine Methyltransferase (TPMT) Genotyping PCR
text:
Test code: 9348
Test name: Thiopurine Methyltransferase (TPMT) Genotyping PCR
Also known as: TPMT; PCR for Thiopurine Methyltransferase (TPMT) Genotyping
Specimen: Whole Blood
Collection instructions: Collect urine for Thiopurine Methyltransferase (TPMT) Genotyping PCR in a clean, leak-proof laboratory container. Avoid contamination with faeces or toilet water. Follow any midstream, first-morning, or timed instruction on the request. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: Thiopurine Methyltransferase (TPMT) genotyping identifies common inherited variants in the TPMT gene that reduce or abolish enzyme activity. The presence of heterozygous or homozygous variants correlates with intermediate or deficient TPMT enzyme activity, respectively, and directly impacts the metabolism of thiopurine drugs such as azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, and thioguanine. Patients with low or absent enzyme function are at high risk of severe, dose-related myelosuppression when treated with standard thiopurine doses. Genotyping provides predictive information on thiopurine tolerance prior to therapy and helps guide dose adjustment or alternative treatment choices. Patients with no variants (wild-type) are usually suitable for standard dosing, while heterozygous carriers require reduced doses with close monitoring. Homozygous variant patients are generally contraindicated for standard thiopurine therapy and may only be considered for significantly reduced dosing under specialist care. Unlike enzyme activity assays, genotyping is not affected by recent transfusions, cytopenias, or intercurrent illness. However, it only detects known polymorphisms and does not capture all possible genetic or non-genetic factors influencing TPMT activity. For optimal patient safety, TPMT genotyping should be interpreted alongside clinical context, blood count monitoring, and, where relevant, consideration of additional pharmacogenetic variants such as NUDT15. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Thiopurine Methyltransferase (TPMT) Enzyme Activity
text:
Test code: 9350
Test name: Thiopurine Methyltransferase (TPMT) Enzyme Activity
Also known as: TPMT
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect urine for Thiopurine Methyltransferase (TPMT) Enzyme Activity in a clean, leak-proof laboratory container. Avoid contamination with faeces or toilet water. Follow any midstream, first-morning, or timed instruction on the request. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: Thiopurine Methyltransferase (TPMT) is a key enzyme in the metabolism of thiopurine drugs such as azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, and thioguanine. Variability in TPMT activity, due to inherited genetic polymorphisms, directly influences drug tolerance and risk of toxicity. Patients with reduced or absent TPMT activity are unable to adequately inactivate thiopurines, predisposing them to severe, potentially life-threatening myelosuppression if treated with standard doses. Assessment of TPMT enzyme activity before initiating thiopurine therapy provides important guidance for individualized dosing. Patients with normal or high activity can usually receive standard dosing, while those with intermediate activity require reduced doses and close monitoring. Individuals with very low or absent activity should generally avoid thiopurine therapy, or only receive minimal doses under specialist supervision. Regardless of TPMT status, regular clinical and hematological monitoring remains essential, as other factors-including NUDT15 variants, concomitant medications, and underlying bone marrow function-also affect drug safety and efficacy. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

metadata.instructions: Collect urine for Thiopurine Methyltransferase (TPMT) Enzyme Activity in a clean, leak-proof laboratory container. Avoid contamination with faeces or toilet water. Follow any midstream, first-morning, or timed instruction on the request. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
metadata.description: Thiopurine Methyltransferase (TPMT) is a key enzyme in the metabolism of thiopurine drugs such as azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, and thioguanine. Variability in TPMT activity, due to inherited genetic polymorphisms, directly influences drug tolerance and risk of toxicity. Patients with reduced or absent TPMT activity are unable to adequately inactivate thiopurines, predisposing them to severe, potentially life-threatening myelosuppression if treated with standard doses. Assessment of TPMT enzyme activity before initiating thiopurine therapy provides important guidance for individualized dosing. Patients with normal or high activity can usually receive standard dosing, while those with intermediate activity require reduced doses and close monitoring. Individuals with very low or absent activity should generally avoid thiopurine therapy, or only receive minimal doses under specialist supervision. Regardless of TPMT status, regular clinical and hematological monitoring remains essential, as other factors-including NUDT15 variants, concomitant medications, and underlying bone marrow function-also affect drug safety and efficacy. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Voltage Gated Potassium Channel (VGKC) Antibodies - LGI1 and CASPR2 and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: This assay, historically reported as the voltage-gated potassium channel (VGKC) antibodies test, primarily detects antibodies directed against proteins associated with the VGKC complex rather than the potassium channel itself, specifically LGI1 (leucine-rich glioma-inactivated 1) and CASPR2 (contactin-associated protein-like 2). These are now recognised as the true, clinically relevant antigens. Only the presence of LGI1 or CASPR2 antibodies is considered pathogenic and diagnostically meaningful; isolated, non-specific VGKC positivity in the absence of these antibodies is generally of limited clinical significance and must be interpreted in the context of the patients clinical phenotype. LGI1 antibodies are strongly associated with autoimmune limbic encephalitis, typically presenting with subacute memory impairment, confusion and seizuresparticularly faciobrachial dystonic seizuresand frequently accompanied by hyponatraemia, with characteristic medial temporal lobe changes on MRI. CASPR2 antibodies are linked to a broader clinical spectrum, including peripheral nerve hyperexcitability, Morvan syndrome, dysautonomia, neuropathic pain and, less commonly, limbic encephalitis, with a stronger association with thymoma and other malignancies. Both conditions are usually highly responsive to early immunotherapy, and detection should prompt neurological evaluation, targeted neuroimaging, CSF/EEG studies, appropriate malignancy screening (particularly in CASPR2-positive cases), and timely initiation of treatment. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 20990.0

text:

Specimen: Streck tube
Collection instructions: Whole Blood in Streck tube x2 (two tubes of 10 ml each). Contact the laboratory to be supplied the Streck tubes upon request.
Description: The EGFR test on liquid biopsy is used to monitor for development of EGFR T790M drug-resistant mutation in patients administered tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy for EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer. It is also used to monitor response to therapy and disease progression in patients treated with EGFR T790M-specific TKIs The EGFR gene mutation test by Droplet Digital PCR detects presence of specific genetic mutations in non-small cell lung cancer tumor cells. The EGFR mutations are commonly seen in lung adenocarcinomas, and less frequently in adenosquamous carcinoma but are extremely rare in squamous cell carcinoma. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Test code: 9408
Test name: HBV Qualitative by Real-time PCR
Also known as: PCR for HBV Qualitative by Real-time
Specimen: Serum,EDTA (Plasma)
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood or named specimen for HBV Qualitative by Real-time PCR. Send with the clinical indication and any prior molecular results. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: Qualitative real-time HBV PCR detects hepatitis B virus DNA and confirms the presence of circulating viral nucleic acid without providing a quantitative viral load. It is useful in selected diagnostic situations, but assessment and monitoring of chronic HBV infection generally require quantitative HBV DNA together with serological and biochemical markers. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 11990.0

name: Allergy Drug Testing Neomycin
text:
Test code: 9413
Test name: Allergy Drug Testing Neomycin
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved blood specimen. This is not a drug-level or challenge test. Send a detailed drug-exposure and reaction history (drug, timing, nature of reaction). A laboratory result alone does not confirm or exclude drug allergy. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: Specialist allergy evaluation for suspected hypersensitivity to Neomycin, a aminoglycoside antibiotic. Validated in-vitro allergy testing is limited for many antimicrobials, so a laboratory result cannot establish or exclude allergy on its own; interpretation should consider the reaction phenotype, timing and any specialist skin or supervised challenge testing. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 3690.0

name: Karyotyping - Bone marrow/Haemat Malignancy
text:
Test code: 9435
Test name: Karyotyping - Bone marrow/Haemat Malignancy
Also known as: Karyotyping - BM/Haemat Malignancy
Specimen: Sodium Heparin,Whole Blood
Collection instructions: Collect 1?3 mL of bone marrow aspirate into a sodium heparin (green top) tube for cytogenetic karyotyping analysis. Immediately after collection, gently invert the tube 8?10 times to ensure proper mixing with the anticoagulant; avoid vigorous shaking to prevent cellular damage and reduced viability. Ensure the specimen is clearly labeled and free from clots or excessive peripheral blood dilution. Transport the sample to the laboratory as soon as possible at room temperature (18?25?C). Do not refrigerate or freeze the specimen, as this may compromise cell culture viability. For optimal chromosome growth and metaphase yield, the specimen should ideally reach the laboratory and be processed within 24 hours of collection.
Description: Bone marrow karyotyping is a cytogenetic test used to evaluate the number and structure of chromosomes in dividing bone marrow cells. The test helps detect chromosomal abnormalities associated with hematological disorders such as leukemias, lymphomas, myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs), aplastic anemia, and other bone marrow malignancies. Chromosomal analysis assists in diagnosis, prognosis, disease classification, treatment selection, and monitoring of disease progression or response to therapy. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 13390.0

name: Hepatitis E Virus (HEV) RNA PCR
text:
Test code: 4620
Test name: Hepatitis E Virus (HEV) RNA PCR
Also known as: HEV PCR; Hepatitis E Virus RNA PCR; HEV RNA Qualitative PCR
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood or named specimen for Hepatitis E Virus (HEV) RNA PCR. Send with the clinical indication and any prior molecular results. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: Hepatitis E Virus (HEV) RNA Detection by PCR is a highly sensitive molecular assay used for the direct detection of HEV RNA in blood specimens. The test confirms active HEV infection and is particularly useful in patients with suspected acute hepatitis E, immunocompromised individuals, transplant recipients, and cases where serological findings are inconclusive. Detection of viral RNA provides evidence of ongoing infection and may identify cases before antibody responses become detectable. This assay complements HEV serology (IgM and IgG) and is considered the preferred method for diagnosing active infection in patients with impaired immune responses. HEV RNA testing may also be used for monitoring persistent or chronic HEV infection, particularly in immunosuppressed patients. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings, liver function tests, epidemiological risk factors, and other hepatitis investigations. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 18990.0

name: POLE Mutation Analysis by NGS (Solid Single Gene Assay)
text:
Test code: 9516
Test name: POLE Mutation Analysis by NGS (Solid Single Gene Assay)
Also known as: DNA Polymerase Epsilon Mutation Analysis; POLE Exonuclease Domain Mutation Analysis: POLE Gene Mutation Test; POLE Exonuclease Domain Mutation Analysis; POLE Single Gene NGS Assay
Collection instructions: Submit representative tumour tissue (usually an FFPE block or approved alternative) with the histological diagnosis and estimated tumour content. Provide the clinical indication and any prior molecular or pathology results. Follow current laboratory or referral-laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: POLE Mutation Analysis by Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) is a molecular assay designed to detect clinically significant pathogenic variants in the POLE (DNA polymerase epsilon catalytic subunit) gene, particularly within the exonuclease proofreading domain. Mutations in POLE are associated with an ultramutated tumour phenotype characterized by exceptionally high tumour mutational burden and increased neoantigen formation. The test is primarily utilized in the molecular classification and prognostic stratification of endometrial carcinoma and may also have relevance in selected colorectal and other solid tumours. Identification of pathogenic POLE mutations is clinically important as POLE-mutated tumours often demonstrate favourable prognosis despite high-grade histologic features and may influence risk stratification, adjuvant treatment decisions, and eligibility for immunotherapy-based approaches in selected clinical contexts. Results should be interpreted together with histopathology, mismatch repair (MMR/MSI) status, p53 status, clinical findings, and other relevant molecular studies. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 3 Weeks
Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 53690.0

text:
Test code: 9517
Test name: Hepatitis D Antibodies
Also known as: Hepatitis Delta Virus; Anti-HDV
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Hepatitis D Antibodies and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: Hepatitis D antibodies (anti-HDV) detect serological evidence of exposure to hepatitis D virus in a person with hepatitis B infection. A reactive antibody result does not establish active HDV replication; HDV RNA is required to confirm current infection and should be interpreted with HBsAg and liver disease status. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Rabies Antibody IgG
text:
Test code: 9526
Test name: Rabies Antibody IgG
Also known as: Rabies IgG Antibodies (EIA)
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Rabies Antibody IgG and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The Rabies IgG antibody test detects the presence of Rabies IgG antibody and measures the titre levels for assessment of the protective response and immune status in persons who have received the rabies vaccine. The antibody levels are expected to be highest approximately 2 - 3 weeks after completing a primary Rabies virus vaccination schedule and thereafter the levels subside over time. The lab determines the acceptable seroconversion level above which the vaccination could be considered as successful. It is recommended to check the antibody titre every 6 months in persons at risk of exposure to Rabies cases or contacts. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 13390.0

name: TSI - Thyroid Stimulating Immunoglobulin by CLIA
text:
Test code: 9583
Test name: TSI - Thyroid Stimulating Immunoglobulin by CLIA
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Sample should reach the lab on or before 1st of the month.
Description: Graves disease caused by IgG immunoglobulins, collectively known as thyroid stimulating immunoglobulins (TSI). TSI test is a functional assay detecting stimulating TSH receptor antibodies, primarily used in Graves disease diagnosis and management. It is a useful test when first-line thyroid antibodies tests in hyperthyroidism fail to confirm autoimmune etiology as it is more specific than TPOAb or TgAb. Patients who are candidates for anti-thyroid drug therapy may not respond to this treatment when TSI levels are markedly elevated. The determination of TSI can also assist in predicting hyperthyroidism in neonates due to placental transmission of the immunoglobulins from mothers with hyperthyroidism. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 8990.0

name: Beta Hydroxybutyrate (Ketone Body)
text:
Test code: 9586
Test name: Beta Hydroxybutyrate (Ketone Body)
Also known as: B-Hydroxybutyrate
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Beta Hydroxybutyrate (Ketone Body) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: Beta hydroxybutyrate, a predominant ketone is an extremely reliable guide for monitoring insulin therapy in the treatment of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA). During successful therapy, Total ketones & Beta Hydroxybutyrate decreases but Acetoacetate increases. It may produce a paradoxical situation, as ketosis may appear to worsen because most of the tests for ketosis detects acetoacetate only whereas Beta hydroxybutyrate measurement quantitates this decrease. Its production increases during decreased carbohydrate availability as in starvation & frequent vomiting or decreased carbohydrate utilization as in Diabetes Mellitus, Glycogen storage diseases, Alkalosis & Salicylate poisoning. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 8990.0

name: Autoimmune Myositis Panel IgG (Extended) x16 Markers
text:
Test code: 9562
Test name: Autoimmune Myositis Panel IgG (Extended) x16 Markers
Also known as: Extended
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood and any other listed specimens for Autoimmune Myositis Panel IgG (Extended) x16 Markers. Fast only if the request or a component test requires it. Label all containers with patient and collection details.
Description: The Autoimmune Myositis Panel IgG (Extended) is a multiplex immunoblot assay that detects 16 clinically relevant myositis-specific and myositis-associated autoantibodies in a single test. It is used in the evaluation of suspected idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs), including dermatomyositis, polymyositis, anti-synthetase syndrome, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis, and overlap connective tissue disease-associated myositis. The panel includes antibodies against Mi-2a, Mi-2ß, TIF1?, MDA5, NXP2, SAE1, Jo-1, SRP, PL-7, PL-12, EJ, OJ, Ku, PM-Scl75, PM-Scl100, and Ro52. Detection of specific autoantibodies can assist in disease classification, prognostication, and identification of important clinical associations such as interstitial lung disease, malignancy risk, cutaneous manifestations, and overlap autoimmune syndromes. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with the patients clinical presentation, muscle enzyme levels, imaging studies, electromyography, and muscle biopsy findings where applicable, as the presence or absence of autoantibodies alone does not establish or exclude a diagnosis of inflammatory myopathy. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 24390.0

name: BRCA 1 and BRCA 2 Somatic
text:
Test code: 8855
Test name: BRCA 1 and BRCA 2 Somatic
Description: -360 The BRCA somatic testing checks for presence in tumor cells of mutations in two genes called BRCA1 and BRCA2 . The BRCA1 and BRCA2 are known as tumour suppressor genes - they prevent cells from growing too rapidly or in an uncontrolled way. BRCA somatic testing on tissue biopsies having cancer cells helps to identify patients with cancer, particularly advanced ovarian cancer and also prostate cancer, who may benefit from PARP inhibitors depending on presence of BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes. Unlike germline mutation testing that looks for inherited mutations, the somatic mutations are not hereditary mutations but are acquired mutations confined to the tumor cells / tissues.

name: Alzheimer’s Disease CSF Screening Panel (Tau and Amyloid)
text:
Test code: 1016
Test name: Alzheimer’s Disease CSF Screening Panel (Tau and Amyloid)
Also known as: CSF Tau and Amyloid Profile; Alzheimer’s Disease CSF Biomarker Profile; CSF Aß42, Aß40, Tau Profile
Specimen: CSF
Collection instructions: CSF collected via lumbar puncture; gravity drip method is advised and the use of tubings is discouraged in collections. Samples should be handled under standard pre-analytical protocols (avoid blood contamination; prompt centrifugation and freezing if delayed). Transportation should be at 2-8 C and if delay is anticipated frozen at -15 to -25 C. Minimum 3 ml of CSF is recommended.
Description: This profile aids in the evaluation of patients with cognitive impairment or suspected early Alzheimers disease. The combined analysis of Aß42, Aß40, and their ratio, alongside total Tau, provides higher sensitivity and specificity than single markers. The profile measures core cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers associated with Alzheimers disease (AD) pathology using ELISA methodology. The panel includes: - CSF Total Tau (tTau): Reflects the extent of neuronal injury and degeneration - CSF ß-Amyloid (1-42): A key peptide that decreases in CSF with amyloid plaque deposition in the brain. - CSF ß-Amyloid (1-40): The predominant amyloid peptide in CSF; included to normalize Aß42 variability - CSF ß-Amyloid 42/40 Ratio: Improves diagnostic accuracy by accounting for inter individual variation in Aß production, increasing specificity for amyloid pathology. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 37390.0

text:
Test code: 1019

Also known as: Anti Microsomal AbAMA-M2
Specimen: Serum,Plasma
Description: Anti-microsomal antibodies, more commonly referred to as anti-thyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) antibodies, are autoantibodies directed against an enzyme involved in thyroid hormone synthesis. Their presence is a hallmark of autoimmune thyroid diseases such as Hashimoto s thyroiditis and Graves disease. This test is used to support the diagnosis of autoimmune thyroid dysfunction, especially in patients with abnormal thyroid function tests, goitre, or clinical symptoms suggestive of hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism. Elevated anti-TPO levels may also indicate a risk of thyroid dysfunction during or after pregnancy.

name: Blood Culture (Paediatric)
text:
Test code: 1025
Test name: Blood Culture (Paediatric)
Also known as: Pediatric (Blood Culture)/ Pediatric bottle
Specimen: Blood Culture
Collection instructions: Collection Instructions The optimal sample for blood culture is one of adequate amount and collected in a manner that prevents contamination of the sample by skin flora. As much as possible, blood should be collected prior to initiation of antibiotics, unless it is a follow-up sample for previously positive culture. Samples should be collected from peripheral vessels. 1)Apply a tourniquet and identify the blood vessel. 2)Wash the skin with soap and water if it is visibly unclean and wipe dry. 3)Clean the area vigorously with 70% alcohol starting at the intended site of puncture and going outward in concentric circles. 4)Apply 10% povidone iodine over the area of intended puncture. 5)Allow the skin to dry. 6)Remove the caps off blood culture bottles and wipe the top of the vials with an alcohol swab. Allow this to dry. 7)For other vessels other than commercial blood culture bottles, wipe off the tops with alcohol and allow them to dry prior to use. 8)With a sterile needle, collect the sample: Paediatric 2 - 5 mls Neonates 1 - 3 mls 9)Distribute blood evenly into the aerobic and anaerobic blood culture bottles for adults. For paediatric patients, place all the blood into the automated paediatric blood culture bottles that are specifically designed for smaller amounts of blood. 10)If the vessel must be palpated again, the disinfection of the skin must be repeated prior to collection. 11)Place a gauze pad / cotton swab over the venipuncture site, applying mild pressure. Check bleeding has ceased and apply an adhesive or gauze bandage over the site. 12)Label the bottles with the patient s names, age and collection details (Date and time). Be careful not to write or cover the commercial bottles bar codes. 13)Ensure appropriate disposal of waste.
Reported turnaround: After Five Days
Report date: 5-Days
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 3690.0

name: MRD T-Lymphoblastic Leukemia (T-ALL) by Multiparametric Flow Cytometry
text:
Test code: 1056
Test name: MRD T-Lymphoblastic Leukemia (T-ALL) by Multiparametric Flow Cytometry
Also known as: T-ALL MRD by Flow Cytometry; Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) T-ALL; Measurable Residual Disease (MRD) T-ALL;Residual T-ALL Detection by Flow Cytometry; Post-treatment T-ALL Flow Cytometry; Leukemia MRD Panel T-ALL;
Specimen: Bone Marrow Aspirate
Description: T-Lymphoblastic Leukemia / Lymphoma Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) by Multiparametric Flow Cytometry is a high-sensitivity assay used for detection and quantification of residual leukemic T-lymphoblasts following therapy in patients with T-acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (T-ALL/LBL). The assay utilizes advanced multicolor flow cytometry to identify aberrant leukemia-associated immunophenotypes (LAIP) and/or abnormal immature T-cell populations that differ from normal thymic or regenerating T-cell precursors using both leukemia-associated and different-from-normal analytical approaches. This test is primarily performed for post-induction, consolidation, maintenance, relapse assessment, and treatment response monitoring in T-ALL. MRD status is a major independent prognostic marker and is widely used for risk stratification, evaluation of therapeutic response, transplant decision-making, and relapse prediction. Analytical sensitivity typically ranges from 10^4m to 10^5 depending on specimen quality, cellularity, and assay design. Fresh bone marrow aspirate is the preferred specimen. Concurrent review of prior diagnostic immunophenotyping and treatment history is strongly recommended for accurate interpretation

name: Prenatal Sickle Cell Mutation Test - Amniotic Fluid
text:
Test code: 4501
Test name: Prenatal Sickle Cell Mutation Test - Amniotic Fluid
Also known as: Sickle Cell Anemia Mutation Prenatal Diagnosis; Sickle Cell Disease Intrauterine Screen
Specimen: Amniotic Fluid
Collection instructions: Amniotic Fluid in a sterile screw cap tube (~20 ml). Sample should be transported preferably at 2-8 degrees /refrigerated
Description: This test provides definitive prenatal diagnosis of sickle cell disease through DNA-based analysis of the HBB (ß-globin) gene performed on amniotic fluid obtained at approximately 15-16 weeks gestation. The assay targets the HbS mutation (Glu6Val; c.20A>T) and determines the fetal genotype as AA (normal), AS (carrier), or SS (affected). Testing is performed using validated PCR-based methods and/or sequencing, with high analytical sensitivity and specificity (>99%). This test is diagnostic (not screening) and is primarily indicated in pregnancies where both parents are known carriers (HbAS) or where there is a family history of sickle cell disease. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with parental genotypes and clinical context. Testing is performed through an accredited partner reference laboratory, as this is a specialized assay not currently offered in-house. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 21990.0

text:

name: Pan-TRK (NTRK1/2/3) Immunohistochemistry (Clone EPR17341)
text:
Test code: 5257
Test name: Pan-TRK (NTRK1/2/3) Immunohistochemistry (Clone EPR17341)
Also known as: Pan-TRK (Clone EPR17341) IHC
Specimen: BLOCKS
Collection instructions: For Pan-TRK (NTRK1/2/3) Immunohistochemistry (Clone Epr17341), submit representative tissue in approved fixative, or the specified paraffin block and slides. Label the anatomical site and provide relevant clinical, imaging, and previous pathology information. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: Pan-TRK immunohistochemistry using the EPR17341 detects expression of TRK proteins (TRKA, TRKB, TRKC) encoded by NTRK1, NTRK2, and NTRK3. It serves as a screening assay for tumors harboring oncogenic NTRK gene fusions, which are actionable alterations associated with response to targeted TRK inhibitors such as Larotrectinib and Entrectinib. The test is particularly useful in selected tumor types including secretory carcinomas, pediatric sarcomas, and other malignancies where NTRK fusions are enriched or therapeutically relevant. Interpretation is based on staining pattern and intensity (cytoplasmic and/or nuclear), and results should be correlated with tumor morphology and clinical context. While sensitive, Pan-TRK IHC is not specific for NTRK gene fusions, as physiologic TRK expression may be seen in neural and smooth muscle tissues. Therefore, positive or equivocal results require confirmatory molecular testing, preferably with RNA-based next-generation sequencing for definitive detection of NTRK fusions. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 9990.0

Interpret together with serum treponemal/nontreponemal tests, CSF cell count and protein, and the clinical presentation.

name: NTRK Gene Fusion Analysis by RNA-Based NGS
text:
Test code: 5268
Test name: NTRK Gene Fusion Analysis by RNA-Based NGS
Also known as: NTRK1/2/3 Fusion Panel RNA NGS); TRK Fusion NGS
Specimen: BLOCKS
Collection instructions: Submit representative tumour tissue (usually an FFPE block or approved alternative) with the histological diagnosis and estimated tumour content. Provide the clinical indication and any prior molecular or pathology results. Follow current laboratory or referral-laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: NTRK gene fusion analysis by RNA-based next-generation sequencing (NGS) is a high-sensitivity, definitive molecular assay for the detection of oncogenic fusions involving NTRK1, NTRK2, and NTRK3. These gene rearrangements result in constitutive activation of TRK signaling pathways and are actionable biomarkers predictive of response to targeted TRK inhibitors such as Larotrectinib and Entrectinib. RNA-based platforms are preferred as they directly detect expressed fusion transcripts, enabling identification of both known and novel fusion partners with high analytical sensitivity. This assay is indicated for patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors where identification of targetable alterations may impact therapeutic decision-making, particularly in tumors enriched for NTRK fusions or those negative for other common driver mutations. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with histopathological and clinical findings. In cases with prior positive Pan-TRK IHC screening, this test serves as confirmatory molecular validation, while a negative result effectively excludes clinically significant NTRK fusions within the assays detection limits. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Immunoglobulin IgG (Total IgG)
text:
Test code: 7361
Test name: Immunoglobulin IgG (Total IgG)
Also known as: IgG
Specimen: Serum,Lithium Heparin
Collection instructions: Arial; Allow specimen to clot completely at room temperature. Separate serum or plasma from cells ASAP or within 2 hours of collection. Transport aat 2-8 degrees celcius
Description: Arial; IgG is the most abundant immunoglobulin in plasma (70-75%) and plays a key role in long-term immunity through pathogen neutralization, complement activation, and opsonization. It is the only antibody class that crosses the placenta, providing passive immunity to the fetus and neonate. IgG is measured in serum, plasma, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and urine to aid in the diagnosis of infections, chronic inflammatory or autoimmune conditions (e.g., lupus, autoimmune hepatitis), immunodeficiencies, and monoclonal gammopathies such as multiple myeloma. In CSF, elevated IgG can reflect CNS infections or diseases like multiple sclerosis and may indicate intrathecal IgG production, especially when evaluated alongside albumin ratios or oligoclonal bands. In urine, IgG helps differentiate selective from unselective glomerular proteinuria and monitor kidney disease progression.
Reported turnaround: One Hour

Testing days: One Hour

name: Thyroglobulin (Tg) with Anti-Thyroglobulin Ab (TgAb)
text:
Test code: 7351
Test name: Thyroglobulin (Tg) with Anti-Thyroglobulin Ab (TgAb)
Also known as: TG
Description: Thyroglobulin (Tg) is a protein produced exclusively by thyroid follicular cells, both normal and malignant, and serves as a sensitive tumor marker for patients with differentiated thyroid cancer (papillary and follicular). Serum Tg levels are primarily used to monitor for residual, recurrent, or metastatic disease following total thyroidectomy and radioiodine ablation. However, its interpretation must always consider the presence of anti-thyroglobulin antibodies (TgAb), which can interfere with Tg measurement and lead to inaccurate results. Tg may also be detectable in benign thyroid conditions, such as multinodular goiter or thyroiditis, and is not useful as a diagnostic test for thyroid cancer in patients with an intact thyroid gland.
Tests included: Anti-thyroglobulin antibody, Thyroglobulin Levels (Serum)

name: HPV DNA PCR
text:
Test code: 4658 Test name: HPV DNA PCR Also known as: Human Papilloma Virus;Self Collection;Self Sampling Specimen: Swab Collection instructions:

Self collected swab

LBC sample

Description:

HPV is a viral infection that causes common skin and mucous membrane warts. Certain high-risk strains are known to progress cancer. It is now well-established that a persistent infection with a high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) genotype is the main cause of cervical cancer. It is possible to have an HPV infection without any cytologic abnormalities.

 

Checking for HR-HPV genotypes is a reliable and accurate primary screening tool for cervical cancer in women between 25 and 65 years without need for Pap smear while those under 25 years are recommended to have Pap smear. Detection of one or more high risk genotypes is associated with an increased risk of development of cervical cancer.

 

The HPV DNA PCR test at Dr. Kalebi Labs (DKL) has been performed using the FDA approved Cobas 5800 assay which automatically detects 14 HR - HPV genotypes (16, 18, 31, 33, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66 and 68) with individual typing of HPV 16 and HPV 18 simultaneously.

This test is not intended for women who have undergone full hysterectomy.

Tests included: HPV 16, HPV 18, HPV Other Reported turnaround: 1 Week Report date: 1-Week Testing days: Mon-Fri Standard price (KES): 6990.0

name: IA2 Antibodies (Insulinoma-Associated-2 Antibody)
text:
Test code: 9960
Test name: IA2 Antibodies (Insulinoma-Associated-2 Antibody)
Also known as: Insulinoma Antigen 2 Autoantibody; Islet Antigen-2 (IA-2)
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for IA2 Antibodies (Insulinoma-Associated-2 Antibody) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The Insulinoma-Associated-2 Antibody (IA-2 Ab) test is used to aid in diagnosing autoimmune Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM). IA-2 is a protein tyrosine phosphatase located in pancreatic ß-cell secretory granules, and the presence of antibodies against IA-2 indicates autoimmune destruction of ß-cells. IA-2 antibodies are typically found in individuals with new-onset T1DM and, like other diabetes-related autoantibodies, their detection helps distinguish T1DM from Type 2 or other non-autoimmune diabetes forms. A positive IA-2 antibody result supports a diagnosis of autoimmune T1DM, especially when combined with other autoantibodies such as GAD65, ZNT8, and insulin autoantibodies. Multiple positive antibodies increase diagnostic confidence and predict higher risk of progression in at-risk individuals. A negative IA-2 result does not exclude T1DM, as not all patients develop detectable levels of this antibody. Interpretation should always be integrated with clinical findings. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 8990.0

name: Creatine Kinase - Total
text:
Test code: 6814
Test name: Creatine Kinase - Total
Also known as: Creatine Kinase CK
Specimen: Serum
Description: Creatine kinase (CK) is a dimeric enzyme measured in serum or plasma to aid in the diagnosis of muscle injuries, myocardial infarction, and neuromuscular disorders. It exists as three cytosolic isoenzymes CK-MM (skeletal muscle), CK-MB (cardiac muscle), and CK-BB (brain) as well as a mitochondrial isoenzyme. CK levels rise significantly in skeletal muscle damage (e.g., rhabdomyolysis, Duchenne muscular dystrophy) and in cardiac injury, where levels increase within 4 hours of myocardial infarction, peak at 12 24 hours, and normalize within 3 4 days. Although troponins are now preferred for cardiac diagnostics due to greater specificity, CK remains valuable for evaluating chronic myopathies, statin-induced myotoxicity, and drug-related muscle effects. Monitoring CK is recommended before and during lipid-lowering therapy in patients with muscle-related symptoms.
Reported turnaround: One Hour

name: Ferritin - Inflammatory Marker
text:
Test code: 6834
Test name: Ferritin - Inflammatory Marker
Also known as: Ferritin
Specimen: Serum,Lithium Heparin
Description: Ferritin is a protein that stores iron and is primarily located in the liver, spleen, muscles, and bone marrow, with small amounts circulating in blood. Serum ferritin levels correlate with total body iron stores and are used to diagnose iron deficiency (e.g. iron deficiency anemia) and iron overload (e.g. hemochromatosis). A level below 15 \'ecg/L confirms iron deficiency, while elevated levels can indicate iron overload or act as an acute phase reactant in cases of inflammation, infection, liver or renal disease, and malignancy.

name: Toxoplasma Antibody Igg Avidity
text:
Test code: 6853
Test name: Toxoplasma Antibody Igg Avidity
Also known as: Toxo IgG Avidity
Specimen: Serum
Description: The Toxoplasma Antibody IgG Avidity test is used to help determine the timing of infection with Toxoplasma gondii, particularly in pregnant women. While standard IgG and IgM tests can indicate exposure, IgG avidity testing measures the strength of the IgG antibody binding to the antigen, which increases over time. A low avidity result suggests a recent infection (typically within the last 3-5 months), while high avidity indicates a past infection. This distinction is critical in assessing the risk of congenital toxoplasmosis and guiding further clinical management.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: DAILY

name: Liver Function Test (LFT) - Extended {x12 Paremeters}
text:
Test code: 6860
Test name: Liver Function Test (LFT) - Extended {x12 Paremeters}
Also known as: LFT Extended
Specimen: Serum
Description: Liver Function Test (LFT) - Extended (12 Parameters) with GLDH is a comprehensive liver assessment panel designed to provide an in-depth evaluation of liver function, hepatocellular integrity, and biliary system status. This extended panel includes ALT (Alanine Aminotransferase), AST (Aspartate Aminotransferase), ALP (Alkaline Phosphatase), GGT (Gamma Glutamyltransferase), Total Protein, Albumin, Bilirubin Profile (Total, Direct & Indirect), LDH (Serum), and GLDH (Glutamate Dehydrogenase), a highly specific marker of liver cell injury. The inclusion of GLDH enhances detection of acute hepatocellular damage, toxic injury, ischemic events, and severe inflammatory liver conditions, making this panel particularly useful for detailed clinical evaluation and monitoring of complex liver disorders. The test requires a serum sample and has an approximate turnaround time of 1 hour.

text:

Specimen: Serum
Description: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) is a spiral-shaped bacterium implicated in chronic gastritis, peptic ulcer disease, and has a known association with gastric carcinoma and MALT lymphoma. The H. pylori IgG antibody test detects immune response to past or ongoing infection and is useful in the initial screening and diagnosis of H. pylori exposure. While a positive result suggests current or prior infection, it does not distinguish between active and resolved infections. This test is especially helpful when non-invasive testing is preferred, or in settings where stool antigen or urea breath tests are not feasible.

name: HOMA-IR (Insulin Resistance Testing)
text:
Test code: 6894
Test name: HOMA-IR (Insulin Resistance Testing)
Also known as: HOMA-IR (Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance);Insulin resistance testing
Specimen: Serum,Plasma,Flouride
Collection instructions: Serum, Plasma (Fluoride) both required; Fast 8-12 hours. Collect Serum and Fluoride Plasma tubes at the same draw, both are required.
Description: HOMA-IR (Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance) is a calculated index derived from fasting plasma glucose and fasting insulin concentrations, used as a surrogate marker of insulin resistance. It reflects the balance between hepatic glucose output and pancreatic \'e2-cell insulin secretion under fasting steady-state conditions. Elevated HOMA-IR values indicate reduced insulin sensitivity, typically associated with compensatory hyperinsulinemia, and are commonly seen in obesity, metabolic syndrome, prediabetes, and related cardiometabolic disorders. Clinically, HOMA-IR provides a practical, non-invasive, and cost-effective method for assessing insulin resistance in routine laboratory practice. It is particularly useful for early detection of metabolic dysfunction in patients with normal glucose levels but underlying hyperinsulinemia. However, as a static model, it does not capture dynamic insulin responses and may be less reliable in advanced diabetes or conditions affecting \'e2-cell function. Results should therefore be interpreted in conjunction with clinical context, glycaemic indices (e.g., HbA1c), and other metabolic parameters such as lipid profile.
Tests included: Blood Glucose (Fasting), HOMA-% S, HOMA-IR, HOMA1-%B, Insulin (Fasting), QUICKI
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour
Standard price (KES): 3990.0

name: Herpes IGM-(HSV 1/2 IGM)
text:
Test code: 6932
Test name: Herpes IGM-(HSV 1/2 IGM)
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: A serum sample is required for analysis, collected in a plain tube or serum separator tube (SST). Blood should be allowed to clot completely and centrifuged promptly to separate serum. The specimen may be stored at room temperature (18-22\'b0C) for up to 8 hours or refrigerated at 2-8\'b0C for up to 7 days. For longer storage, serum should be frozen at ?20\'b0C and protected from repeated freeze-thaw cycles. Samples should be clear and free from significant haemolysis, lipaemia, or particulate matter, and should be brought to room temperature and mixed well prior to testing.
Description: The HSV 1/2 IgM assay is a chemiluminescent immunoassay (CLIA) used for the quantitative detection of IgM class antibodies against Herpes Simplex Virus types 1 and 2 in human serum or plasma. Detection of HSV IgM antibodies may indicate a recent or active infection and can support the diagnosis of primary HSV infection when interpreted alongside clinical findings and other laboratory tests.
Reported turnaround: Three Hours
Report date: 3-h
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 3390.0
