Wipe the vulva from front to back. ? Void without re-contaminating the urethral opening. ? Initial urine to be passed into toilet, the patient must interrupt the flow of urine. ? Then collect the midstream portion in a sterile container. ? Empty bladder into the toilet ? Male ? Clean the urethral opening with tap water and cotton wool. ? Void without re-contaminating the urethral opening. ? Initial urine to be passed into toilet the patient must interrupt the flow of urine. ? Then collect the midstream portion in a sterile container. ? Empty bladder into the toilet ? Infant urine collection ? Wash / disinfect hands and put on gloves ? Clean the area around the urethral opening with tap water. Dry the surrounding area and perineum with clean cotton wool swab. ? Expose the adhesive surface of the paediatric bag, by removing the paper packaging ? For males, the penis should be projected through the opening in the urine bag. ? For females, the opening of the urine bag is to be placed so as to cover the upper half of the genital area. ? Clean scissors with an alcohol swab (before and after cutting urine bag), allow to dry air before cutting the bag. ? When urine is obtained, remove the bag, cut off the corner of the bag and pour urine into a sterile urine container. Do not pour urine through the opening of the bag. ? Hold the specimen bottle on the outside without touching the rim. ? Catheter specimens ? Wash / disinfect hands and put on gloves. ? Clamp the tube with forceps / clamp below urine collection port. ? Wait for urine to collect in the tube. ? Clean urine collection port with alcohol swab. ? Collect at least 10ml urine from the port. ? Pour urine into the specimen bottle. ? Unclamp the tube. ? Do not collect urine from the urine bag. ? State source on requisition form i.e. catheter specimen

name: Allergy Panel - Full Adult Profile x54 Allergens
text:
Test code: 7102
Test name: Allergy Panel - Full Adult Profile x54 Allergens
Also known as: Atopy
Specimen: Serum
Description: The Allergy Panel - Full Profile (x54 Allergens) is a comprehensive Euroimmun immunoblot-based test designed to detect specific IgE antibodies against a wide range of food and inhalant allergens. It provides an in-depth sensitization profile, supporting accurate diagnosis and management of allergic conditions such as rhinitis, asthma, urticaria, eczema, and food-related hypersensitivity. This extensive panel includes animal danders (cat, dog, horse), house dust mites (Dermatophagoides farinae, Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus), moulds (Alternaria alternata, Aspergillus fumigatus, Cladosporium herbarum, Penicillium notatum), pollens from trees (alder, birch, cypress, hazel, oak), grasses (orchard grass, timothy grass, sweet vernal grass, cultivated rye), and weeds (mugwort, common ragweed, English plantain). It also covers a wide variety of food allergens, including cow s milk proteins (alpha-lactalbumin, beta-lactoglobulin, casein, bovine serum albumin), egg white and yolk, peanut, soybean, wheat and rye flour, rice, sesame, crab, shrimp/prawn, beef, mutton/lamb, apple, apricot, carrot, potato, tomato, kiwi, celery, almond, and hazelnut, along with venoms (honey bee and common wasp) and latex. By combining both food and respiratory allergens, this panel offers a holistic evaluation of allergic sensitization, enabling clinicians to identify triggers, assess cross-reactivity, and guide targeted allergy management or immunotherapy.
Tests included: Alder, Almond, Alpha-Lactalbumin , Alternaria alternata, Apple, Apricot, Aspergillus fumigatus, Baker's yeast, Beef, Beta-Lactoglobulin, Birch, Bovine serum albumin, Carrot, Casein, Cat, Celery, Cladosporium herbarum, Cockroach, German, Codfish, Common ragweed, Common wasp venom, Cow's milk, Crab, Cultivated rye, Cypress, Dermatophagoides farinae, Dermatophagoides pter., Dog, Egg white, Egg yolk, English plantain, Hazel, Hazelnut, Honey bee venom, Horse, House dust, Kiwi, Latex, Mugwort, Mutton/ Lamb, Oak, Orchard grass, Peanut, Penicillium notatum, Potato, Rice, Rye flour, Sesame, Shrimp/ Prawn, Soybean, Sweet vernal grass, Timothy grass, Tomato, Wheat flour

name: Autoimmune Myositis Panel (Basic) x7 Markers
text:
Test code: 7109
Test name: Autoimmune Myositis Panel (Basic) x7 Markers
Also known as: Fixed Euroimmune Profile
Description: The Autoimmune Myositis Panel (Basic) is a targeted immunoblot assay designed to detect seven clinically significant myositis-specific and myositis-associated autoantibodies associated with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs) and overlap connective tissue diseases. The panel includes antibodies against Jo-1, PL-7, PL-12, Mi-2\'e2, Ku, PM-Scl (PM), and Ro52, providing a focused serological assessment for patients with suspected polymyositis, dermatomyositis, anti-synthetase syndrome, overlap myositis, and connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease. Detection of these autoantibodies can support diagnosis, aid disease subclassification, and identify important clinical associations such as interstitial lung disease, characteristic cutaneous manifestations, and overlap syndromes involving systemic sclerosis and other autoimmune rheumatic diseases. Results should be interpreted alongside clinical findings, serum muscle enzyme levels, imaging studies, electromyography, and muscle biopsy findings where indicated, as autoantibody results alone are not diagnostic of inflammatory myopathy.
Tests included: Jo-1, Ku, Mi-2ß, PL-12, PL-7, PM, Ro-52

text:

Test name: Aldosterone Renin Ratio (ARR)
Also known as: Plasma Aldosterone- Direct renin ratio
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood),Serum
Collection instructions: • Aldosterone Renin ratio(ARR) samples are ideally collected in the morning after patients have been out of bed for at least 2 hours,usually after they have been seated for 5-15minutes. · Patients should have unrestricted dietary salt intake before testing and should be potassium-replete. · Where possible, cessation of all possible interfering drugs should be done at the discretion of the attending physician; substitute medications that have a minimal effect on the ARR may be considered. · Despite these recommendations, ARR can be confidently interpreted despite the effects of continuous medications or sub-optimal conditions therefore testing should NOT be delayed to achieve perfect pre-analytical or biological conditions. · Samples MUST be collected at the same time.
Description: Aldosterone renin ratio (ARR) is used in the evaluation of patients for Primary aldosteronism. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Renin
text:
Test code: 7004
Test name: Renin
Also known as: Direct renin Concentration
Specimen: EDTA (Plasma)
Description: Renin is an enzyme secreted by the kidneys that plays a vital role in the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS), which regulates blood pressure, electrolyte balance, and fluid volume. Measurement of renin levels is clinically important in the diagnosis and classification of hypertension, particularly in differentiating between primary and secondary causes. It is commonly ordered alongside aldosterone to evaluate conditions such as primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn s syndrome), renovascular hypertension, and adrenal tumors. Interpretation of renin should consider patient posture, sodium intake, and concurrent medications, as these can influence results.
Reported turnaround: Three Hours

Testing days: DAILY-0

name: Blood Culture Aerobic ID,C & S
text:
Test code: 7119
Test name: Blood Culture Aerobic ID,C & S
Specimen: Blood Culture
Collection instructions: Collection Instructions The optimal sample for blood culture is one of adequate amount and collected in a manner that prevents contamination of the sample by skin flora. As much as possible, blood should be collected prior to initiation of antibiotics, unless it is a follow-up sample for previously positive culture. Samples should be collected from peripheral vessels. 1)Apply a tourniquet and identify the blood vessel. 2)Wash the skin with soap and water if it is visibly unclean and wipe dry. 3)Clean the area vigorously with 70% alcohol starting at the intended site of puncture and going outward in concentric circles. 4)Apply 10% povidone iodine over the area of intended puncture. 5)Allow the skin to dry. 6)Remove the caps off blood culture bottles and wipe the top of the vials with an alcohol swab. Allow this to dry. 7)For other vessels other than commercial blood culture bottles, wipe off the tops with alcohol and allow them to dry prior to use. 8)With a sterile needle, collect the sample: Adult 8 - 10 mls 9)Distribute blood evenly into the aerobic and anaerobic blood culture bottles for adults. For paediatric patients, place all the blood into the automated paediatric blood culture bottles that are specifically designed for smaller amounts of blood. 10)If the vessel must be palpated again, the disinfection of the skin must be repeated prior to collection. 11)Place a gauze pad / cotton swab over the venipuncture site, applying mild pressure. Check bleeding has ceased and apply an adhesive or gauze bandage over the site. 12)Label the bottles with the patient s names, age and collection details (Date and time). Be careful not to write or cover the commercial bottles bar codes. 13)Ensure appropriate disposal of waste.
Description: Blood culture involves the aseptic collection of blood into a specialized aerobic culture bottle designed to support the growth of aerobic and facultative anaerobic microorganisms. The specimen is incubated in a continuous-monitoring automated blood culture system, such as the BACTEC blood culture system or BacT/ALERT system, which detects microbial growth based on metabolic activity. When growth is detected, a Gram stain is performed promptly, followed by organism identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) as clinically indicated. The minimum standard incubation period is 5 days (120 hours), which is sufficient to detect the vast majority of clinically significant bloodstream pathogens, most of which flag positive within the first 24-72 hours. Positive results are reported immediately upon detection of growth to facilitate timely targeted therapy. If no growth is detected, the culture is finalized and reported as No growth after 5 days of incubation. Extended incubation (up to 7-14 days) may be undertaken in specific clinical scenarios - such as suspected infections with fastidious organisms (e.g., HACEK group, Brucella) or certain fungal pathogens as per the laboratory protocol.
Reported turnaround: After One Week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 5390.0

name: Blood Culture Anaerobic ID,C & S
text:
Test code: 7121
Test name: Blood Culture Anaerobic ID,C & S
Specimen: Blood Culture
Collection instructions: Collection Instructions The optimal sample for blood culture is one of adequate amount and collected in a manner that prevents contamination of the sample by skin flora. As much as possible, blood should be collected prior to initiation of antibiotics, unless it is a follow-up sample for previously positive culture. Samples should be collected from peripheral vessels. 1)Apply a tourniquet and identify the blood vessel. 2)Wash the skin with soap and water if it is visibly unclean and wipe dry. 3)Clean the area vigorously with 70% alcohol starting at the intended site of puncture and going outward in concentric circles. 4)Apply 10% povidone iodine over the area of intended puncture. 5)Allow the skin to dry. 6)Remove the caps off blood culture bottles and wipe the top of the vials with an alcohol swab. Allow this to dry. 7)For other vessels other than commercial blood culture bottles, wipe off the tops with alcohol and allow them to dry prior to use. 8)With a sterile needle, collect the sample: Adult 8 - 10 mls 9)Distribute blood evenly into the aerobic and anaerobic blood culture bottles for adults. For paediatric patients, place all the blood into the automated paediatric blood culture bottles that are specifically designed for smaller amounts of blood. 10)If the vessel must be palpated again, the disinfection of the skin must be repeated prior to collection. 11)Place a gauze pad / cotton swab over the venipuncture site, applying mild pressure. Check bleeding has ceased and apply an adhesive or gauze bandage over the site. 12)Label the bottles with the patient s names, age and collection details (Date and time). Be careful not to write or cover the commercial bottles bar codes. 13)Ensure appropriate disposal of waste.

Description: Anti-nRNP antibodies target components of the U1 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (snRNP) complex involved in RNA splicing. These autoantibodies are frequently associated with mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD) and may also be seen in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), systemic sclerosis, and polymyositis. Detection of Anti-nRNP is useful in diagnosing and classifying connective tissue diseases, especially when clinical features overlap. In MCTD, high titers of Anti-U1 RNP are a defining serological hallmark and aid in distinguishing it from other autoimmune disorders. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: IGRA TB Quantiferon
text:
Test code: 7065
Test name: IGRA TB Quantiferon
Also known as: Interferon-Gamma Release Assay (IGRA); TB Gold Quantiferon DKL Mycobacterial / TB Tests
Specimen: Lithium Heparin
Collection instructions: Collect 8-10 mL of venous blood into two lithium heparin (green top) tubes. Use a recommended needle size of 21-23 gauge for collection, and avoid small-bore needles (e.g., 25G or smaller), butterfly sets with excessive suction, or difficult draws, as these increase the risk of hemolysis. Ensure a smooth venepuncture technique and avoid excessive tourniquet time or forceful aspiration. Immediately after collection, gently invert the tubes 8-10 times to mix; do not shake vigorously as this may cause hemolysis. The sample should be transported to the laboratory as soon as possible. During transport and storage, maintain the specimen at room temperature between 18-25degrees. Do not refrigerate or freeze the sample at any time.
Description: Interferon-Gamma Release Assay (IGRA) is a blood test used to detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection by measuring interferon-gamma release from T-cells in response to TB-specific antigens. It is unaffected by BCG vaccination, useful for diagnosing latent TB infection, and preferred in BCG-vaccinated individuals or where PPD/TST (Mantoux Test) is inconclusive. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Tests included: Concentration (T-N) , Concentration of Background Control culture tube (N), Concentration of Testing culture tube (T) , QUANTIFERON TB GOLD
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

Description: Cystine Quant (Urine) is a laboratory test used to measure the amount of cystine in a urine sample. name: Karyotyping - Peripheral Blood
text:
Test code: 7899
Test name: Karyotyping - Peripheral Blood
Also known as: Peripheral Blood for Karyotyping
Specimen: Sodium Heparin
Collection instructions: Collect 3-5 mL of peripheral blood into a sodium heparin (green top) tube, or a bone marrow aspirate where indicated, especially for hematological malignancies. Immediately after collection, gently invert the tube 8-10 times to mix; avoid vigorous shaking to prevent cell damage. Ensure the sample is properly labeled and free from clots. Transport the specimen to the laboratory as soon as possible while maintaining room temperature (18-25?C). Do not refrigerate or freeze the sample. The specimen should ideally be processed within 24 hours to ensure viable cells for culture and analysis.
Description: Karyotyping is a cytogenetic test used to evaluate the number and structure of chromosomes in a patients cells. It allows for the detection of chromosomal abnormalities such as aneuploidies, deletions, duplications, translocations, and other structural rearrangements. This test is commonly used in the evaluation of hematological malignancies, including conditions such as Chronic Myeloid Leukemia, as well as in cases of congenital abnormalities, infertility, and recurrent pregnancy loss. It provides a global view of the genome and is often used alongside more targeted techniques such as FISH for comprehensive analysis. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 3 Weeks
Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 12990.0

name: NGS EGFR Mutation Analysis on Tissue Biopsy
text:
Test code: 6655
Test name: NGS EGFR Mutation Analysis on Tissue Biopsy
Also known as: EGFR Mutation Test Tissue Biopsy; EGFR Test by NGS Next Generation Sequencing
Specimen: Block (FFPE),TISSUE
Collection instructions: Formalin-Fixed Paraffin-Embedded (FFPE) Tissue Block, or Tissue in Formalin which has presence of cancer cells.
Description: The EGFR gene mutation test detects presence of specific genetic mutations in non-small cell lung cancer tumor cells that are in turn useful in determining whether the cancer can be treated with EGFR-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as gefitinib and erlotinib. The EGFR mutations are commonly seen in lung adenocarcinomas, and less frequently in adenosquamous carcinoma but are extremely rare in squamous cell carcinoma. Some mutations in EGFR, such as the L858R mutation and exon 19 deletion, have been shown to be predictive of response to EGFR-directed tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) in patients with non-small cell lung cancer. Other EGFR mutations, such as T790M and exon 20 insertion, are associated with resistance to EGFR TKIs. For testing on tissue biopsy, histologic section of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue is examined by a pathologist to confirm presence of tumor then DNA is extracted analysis of the EGFR mutations. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 4 Weeks
Report date: 4-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 29990.0

name: NGS KRAS Mutation Analysis
text:
Test code: 7190
Test name: NGS KRAS Mutation Analysis
Also known as: KRAS mutation analysis by next-generation sequencing; Genetic Test NGS KRAS; KRAS NGS; KRAS Mutation – Colorectal Cancer; KRAS Mutation – Solid Tumour
Specimen: Biopsy,FFPE tumour tissue block
Collection instructions: Submit a representative FFPE tumour block containing adequate viable tumour or appropriately prepared unstained sections from the tumour block. A corresponding H&E-stained slide and histopathology report should be provided where available to support assessment of tumour adequacy and selection of the appropriate tumour-rich area for testing. Specimens with extensive necrosis, very low tumour cellularity, insufficient tissue or significantly degraded DNA may be unsuitable for analysis or may require repeat sampling.
Description: KRAS mutation analysis by next-generation sequencing (NGS) is a targeted molecular test for detection of clinically significant somatic variants in the KRAS gene from tumour tissue. KRAS is an important oncogenic driver in several solid tumours, particularly colorectal cancer, and mutation status may provide predictive and therapeutic information. In colorectal cancer, activating KRAS mutations are associated with lack of benefit from anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody therapy such as cetuximab and panitumumab. NGS provides broader sequence interrogation than conventional targeted PCR assays and may detect a wider spectrum of KRAS variants within the regions covered by the validated assay. Results should be interpreted together with the tumour type, histopathological findings and clinical context. A negative result indicates that no clinically relevant KRAS variant was detected within the analytical scope of the assay and does not exclude alterations outside the regions tested. Where comprehensive RAS or broader tumour profiling is required, extended KRAS/NRAS/HRAS/BRAF pathway testing or a multigene solid-tumour NGS panel may be more appropriate. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 4 Weeks
Report date: 4-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 29990.0

name: PDL-1 Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
text:
Test code: 7191
Test name: PDL-1 Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
Also known as: PDL1 IHC;
Collection instructions: FFPE block (formalin fixed paraffin embedded tissue block) containing tumour cells as confirmed from histopathological examination of the tissue specimen.
Description: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunohistochemistry test is used for identification of neoplasms expressing programmed cell death- ligand 1 (PD-L1). PD-L1 is an immune-related biomarker that can be expressed on the surface of many tissue types, including tumor cells. For certain types and stages of cancer, testing for PD-L1 expression may help to identify patients most likely to benefit from treatment with PD-1 inhibitors. Novel immunotherapies, known as immune checkpoint inhibitors, can interrupt signals generated by immune checkpoint proteins, such as PD-L1, and can enhance antitumor T-cell immunity. Several immune checkpoint inhibitors, including pembrolizumab, nivolumab, ipilimumab, and others, have been approved for a number of clinical indications and are being evaluated in multiple malignancies. The FDA divides PD-L1 immunohistochemistry (IHC) tests into two groups: companion diagnostic tests, which provide information that is essential for the safe and effective use of a drug (test results are required for drug use), and complementary or codiagnostic tests, which may be used in treatment selection but are not considered essential for use of the corresponding therapy (test results are NOT required for drug use)
Reported turnaround: After One Week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 11990.0

name: Fecal elastase
text:
Test code: 7967
Test name: Fecal elastase
Specimen: STOOL
Collection instructions: Submit the stool specimen required for faecal elastase testing according to the current referral-laboratory procedure. Label the specimen clearly and confirm current collection, stability and transport requirements before collection.
Description: Fecal elastase measures pancreatic elastase in stool as a non-invasive marker of pancreatic exocrine function. A reduced result may support pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, but interpretation should consider stool consistency, clinical findings and the assay's reference interval. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 13690.0

name: DNA profile per individual (x1 for Paternity)
text:
Test code: 7868
Test name: DNA profile per individual (x1 for Paternity)
Also known as: PaternityDNA test
Specimen: Swab
Collection instructions: DNA Paternity Testing Specimen - Buccal Swab (Cotton Swab) or dried blood spot on treated or untreated paper. Buccal Swab Specimen Collection Instructions 1. Prepare the Collection Kit: Ensure the kit contains sterile buccal swabs (minimum 2 per individual), labeled collection envelopes or tubes, gloves, and a consent form. 2. Label each envelope or tube clearly with the individual's full name, date of birth, and collection date. 3. Ensure Proper Identification: Verify and record the identity of each donor using a valid form of identification. 4. Complete the chain-of-custody form if required. 5. Pre-Collection Instructions: Do not eat, drink, smoke, chew gum, or brush teeth for at least 30 minutes prior to sample collection. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Ensure each sample is properly sealed and labeled. 9. Documentation: Complete and sign all required documentation, including consent and identification forms. Ensure accurate linkage of sample ID to the donor's identity. 10. Transport to Laboratory: Place all labeled envelopes, consent forms, and chain-of-custody documents in the collection kit or transport bag. Deliver to the laboratory under standard room temperature conditions. Avoid exposure to moisture or heat.
Reported turnaround: After Three Days
Report date: 3-Days
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 16390.0

text:

name: Candida albicans Detection by Real-Time PCR
text:
Test code: 7893
Test name: Candida albicans Detection by Real-Time PCR
Also known as: Candida albicans DNA Detection; Fungal PCR – Candida albicans
Specimen: Swab,Urethral Swab,Urine,Fluids,Tissue Biopsy,High Vaginal Swab (HVS)
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood or named specimen for Candida Albicans Detection by Real-Time PCR. Send with the clinical indication and any prior molecular results. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: This test qualitatively detects the presence of Candida albicans DNA using real-time Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR) methodology. Candida albicans is the commonest cause of Vulvovaginal Candidiasis and may also be associated with mucocutaneous, genitourinary, and invasive fungal infections depending on the clinical context. The assay offers rapid and highly sensitive molecular detection and may be particularly useful in patients with recurrent or persistent symptoms, equivocal microscopy/culture findings, prior antifungal exposure, or suspected low organism burden. Detection of Candida DNA should always be interpreted alongside the patients clinical presentation, as asymptomatic colonization may occur, especially in genital specimens. Negative results do not entirely exclude fungal infection where organism burden is below the assay detection threshold or sampling is suboptimal. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 1 week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 11990.0

name: TB PCR (Tissue Block)
text:
Test code: 1001
Test name: TB PCR (Tissue Block)
Also known as: PCR for TB; (Tissue Block)
Collection instructions: Submit the tissue block/specimen required for TB PCR (Tissue Block), clearly labelled with the tissue site and relevant clinical information. Confirm current referral-laboratory acceptance and processing requirements.
Description: The TB PCR with INH and RIF Sensitivity (Molecular Drug Resistance Testing) assay detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) DNA in tissue and simultaneously screens for common mutations associated with resistance to Rifampicin (RIF) and Isoniazid (INH)-the two most important first-line anti-TB drugs. It provides rapid results that can guide early treatment decisions, particularly in settings where multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) is a concern. However, molecular assays detect only the most frequent resistance-conferring mutations, so phenotypic culture-based drug susceptibility testing remains essential to confirm results and identify resistance to other drugs. A negative PCR does not exclude TB, and results must be interpreted alongside histology, culture, and clinical findings. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: DNA Paternity Test x2 (Father & Child)
text:
Test code: 7991
Test name: DNA Paternity Test x2 (Father & Child)
Also known as: Paternity Test; DNA test (Father and Child)
Specimen: Swab
Collection instructions: DNA Paternity Testing Specimen - Buccal Swab (Cotton Swab) or dried blood spot on treated or untreated paper. Buccal Swab Specimen Collection Instructions 1. Prepare the Collection Kit: Ensure the kit contains sterile buccal swabs (minimum 2 per individual), labeled collection envelopes or tubes, gloves, and a consent form. 2. Label each envelope or tube clearly with the individual's full name, date of birth, and collection date. 3. Ensure Proper Identification: Verify and record the identity of each donor using a valid form of identification. 4. Complete the chain-of-custody form if required. 5. Pre-Collection Instructions: Do not eat, drink, smoke, chew gum, or brush teeth for at least 30 minutes prior to sample collection. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Ensure each sample is properly sealed and labeled. 9. Documentation: Complete and sign all required documentation, including consent and identification forms. Ensure accurate linkage of sample ID to the donor's identity. 10. Transport to Laboratory: Place all labeled envelopes, consent forms, and chain-of-custody documents in the collection kit or transport bag. Deliver to the laboratory under standard room temperature conditions. Avoid exposure to moisture or heat.
Description: The DNA Paternity Testing Autosomal STR (Fragment Analysis) uses deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) to accurately determine whether there is a biological relationship between a child and a man (alleged father). The DNA Paternity Test may be done for legal reasons usually following a court order or legal discussions with lawyers, or it can also be done for peace-of-mind where the parties concerned wish to confirm the paternity of a child in relation to the man in question. At DKL it is a requirement to follow strict chain of custody and proper documentation with consent of the relevant parties when collecting the samples for DNA Paternity Test so that the test process and test results are accurate and able to wisthstand scrutiny.
Reported turnaround: After Three Days
Report date: 3-Days
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 31990.0

Description: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) is a molecule that carries our genetic code and is unique to each of us. Almost every cell in the body contains a complete set of DNA that is inherited from our biological parents. A person gets half of their DNA from their mother and half from their father. Paternity testing compares DNA from different individuals to find out if they are biologically related. The most common reason for paternity testing is to identify a child s biological father. A complete paternity test must test samples from the alleged father, the mother and the child. By testing the mother, we can see which half of the DNA she contributed to the child. Once this is determined, the remaining DNA contribution (other half) is only compared to the alleged father s DNA.

name: Gut Microbiome Analysis
text:
Test code: 8892
Test name: Gut Microbiome Analysis
Also known as: Gut Microbiome Profile; Gut Microbiota Analysis; Gut Flora Analysis; Gut Dysbiosis Profile
Specimen: STOOL
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Gut Microbiome Analysis and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The Gut Microbiome Analysis is an advanced molecular stool test designed to characterize the composition and diversity of microorganisms inhabiting the gastrointestinal tract, collectively referred to as the gut microbiome. Using next-generation sequencing (NGS) and/or targeted microbial genomic analysis, the test evaluates the relative abundance of key bacterial taxa and commensal microbial populations, providing insights into microbial balance (eubiosis), dysbiosis, microbial diversity, and selected gut ecosystem patterns associated with gastrointestinal and systemic health. This assay may assist in the evaluation of conditions associated with altered gut microbiota, including chronic gastrointestinal symptoms, irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), post-antibiotic dysbiosis, metabolic disorders, immune dysregulation, and selected nutrition or wellness assessments. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings, dietary factors, medications (especially antibiotics and probiotics), and other laboratory investigations. This test is not intended as a standalone diagnostic assay for infectious gastroenteritis or specific gastrointestinal diseases. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 5 Weeks
Report date: 5-w
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 32990.0

name: Filaria Antigen
text:
Test code: 9906
Test name: Filaria Antigen
Also known as: Circulating Filarial Antigen (CFA); Wuchereria bancrofti Antigen; Lymphatic Filariasis Antigen
Specimen: Whole Blood
Collection instructions: Collect blood at any time of day. Unlike microfilaria microscopy, nocturnal collection is not required, because circulating filarial antigen does not show the same clinically important periodicity as circulating microfilariae. Where possible, document relevant travel/residence history, previous antifilarial treatment and clinical suspicion of lymphatic filariasis.
Description: Detection of circulating filarial antigen for investigation of lymphatic filariasis due principally to Wuchereria bancrofti. Antigen testing detects products of adult filarial worms and may therefore identify infection even when peripheral microfilariae are absent or below the detection threshold of microscopy. W. bancrofti causes approximately 90% of lymphatic filariasis worldwide. This test is not a general screen for all filarial infections. Standard circulating filarial antigen assays are primarily directed at W. bancrofti and should not be relied upon to diagnose Brugia malayi, Brugia timori, Loa loa, Onchocerca volvulus or Mansonella infections. Microscopy and/or species-appropriate serological or molecular testing should be considered where these infections are suspected. A positive antigen result supports current or recent W. bancrofti infection, although antigen may persist after treatment or loss of reproductive adult worms. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 3990.0

name: Filaria Antibody
text:
Test code: 9907
Test name: Filaria Antibody
Also known as: Filarial Antibody Test; Filaria IgG Antibody; Filarial Serology
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect 2?3 mL blood in a plain or serum separator tube. No specific time-of-day collection is required. Where possible, provide relevant travel or residence history, suspected filarial species, clinical presentation and previous antifilarial treatment, as these materially affect interpretation.
Description: Serological detection of antibodies to filarial parasites, used as supportive evidence of exposure or infection in patients with suspected filariasis. Depending on the assay, antibodies may be detected in infections caused by filarial nematodes such as Wuchereria bancrofti, Brugia spp., Loa loa, Onchocerca volvulus and Mansonella spp. The exact species coverage and degree of cross-reactivity depend on the antigen composition of the assay. A positive antibody result indicates exposure to filarial antigens but does not reliably distinguish active from past infection, and antibodies may persist after successful treatment. Cross-reactivity between different filarial species and, with some assays, other helminths may occur. A negative result does not completely exclude infection, particularly in early disease or immunologically hyporesponsive patients. Results should therefore be interpreted with clinical and epidemiological findings and, where appropriate, microfilaria microscopy, circulating filarial antigen testing and/or molecular testing. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 4190.0

Test code: 9910 Test name: DU Test (Weak D / RhD Variant) Also known as: Weak D antigen test;RhD weak expression test Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood) Description:

The Du test (Weak D test) detects weak or partial expression of the RhD antigen using the indirect antiglobulin method. It is primarily used in RhD typing of blood donors, pregnant women, and transfusion candidates. Donors with weak D are classified as RhD positive, while recipients and pregnant women may be managed as RhD negative to prevent alloimmunization. name: Histopathology Kidney biopsy with Direct Immunofluorescence
text:
Test code: 9915
Test name: Histopathology Kidney biopsy with Direct Immunofluorescence
Also known as: Renal biopsy with Direct Immunofluorescence
Collection instructions: Submit Kidney biopsy specimen in formalin (for light microscopy) and buffered normal saline / transport media (for immunofluorescence). Separate biopsy core in glutaraldehyde / EM fixative is advised for electron microscopy (EM) in the event EM is required as additional test.
Description: Medical kidney biopsy with direct immunofluorescence combines light-microscopic assessment of glomerular, tubulointerstitial and vascular pathology with direct immunofluorescence for tissue-bound immunoglobulins, complement and/or light chains as appropriate. The combined findings support classification of immune-complex, pauci-immune, anti-GBM, monoclonal-deposition and other renal diseases; electron microscopy may still be required for complete assessment. Turnaround time depends on specimen adequacy and whether additional stains, immunohistochemistry, electron microscopy or clinical correlation are required. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 21990.0

name: BRAF PCR
text:
Test code: 7291
Test name: BRAF PCR
Also known as: PCR for BRAF
Specimen: TISSUE
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood or named specimen for BRAF PCR. Send with the clinical indication and any prior molecular results. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: This test detects clinically significant BRAF gene mutations in DNA extracted from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor tissue using a validated PCR-based method. The assay is designed primarily to identify activating mutations in codon 600 (including V600E and related variants), which occur in a range of malignancies such as melanoma, colorectal carcinoma, papillary thyroid carcinoma, and selected brain and hematologic tumors. Detection of a BRAF mutation may support diagnosis and has important therapeutic implications, including eligibility for targeted BRAF inhibitor therapy in appropriate clinical settings. A negative result indicates that no detectable BRAF mutation within the regions covered by the assay was identified but does not exclude mutations outside the tested regions or the presence of other oncogenic drivers. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with histopathological and clinical findings, and additional molecular testing may be recommended where clinically indicated. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 15390.0

name: DNA Paternity Test x4 Individuals
text:
Test code: 7993
Test name: DNA Paternity Test x4 Individuals
Also known as: Paternity Test; DNA test (4 persons)DNA test (4 people)
Collection instructions: DNA Paternity Testing Specimen - Buccal Swab (Cotton Swab) or dried blood spot on treated or untreated paper. Buccal Swab Specimen Collection Instructions 1. Prepare the Collection Kit: Ensure the kit contains sterile buccal swabs (minimum 2 per individual), labeled collection envelopes or tubes, gloves, and a consent form. 2. Label each envelope or tube clearly with the individual's full name, date of birth, and collection date. 3. Ensure Proper Identification: Verify and record the identity of each donor using a valid form of identification. 4. Complete the chain-of-custody form if required. 5. Pre-Collection Instructions: Do not eat, drink, smoke, chew gum, or brush teeth for at least 30 minutes prior to sample collection. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Ensure each sample is properly sealed and labeled. 9. Documentation: Complete and sign all required documentation, including consent and identification forms. Ensure accurate linkage of sample ID to the donor's identity. 10. Transport to Laboratory: Place all labeled envelopes, consent forms, and chain-of-custody documents in the collection kit or transport bag. Deliver to the laboratory under standard room temperature conditions. Avoid exposure to moisture or heat.
Description: The DNA Paternity Testing Autosomal STR (Fragment Analysis) uses deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) to accurately determine whether there is a biological relationship between a child and a man (alleged father). The DNA Paternity Test may be done for legal reasons usually following a court order or legal discussions with lawyers, or it can also be done for peace-of-mind where the parties concerned wish to confirm the paternity of a child in relation to the man in question. At DKL it is a requirement to follow strict chain of custody and proper documentation with consent of the relevant parties when collecting the samples for DNA Paternity Test so that the test process and test results are accurate and able to wisthstand scrutiny.
Reported turnaround: After Three Days
Report date: 3-Days
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 62690.0

metadata.instructions: DNA Paternity Testing Specimen - Buccal Swab (Cotton Swab) or dried blood spot on treated or untreated paper. Buccal Swab Specimen Collection Instructions 1. Prepare the Collection Kit: Ensure the kit contains sterile buccal swabs (minimum 2 per individual), labeled collection envelopes or tubes, gloves, and a consent form. 2. Label each envelope or tube clearly with the individual's full name, date of birth, and collection date. 3. Ensure Proper Identification: Verify and record the identity of each donor using a valid form of identification. 4. Complete the chain-of-custody form if required. 5. Pre-Collection Instructions: Do not eat, drink, smoke, chew gum, or brush teeth for at least 30 minutes prior to sample collection. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Ensure each sample is properly sealed and labeled. 9. Documentation: Complete and sign all required documentation, including consent and identification forms. Ensure accurate linkage of sample ID to the donor's identity. 10. Transport to Laboratory: Place all labeled envelopes, consent forms, and chain-of-custody documents in the collection kit or transport bag. Deliver to the laboratory under standard room temperature conditions. Avoid exposure to moisture or heat.
metadata.description: The DNA Paternity Testing Autosomal STR (Fragment Analysis) uses deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) to accurately determine whether there is a biological relationship between a child and a man (alleged father). The DNA Paternity Test may be done for legal reasons usually following a court order or legal discussions with lawyers, or it can also be done for peace-of-mind where the parties concerned wish to confirm the paternity of a child in relation to the man in question. At DKL it is a requirement to follow strict chain of custody and proper documentation with consent of the relevant parties when collecting the samples for DNA Paternity Test so that the test process and test results are accurate and able to wisthstand scrutiny.

name: Endomysial Antibody IgG
text:

Test name: Endomysial Antibody IgG
Also known as: EMA ANTI-EMA Anti-Endomysial IgG
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Endomysial Antibody IgG and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.

name: Vet Blood Culture – Aerobic & Anaerobic
text:
Test code: 1985
Test name: Vet Blood Culture – Aerobic & Anaerobic
Also known as: Pediatric (Blood Culture)/ Pediatric bottle
Specimen: BLOOD
Description: This test involves the aseptic collection of blood into a specialized aerobic culture bottle designed to support the growth of aerobic and facultative anaerobic microorganisms. The specimen is incubated in a continuous-monitoring automated blood culture system, such as the BACTEC blood culture system or BacT/ALERT system, which detects microbial growth based on metabolic activity. When growth is detected, a Gram stain is performed promptly, followed by organism identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) as clinically indicated. The standard incubation period is 5 days (120 hours), which is sufficient to detect the vast majority of clinically significant bloodstream pathogens, most of which flag positive within the first 24 72 hours. Positive results are reported immediately upon detection of growth to facilitate timely targeted therapy. If no growth is detected, the culture is finalized and reported as No growth after 5 days of incubation. Extended incubation (up to 7 14 days) may be undertaken in specific clinical scenarios such as suspected infections with fastidious organisms (e.g., HACEK group, Brucella) or certain fungal pathogens based on clinician request or laboratory protocol.
Reported turnaround: After One Week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 8990.0

name: Von Willebrand Factor Antigen
text:
Test code: 8568
Test name: Von Willebrand Factor Antigen
Also known as: VWF Antigen; VWF:Ag
Specimen: Citrated
Collection instructions: • Collect the sample when the patient is not acutely ill or post-surgery, as inflammation or stress may affect levels. · Use a light blue-top tube containing 3.2% sodium citrate (Na citrate) as anticoagulant. · Ensure the tube is filled to the correct volume (9 parts blood to 1 part anticoagulant). · Avoid prolonged tourniquet application (not more than 1 minute) or traumatic draws(do not probe or use small needles) to prevent falsely elevated levels. · Immediately and gently invert the tube 4-6 times to mix blood with anticoagulant.Do not shake vigorously. · Transport to the laboratory within 4 hours of collection.Keep sample at room temperature (18-24?C). If submitting to the lab will take more than 4 hours, process as follows: - Centrifuge the citrated blood sample at room temperature for 15min to separate plasma. - Transfer supernatant plasma into a plastic, screw-cap vial(not glass). - Freeze immediately at -20?C (short term, up to 2 weeks)or -70?C or below (for longer storage or transport). - Ship frozen plasma on dry ice to the lab
Description: This assay quantitatively measures circulating von Willebrand factor antigen and is used to assess the amount of VWF present in plasma. It is indicated in the evaluation of unexplained mucocutaneous bleeding, suspected von Willebrand disease, and selected acquired bleeding disorders. The result should be interpreted in conjunction with VWF activity assays and clinical findings. VWF levels may be influenced by stress, inflammation, pregnancy, estrogen therapy, and blood group, particularly group O, which is associated with lower baseline VWF concentrations. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 11990.0

name: Oligoclonal Bands in CSF (CSF Only)
text:
Test code: 5112
Test name: Oligoclonal Bands in CSF (CSF Only)
Also known as: CSF IgG Band: Oligoclonal Band
Specimen: CSF
Collection instructions: Collect 2-3 mL of cerebrospinal fluid by lumbar puncture under strict aseptic conditions into a sterile, screw-capped, leak-proof container without additives. Avoid blood contamination, as it can compromise results, and transport the sample to the laboratory immediately at room temperature (do not refrigerate or freeze). Clearly label the container with the patients full details, date, and time of collection. Note: in some cases, a paired serum sample may be requested for comparative analysis; please confirm with the laboratory beforehand.
Description: CSF Oligoclonal Bands is used to detect presence of increased intrathecal synthesis of immunoglobulins, particularly IgG, which occurs in demyelinating diseases like Multiple sclerosis. Oligoclonal bands are present in 90% of patients with clinically diagnosed Multiple sclerosis. Oligoclonal bands are also seen in Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, Inflammatory polyneuropathy, CNS lupus & brain tumors. Simultaneous Isoelectric focusing of serum and CSF samples (IgG Index) helps to distinguish between the production of oligoclonal bands due to Peripheral gammopathy from that due to local production in the CNS. CSF Oligoclonal Bands IgG index (serum and CSF) is preferred to CSF Oligoclonal Bands IgG (CSF) alone. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 9990.0

text:

Also known as: MSI Microsatellite Instability / MMR Mixed Mach Repair Protein Immunhostochemistry
Specimen: TISSUE,BLOCKS,BLOCKS FOR REVIEW
Collection instructions: For MMR (mismatch repair) immunohistochemistry (IHC), the specimen typically required is formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue. This is usually obtained from a biopsy or surgical resection of the tumor, such as colorectal, endometrial, or other cancers where MMR status is relevant. The tissue must contain at least 15-30% tumor cells for analysis. This is checked by reviewing the original slide on which the diagnosis was made or reviewing a recut slide from the block.Please submit a copy of the initial histopathology report with the sample.
Description: MSI testing is often performed alongside or as a follow-up to MMR IHC to confirm MMR deficiency or guide treatment decisions (e.g., immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors). If both MMR IHC and MSI testing are planned, the same FFPE tumor sample can often be used, but labs may need multiple sections to ensure sufficient material. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Electron Microscopy Renal Biopsy (Specimen in EM Fixative)
text:
Test code: 9069
Test name: Electron Microscopy Renal Biopsy (Specimen in EM Fixative)
Also known as: Electron Microscopy (Specimen in EM Fixative)
Collection instructions: Submit Kidney biopsy in 3% Buffered Glutaraldehyde solution.
Description: Electron microscopy (EM) of renal biopsy is a specialised ultrastructural examination performed to evaluate the glomeruli, tubules, interstitium and blood vessels at very high magnification. It enables detailed assessment of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), podocyte foot processes, mesangium, endothelial cells, immune deposits and other ultrastructural features that are not detectable by routine light microscopy or immunofluorescence. EM is an essential component of the diagnostic work-up for many medical renal diseases, including minimal change disease, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), membranous nephropathy, hereditary nephropathies (e.g. Alport syndrome and thin basement membrane nephropathy), complement-mediated glomerulopathies and selected immune complex-mediated diseases. It is interpreted alongside clinical information, light microscopy and immunofluorescence findings to provide an integrated clinicopathological diagnosis. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 3 Weeks
Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 23990.0

text:

Also known as: Leishmania Antibody Test; Kala azar; RK39

Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: RK39, also known as the K39 antigen, is a recombinant antigen derived from a kinesin-related protein of Leishmania chagasi/infantum, used primarily in the serodiagnosis of visceral leishmaniasis (VL). It is widely employed in rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs), particularly in endemic regions such as South Asia, East Africa, and parts of Latin America. The test detects anti-Leishmania antibodies in blood or serum, offering a quick, user-friendly, and field-adaptable method with high sensitivity and specificity in regions like India and Nepal, though performance can be lower in East Africa due to strain variation. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Anti PLA2 Receptor Antibody (PLA2R)
text:
Test code: 7321
Test name: Anti PLA2 Receptor Antibody (PLA2R)
Also known as: PLA2 Receptor Antibody
Specimen: Serum
Description: Phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R) is a type 1 transmembrane receptor which is mainly expressed in the podocytes of the renal glomeruli. Autoantibodies against M-type PLA2R (Anti-PLA2R autoantibodies) are detected in around 70% of adult patients with primary membranous nephropathy (pMN), but not in patients with secondary forms of membranous nephropathy, other glomerulonephropathies or autoimmune diseases or in healthy blood donors. Anti-PLA2R autoantibodies are thus highly specific for pMN, of which pMN is the most frequent cause (around 20% of cases) of nephrotic syndrome in adults. The anti-PLA2R test at DKL is performed using chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA) method on Euroimmun platform.
Reported turnaround: Three Hours
Report date: 3-h
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 9990.0

name: IGRA TB Quantiferon (Urgent)
text:
Test code: 8992
Test name: IGRA TB Quantiferon (Urgent)
Also known as: Interferon-Gamma Release Assay (IGRA); TB Gold Quantiferon
Specimen: Lithium Heparin
Collection instructions: Collect 8-10 mL of venous blood into two lithium heparin (green top) tubes. Use a recommended needle size of 21-23 gauge for collection, and avoid small-bore needles (e.g., 25G or smaller), butterfly sets with excessive suction, or difficult draws, as these increase the risk of hemolysis. Ensure a smooth venepuncture technique and avoid excessive tourniquet time or forceful aspiration. Immediately after collection, gently invert the tubes 8-10 times to mix; do not shake vigorously as this may cause hemolysis. The sample should be transported to the laboratory as soon as possible. During transport and storage, maintain the specimen at room temperature between 18-25 degrees. Do not refrigerate or freeze the sample at any time.
Description: Interferon-Gamma Release Assay (IGRA) is a blood test used to detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection by measuring interferon-gamma release from T-cells in response to TB-specific antigens. It is unaffected by BCG vaccination, useful for diagnosing latent TB infection, and preferred in BCG-vaccinated individuals or where PPD/TST (Mantoux Test) is inconclusive. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 3 Days
Report date: 71-Hours
Testing days: After One Day
Standard price (KES): 18690.0

text:
Test code: 8778
Test name: Urine Culture, ID & Sensitivity + Automated Urinalysis
Also known as: Urine ID & CS + urinalysisUrine Culture, ID and Sensitivity + urinalysisCulture Urine, ID and Sensitivity + urinalysis
Specimen: Urine
Collection instructions: ? Female ? Thoroughly clean the urethral area with tap water and cotton wool. ? Wipe the vulva from front to back. ? Void without re-contaminating the urethral opening. ? Initial urine to be passed into toilet, the patient must interrupt the flow of urine. ? Then collect the midstream portion in a sterile container. ? Empty bladder into the toilet ? Male ? Clean the urethral opening with tap water and cotton wool. ? Void without re-contaminating the urethral opening. ? Initial urine to be passed into toilet the patient must interrupt the flow of urine. ? Then collect the midstream portion in a sterile container. ? Empty bladder into the toilet ? Infant urine collection ? Wash / disinfect hands and put on gloves ? Clean the area around the urethral opening with tap water. Dry the surrounding area and perineum with clean cotton wool swab. ? Expose the adhesive surface of the paediatric bag, by removing the paper packaging ? For males, the penis should be projected through the opening in the urine bag. ? For females, the opening of the urine bag is to be placed so as to cover the upper half of the genital area. ? Clean scissors with an alcohol swab (before and after cutting urine bag), allow to dry air before cutting the bag. ? When urine is obtained, remove the bag, cut off the corner of the bag and pour urine into a sterile urine container. Do not pour urine through the opening of the bag. ? Hold the specimen bottle on the outside without touching the rim. ? Catheter specimens ? Wash / disinfect hands and put on gloves. ? Clamp the tube with forceps / clamp below urine collection port. ? Wait for urine to collect in the tube. ? Clean urine collection port with alcohol swab. ? Collect at least 10ml urine from the port. ? Pour urine into the specimen bottle. ? Unclamp the tube. ? Do not collect urine from the urine bag. ? State source on requisition form i.e. catheter specimen

name: JAK2 Second-Line Testing Exon 12 Mutation Detection
text:
Test code: 4651
Test name: JAK2 Second-Line Testing Exon 12 Mutation Detection
Also known as: JAK2 Exon 12 Reflex Testing for Polycythemia Vera
Specimen: Whole Blood
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood or named specimen for JAK2 Second-Line Testing Exon 12 Mutation Detection. Send with the clinical indication and any prior molecular results. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: JAK2 exon 12 mutation analysis detects a group of less common activating variants in the JAK2 gene that are primarily associated with polycythemia vera (PV), particularly in cases where the more common JAK2 V617F mutation is not identified. These mutations are found in a small subset of patients with PV and are characteristically associated with isolated erythrocytosis, often with low serum erythropoietin levels. This test is recommended as a second-line investigation in patients with a strong clinical suspicion of PV who test negative for JAK2 V617F. A positive result supports the diagnosis of a clonal erythrocytosis consistent with PV and should be interpreted in the context of clinical findings, hematologic parameters, and bone marrow morphology. A negative result does not exclude PV or other myeloproliferative neoplasms; additional molecular testing (e.g., CALR, MPL) or further hematologic evaluation may be required depending on the clinical scenario. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After Three Days
Report date: 3-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 21990.0

text:
Test code: 5431

Also known as: Methylmalonic Acid Qualitative
Specimen: Urine
Collection instructions: Collect urine for Methylmalonic Acid Qualitative (Urine) in a clean, leak-proof laboratory container. Avoid contamination with faeces or toilet water. name: Catecholamines (Plasma)
text:
Test code: 7659
Test name: Catecholamines (Plasma)
Also known as: Catecholamines
Specimen: Plasma
Collection instructions: Patient Preparation Patient should ideally fast for 8 to 12 hours prior to sample collection (water allowed). Avoid caffeine, nicotine, alcohol, strenuous exercise, and emotional stress for at least 24 hours before sampling, as these may falsely elevate catecholamine levels. If clinically feasible and under physician guidance, medications that may interfere with catecholamine levels (e.g. sympathomimetics, decongestants, tricyclic antidepressants, levodopa, amphetamines, beta blockers) should be reviewed prior to testing. Patient should rest quietly in a supine position for at least 20-30 minutes before blood collection. Sample Requirements Specimen: EDTA plasma Collection tube should be placed immediately on ice after collection. Sample must be transported rapidly under cold conditions and plasma separated promptly. Frozen plasma preferred for referral transport.
Description: Plasma Catecholamines is a specialized biochemical assay that quantitatively measures circulating catecholamines including epinephrine (adrenaline), norepinephrine (noradrenaline), and dopamine in plasma. These hormones are produced by the adrenal medulla and sympathetic nervous system and play a central role in cardiovascular and neuroendocrine regulation. The test is primarily used in the evaluation of suspected pheochromocytoma, paraganglioma, neuroblastoma, autonomic dysfunction, and catecholamine-secreting tumors. Because catecholamine levels are highly sensitive to physiological stress, posture, medications, exercise, and dietary factors, strict patient preparation and specimen handling requirements are critical to minimize false elevations and ensure accurate interpretation. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Tests included: Epinephrine, Norepinephrine
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 16690.0

name: Varicella Zoster Virus (Chicken Pox) IgM CSF
text:
Test code: 7645
Test name: Varicella Zoster Virus (Chicken Pox) IgM CSF
Also known as: Varicella Zoster Virus (Chicken Pox) IgM Abs CSF
Specimen: CSF
Description: The VZV IgM test in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) detects IgM antibodies specific to Varicella Zoster Virus, the causative agent of chickenpox and shingles. Detection of VZV IgM in CSF is indicative of a recent or active central nervous system (CNS) infection, such as VZV encephalitis, meningitis, or myelitis. It is particularly useful in immunocompromised patients or in cases where typical rash is absent. This test assists in confirming CNS involvement in suspected VZV reactivation or primary infection when supported by clinical symptoms and imaging findings.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: MON & THU
Standard price (KES): 3390.0

text:
Test code: 7646
Test name: Varicella Zoster Virus (Chicken Pox) IgG CSF
Also known as: Varicella Zoster Virus (Chicken Pox) IgG Abs CSF

Description: The VZV IgG test in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) detects IgG antibodies against Varicella Zoster Virus, the virus responsible for chickenpox (primary infection) and shingles (reactivation). When interpreted alongside serum IgG levels and IgM findings, this test helps evaluate recent or past exposure and possible viral reactivation affecting the CNS.

name: Copper (24hr Urine)
text:
Test code: 7327
Test name: Copper (24hr Urine)
Also known as: Copper
Specimen: Urine
Collection instructions: Collect a complete 24-hour urine: discard the first void at the start time, then collect every void until the same time the next day. Record start time, stop time, and total volume. Keep the collection as directed by the laboratory. If an aliquot is submitted, send the documented total volume with a well-mixed sample. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: Twenty-four-hour urine copper measures total urinary copper excretion and is used in the evaluation and monitoring of Wilson disease and selected disorders of copper metabolism. Results should be interpreted with ceruloplasmin, serum copper, liver findings and treatment status; contamination of the collection can cause falsely elevated values. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Microfilaria Blood Smear (Filarial Parasite Microscopy)
text:
Test code: 7423
Test name: Microfilaria Blood Smear (Filarial Parasite Microscopy)
Also known as: Microfilariae Blood Film; Microfilaria Thick and ThinBlood Smear; Filarial Parasite
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Submit 2 3 mL EDTA whole blood and document the collection time. Where clinically appropriate, collection should correspond to expected microfilarial periodicity: preferably night-time for suspected Wuchereria bancrofti or Brugia spp. and daytime for suspected Loa loa.
Description: Microscopic examination of stained thick and thin peripheral blood films for detection and morphological identification of circulating microfilariae. The test is used in the investigation of suspected blood-borne filarial infections, including lymphatic filariasis and loiasis. Microfilarial density may vary with the time of day; appropriate specimen timing improves diagnostic yield. A negative microscopy result does not exclude filarial infection, particularly with low-level microfilaraemia, suboptimal collection timing, or filarial species with predominantly tissue-based microfilariae.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour
Standard price (KES): 1390.0

name: NIPT S - Extended Panel (Trisomies + Aneuploidies)
text:
Test code: 7699
Test name: NIPT S - Extended Panel (Trisomies + Aneuploidies)
Also known as: Non-invasive Prenatal Test S
Specimen: Streck tube
Collection instructions: Whole Blood in Streck tube x1 (tube of 10 ml). Contact the laboratory to be supplied the Streck tubes upon request.
Description: NonInvasive Prenatal Testing (NIPT) is a screening test offered during pregnancy to see if the fetus is at risk for having a chromosomal disorder such as Downs syndrome (trisomy 21), Edwards Syndrome (trisomy 18) and Patau syndrome (trisomy 13) amongst others. Whole blood from the mother, which contains fragments of DNA from the fetus, can be collected as early as 10 weeks into the pregnancy, and is used to analyze for these specific congenital disorders. The most common sex chromosome conditions are Turner syndrome, Klinefelter syndrome, Triple X syndrome and XYY syndrome. NIPT S test screens for: Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Trisomy 18, Trisomy 13, Disorders affecting sex chromosomes (X and Y) and any disorders in other chromosomes. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 53990.0

Description: HER2 immunohistochemistry (IHC) evaluates overexpression of the HER2 (ERBB2) transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase on tumor cells, most commonly in breast and gastroesophageal adenocarcinomas. In normal tissue, HER2 expression is low to absent. In tumor samples, staining is assessed based on the intensity and completeness of membranous staining in viable tumor cells. A score of 0 or 1+ (faint or incomplete membranous staining) is considered negative, 2+ (weak to moderate complete membranous staining) is equivocal and typically warrants reflex testing by in situ hybridization (ISH), and 3+ (strong, complete circumferential membranous staining in >10% of tumor cells) is considered positive.
Reported turnaround: After Three Days
Report date: 3-Days
Testing days: DAILY

name: HRR (Homologus Recombinant Repair) Gene Panel
text:
Test code: 7192 Test name: HRR (Homologus Recombinant Repair) Gene Panel Also known as: HRR+ NGS; Genetic Testing Specimen: TISSUE Collection instructions:

Specimen required is FFPE (formalin fixed paraffin embedded) tissue block with cancer confirmed on histopathological exam

Description:

HRR (Homologous Recombination Repair) genetic testing plays an important role in the management of prostate cancer, particularly in men with metastatic disease. Mutations in HRR pathway genes such as BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, CHEK2, PALB2, and RAD51 occur in a significant proportion of patients and are clinically relevant for both treatment selection and prognosis. Current guidelines recommend HRR testing for all men with metastatic prostate cancer, ideally through both germline testing (blood or saliva, to detect inherited mutations) and somatic testing (tumor tissue or circulating tumor DNA, to detect acquired mutations).

 

Identifying HRR mutations has direct therapeutic implications, as these patients are more likely to benefit from PARP inhibitors (e.g., olaparib, rucaparib) and may also show increased sensitivity to platinum-based chemotherapy. Beyond guiding treatment, HRR testing provides prognostic information-particularly as BRCA2 mutations are associated with more aggressive disease-and informs family counseling when germline mutations are detected. Testing is typically performed using NGS-based multigene panels covering the relevant HRR genes.

 

This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Reported turnaround: 4 Weeks Report date: 4-Weeks Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU Standard price (KES): 54990.0

name: Cotinine/ Nicotine (Urine)- Quantitative
text:
Test code: 9914
Test name: Cotinine/ Nicotine (Urine)- Quantitative
Also known as: Nicotine; Cotinine
Specimen: Urine
Collection instructions: Collect urine for Cotinine/ Nicotine (Urine) in a clean, leak-proof laboratory container. Avoid contamination with faeces or toilet water. Follow any midstream, first-morning, or timed instruction on the request. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: This nicotine / cotinine test used immunoassay for the qualitative detection of nicotine, cotinine and drug metabolites in urine. This test can also detects other related compounds. The assay is a screening test and provides only a preliminary analytical test result. A more specific alternate chemical method must be used in order to obtain a confirmed analytical result if clinically warranted. Gas chromatography/ mass spectrometry (GC/MS) is recommended confirmatory method. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 1 week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 4390.0

name: Mycobacterial Culture (Tissue)
text:
Test code: 6533
Test name: Mycobacterial Culture (Tissue)
Also known as: TB Culture
Specimen: TISSUE
Collection instructions: Collect from the suspected site using aseptic technique, preferably before antimicrobials where clinically possible. State the source, collection time, and current antimicrobials. Submit promptly in the approved sterile container. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: Mycobacterial culture of tissue is used to recover Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and/or non-tuberculous mycobacteria, allowing species identification and further susceptibility testing where indicated. Culture is more sensitive than smear microscopy but may take days to weeks; results should be interpreted with molecular testing, microscopy and the clinical context. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Description: Newborn screening for inborn errors of metabolism on dried blood spot uses tandem mass spectrometry to assess amino-acid and acylcarnitine patterns associated with selected amino-acid, organic-acid and fatty-acid oxidation disorders. name: Low Dose - Dexamethasone suppression test (1 mg)
text:
Test code: 3245
Test name: Low Dose - Dexamethasone suppression test (1 mg)
Also known as: Overnight Dexamethasone suppression test
Collection instructions: Collect baseline cortisol sample between 6am and 9am. Give 1mg of Dexamethasone at Midnight and collect sample for cortisol level between 6am and 9am in the morning of the next morning (same day).
Description: The dexamethasone suppression test assesses adrenal gland function, particularly to diagnose Cushing's syndrome, by measuring how cortisol levels change in response to dexamethasone, a synthetic glucocorticoid. The test involves giving a dose of dexamethasone (either a single dose overnight or multiple doses over several days) and then measuring cortisol levels in the blood. For the low-dose dexamethasone suppression test, 1mg of Dexamethasone is taken orally by midnight (12am) then the sample is taken in the morning between 6am and 9am for cortisol measurement.
Tests included: Post-Dexamethasone Cortisol, Pre-Dexamethasone Cortisol (AM)
Reported turnaround: DAILY
Report date: 8-Hours
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 4390.0

name: Ammonia (NH3) {24hr Urine}
text:
Test code: 3254
Test name: Ammonia (NH3) {24hr Urine}
Also known as: AMMONIA; NH3
Specimen: 24 Hrs Urine
Collection instructions: Collect a complete 24-hour urine: discard the first void at the start time, then collect every void until the same time the next day. Record start time, stop time, and total volume. Keep the collection as directed by the laboratory. If an aliquot is submitted, send the documented total volume with a well-mixed sample. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: Twenty-four-hour urine ammonia (ammonium) measures renal ammonium excretion, a major component of net urinary acid excretion. It is useful in the evaluation of acid?base disorders, particularly metabolic acidosis and suspected renal tubular acidosis, and should be interpreted with serum electrolytes/bicarbonate, urine pH and renal function; this is distinct from plasma ammonia testing for hepatic or urea-cycle disorders. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Description: The referral laboratory validates the Thermo Fisher Oncomine Comprehensive Assay v3 on the Genexus System for liquid-biopsy next-generation sequencing of cell-free DNA/RNA, interrogating clinically relevant cancer biomarkers across 161 genes. name: TB PCR (MTB) with RIF/INH Sensitivity - Fluid
text:
Test code: 1153
Test name: TB PCR (MTB) with RIF/INH Sensitivity - Fluid
Also known as: Mycobacterium Tuberculosis PCR with Rifampicin and Isoniazid Sensitivity; Similar PCR to GeneXpert with additional sensitivity for INH in addition to RIF
Description: The TB PCR with INH and RIF Sensitivity (Molecular Drug Resistance Testing) assay detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) DNA in fluid and simultaneously screens for common mutations associated with resistance to Rifampicin (RIF) and Isoniazid (INH)-the two most important first-line anti-TB drugs. It provides rapid results that can guide early treatment decisions, particularly in settings where multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) is a concern. However, molecular assays detect only the most frequent resistance-conferring mutations, so phenotypic culture-based drug susceptibility testing remains essential to confirm results and identify resistance to other drugs. A negative PCR does not exclude TB, and results must be interpreted alongside histology, culture, and clinical findings.
Tests included: INH, MTB, RIF1, RIF2, RIF3
Reported turnaround: After Three Days
Report date: 3-Days
Testing days: 11Am & 5Pm
Standard price (KES): 7990.0

This test differentiates bone-derived ALP from liver and other isoenzymes, enabling accurate determination of the source of elevated total ALP. It is useful in the diagnosis and monitoring of metabolic bone disorders such as osteoporosis, osteomalacia, Paget disease, and bone involvement in malignancy, as well as in assessing treatment response. Elevated bone isoenzyme levels indicate increased osteoblastic activity and should be interpreted alongside clinical findings and related tests including total ALP, liver function tests, calcium, phosphate, and vitamin D. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
