name: CTX C-Terminal Telopeptide (Collagen Type 1C-Telopeptide)
text:
Test code: 3279
Test name: CTX C-Terminal Telopeptide (Collagen Type 1C-Telopeptide)
Also known as: C-Terminal Telopeptide (CTX) Test; C-telopeptide Test: Cross-Laps
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Test available on Plasma (EDTA purple top tube) only. Overnight fasting is mandatory prior to sample collection
Description: The C-terminal telopeptide (CTX) test measures type I collagen breakdown products to assess bone resorption, aiding in the evaluation of osteoporosis, metabolic bone diseases, or bone metastases, and monitoring antiresorptive therapy efficacy. Plasma CTX (preferred) uses a fasting morning blood sample (7-10 AM), offering higher precision (<15% variability) and is ideal for detailed assessment or research, with reference ranges for premenopausal women, postmenopausal women, and men. Urine CTX, collected from a second-morning void or 24-hour sample (normalized to creatinine), is non-invasive but less precise (23-48% variability), suitable for routine monitoring when blood draws are impractical. Elevated levels indicate increased bone resorption; a 25-40% decrease post-therapy suggests effective treatment. Blood CTX (EDTA plasma) is favored in clinic settings for its accuracy, with results interpreted alongside clinical history and other tests (e.g., DEXA, P1NP). This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks

Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: LDH - Pleural Fluid
text:
Test code: 3274
Test name: LDH - Pleural Fluid
Specimen: Fluids
Description: The LDH (lactate dehydrogenase) level in pleural fluid is a key laboratory test used to help determine the cause of a pleural effusion. It is primarily used as part of Light s criteria to differentiate between exudative and transudative effusions. Elevated pleural fluid LDH especially when the pleural fluid/serum LDH ratio is >0.6 or when the absolute LDH level exceeds two-thirds of the serum upper limit of normal suggests an exudative effusion, which is commonly associated with conditions such as infection, malignancy, or inflammatory diseases. Conversely, lower LDH levels in pleural fluid are more consistent with transudative effusions, which typically result from systemic conditions like heart failure, cirrhosis, or nephrotic syndrome. LDH is a marker of cell turnover and inflammation, so increased levels in pleural fluid indicate a higher degree of cellular activity or damage in the pleural space. The LDH test is often performed alongside measurements of total protein in both pleural fluid and serum to apply Light s criteria accurately.
Tests included: Pleural fluid LDH
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 790.0

text:

Description: CH50, or total hemolytic complement, is a blood test that measures the overall activity of the complement system, specifically the classical pathway, in the body. It assesses the ability of complement proteins to work together to lyse (destroy) sensitized erythrocytes (red blood cells). The CH50 test can be used to assess the effectiveness of treatments for conditions like lupus or other autoimmune disorders. Low CH50 levels may indicate a higher risk of certain infections, particularly those caused by encapsulated bacteria. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Description: Vitamin B7 blood test measures the level of biotin (vitamin B7) in the bloodstream. Biotin is a water-soluble B vitamin essential for various bodily functions, including metabolism of fats, carbohydrates, and proteins. It plays a role in maintaining healthy skin, hair, and nails. Biotin is naturally found in certain foods and can also be taken as a supplement. Biotin deficiency, while rare, can cause a range of symptoms including hair loss, skin rashes, and neurological problems. Description: A CSF antibody panel for investigation of suspected autoimmune encephalitis, particularly in patients presenting with subacute encephalopathy, seizures, psychiatric or behavioural disturbance, movement disorders, memory impairment, dysautonomia or other compatible neurological syndromes. name: DNA Maternity Test x2 (Mother & Child)
text:
Test code: 3468
Test name: DNA Maternity Test x2 (Mother & Child)
Also known as: Maternity Test; DNA test (Mother and Child)
Specimen: Swab,None
Collection instructions: DNA Paternity Testing Specimen - Buccal Swab (Cotton Swab) or dried blood spot on treated or untreated paper. Buccal Swab Specimen Collection Instructions 1. Prepare the Collection Kit: Ensure the kit contains sterile buccal swabs (minimum 2 per individual), labeled collection envelopes or tubes, gloves, and a consent form. 2. Label each envelope or tube clearly with the individual's full name, date of birth, and collection date. 3. Ensure Proper Identification: Verify and record the identity of each donor using a valid form of identification. 4. Complete the chain-of-custody form if required. 5. Pre-Collection Instructions: Do not eat, drink, smoke, chew gum, or brush teeth for at least 30 minutes prior to sample collection. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Ensure each sample is properly sealed and labeled. 9. Documentation: Complete and sign all required documentation, including consent and identification forms. Ensure accurate linkage of sample ID to the donor's identity. 10. Transport to Laboratory: Place all labeled envelopes, consent forms, and chain-of-custody documents in the collection kit or transport bag. Deliver to the laboratory under standard room temperature conditions. Avoid exposure to moisture or heat.
Description: The DNA Maternity Testing Autosomal STR (Fragment Analysis) uses deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) to accurately determine the biological relationship between a child and the mother. The DNA Maternity Test may be done for legal reasons usually following a court order or legal discussions with lawyers, immigration purposes. It can also be done where the maternity of a child is disputed. At DKL it is a requirement to follow strict chain of custody and proper documentation with consent of the relevant parties when collecting the samples for DNA Maternity Testing so that the test process and test results are accurate and able to wisthstand scrutiny.
Reported turnaround: 1-2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 32990.0

name: TB PCR (MTB) Qualitative -CSF
text:
Test code: 4786
Test name: TB PCR (MTB) Qualitative -CSF
Also known as: Mycobacterium Tuberculosis:TB PCR Cerebrospinal Fluid(CSF)
Description: The TB PCR with INH and RIF Sensitivity (Molecular Drug Resistance Testing) assay detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) DNA in CSF and simultaneously screens for common mutations associated with resistance to Rifampicin (RIF) and Isoniazid (INH)-the two most important first-line anti-TB drugs. It provides rapid results that can guide early treatment decisions, particularly in settings where multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) is a concern. However, molecular assays detect only the most frequent resistance-conferring mutations, so phenotypic culture-based drug susceptibility testing remains essential to confirm results and identify resistance to other drugs. A negative PCR does not exclude TB, and results must be interpreted alongside histology, culture, and clinical findings.
Reported turnaround: After Three Days
Report date: 3-Days
Testing days: 9am - 1pm - 5pm
Standard price (KES): 6690.0

name: Myoglobin, Urine
text:
Test code: 6800
Test name: Myoglobin, Urine
Also known as: Urine Myoglobin
Specimen: Urine
Collection instructions: Collect urine for Myoglobin, Urine in a clean, leak-proof laboratory container. Avoid contamination with faeces or toilet water. Follow any midstream, first-morning, or timed instruction on the request. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: Urine myoglobin is a test used to detect myoglobin released into the urine following skeletal muscle injury, most commonly in suspected rhabdomyolysis. It is performed on a fresh urine sample using an immunoassay method. Clinically, it is indicated in patients with dark urine, muscle injury, or unexplained acute kidney injury, especially when urine dipstick is positive for blood but microscopy shows few or no red blood cells. A positive result supports muscle breakdown and signals risk of myoglobin-induced acute kidney injury. Interpretation should be correlated with serum creatine kinase, myoglobin in blood and renal function. Because myoglobin is rapidly cleared and unstable, early sample collection and prompt analysis are essential to avoid false-negative results. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 1 week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 4390.0

name: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) Panel by FISH
text:
Test code: 6566
Test name: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) Panel by FISH
Also known as: CLL
Specimen: Heparin
Collection instructions: Collect 3?5 mL peripheral blood in a sodium-heparin tube. Bone marrow aspirate may be submitted where clinically indicated. Gently invert the tube 8?10 times immediately after collection; do not shake. Ensure the specimen is correctly labelled and free from clots. Keep at room temperature and transport promptly. Do not refrigerate or freeze unless the receiving laboratory instructs otherwise.
Description: The CLL FISH Panel is a molecular cytogenetic test used to detect common chromosomal abnormalities associated with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia. The test utilizes Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) to identify specific genetic alterations in interphase cells without the need for cell culture. This panel typically evaluates key abnormalities including deletions of 13q, 11q, and 17p, as well as trisomy 12. These genetic findings play an important role in diagnosis, prognosis, and risk stratification, and may guide treatment decisions. FISH analysis is highly sensitive and can detect abnormalities even when conventional cytogenetics is normal or when dividing cells are limited. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 40690.0

name: Varicella Zoster Antibodies CSF (IgG & IgM)
text:
Test code: 4587
Test name: Varicella Zoster Antibodies CSF (IgG & IgM)
Specimen: CSF
Description: This test detects both IgG and IgM antibodies to Varicella Zoster Virus (VZV) in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) to aid in the diagnosis of central nervous system (CNS) infections caused by VZV, such as encephalitis, meningitis, myelitis, or vasculopathy. Presence of IgM suggests a recent or active infection, while IgG, especially when found in higher levels than in serum or with evidence of intrathecal synthesis, supports ongoing or past infection with possible CNS involvement. This combined antibody profile is particularly useful in immunocompromised individuals and cases lacking classic rash presentation.
Tests included: Varicella Zoster Virus (Chicken Pox) IgM CSF , Varicella Zoster Virus (Chicken Pox) IgG CSF

name: Homocystinuria under New Born Screening for Inborn Error of Metabolism on Blood (DBS)
text:
Test code: 4571
Test name: Homocystinuria under New Born Screening for Inborn Error of Metabolism on Blood (DBS)
Also known as: Inborn Error of Metabolism by Tandem Mass Spectrometry (TMS) on Dry Blood Spot HCY
Specimen: Whole Blood

name: Complement Factor H Antibody Test (Anti CFH)
text:
Test code: 7249
Test name: Complement Factor H Antibody Test (Anti CFH)
Also known as: Anti-complement Factor H Antibody; Anti CFH autoantibodies detection
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: d- Preferred Sample Type: Serum - Collection: Use a serum separator tube (SST / gold top). Centrifuge at 1500 x g for 10-15 minutes. - Minimum volume: 2 mL of serum - Handling and Storage: Keep refrigerated at 2-8?C. - Transport: Refrigerated (cold pack) for shipping to reference lab Additional Notes: Do not use hemolyzed, lipemic, or icteric samples.
Description: The Anti-Complement Factor H (Anti-CFH) test is a blood test used to detect autoantibodies against complement factor H, a regulatory protein of the complement system. Anti-factor H autoantibodies are found in a subset of patients with atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS), a rare and severe disease characterized by microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury. The test helps in confirming the diagnosis and guiding treatment decisions (e.g. plasma exchange, eculizumab, immunosuppression). This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 15390.0

name: Chromosomal Microarray 750 K (Cytogenetics) Blood
text:
Test code: 8169
Test name: Chromosomal Microarray 750 K (Cytogenetics) Blood
Also known as: CMA Blood Chromosomal Microarray; High resolution Micro-array
Specimen: Hepranized,EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: 2-5 mL of EDTA whole blood
Description: Chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) is a high-resolution genomic test that detects copy number variations (CNVs), including submicroscopic deletions and duplications, across the genome. When performed on peripheral blood, CMA is commonly used in the evaluation of patients with developmental delay, intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorders, multiple congenital anomalies, and unexplained dysmorphic features. It may also be employed in the context of hematological malignancies to detect somatic chromosomal imbalances. Peripheral blood is the standard source for germline CMA testing. The test provides superior resolution compared to conventional karyotyping and can uncover clinically significant variants that are not visible by traditional cytogenetics. However, CMA does not detect balanced translocations, low-level mosaicism, or point mutations. Results must be interpreted in the context of clinical findings, family history, and other genetic studies. Incidental findings or variants of uncertain significance (VUS) may be identified, and appropriate pre- and post-test genetic counseling is recommended. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 32990.0

name: Extended Paternity Testing
text:
Test code: 8003
Test name: Extended Paternity Testing
Also known as: PaternityDNA test
Collection instructions: DNA Paternity Testing Specimen - Buccal Swab (Cotton Swab) or dried blood spot on treated or untreated paper. Buccal Swab Specimen Collection Instructions 1. Prepare the Collection Kit: Ensure the kit contains sterile buccal swabs (minimum 2 per individual), labeled collection envelopes or tubes, gloves, and a consent form. 2. Label each envelope or tube clearly with the individual's full name, date of birth, and collection date. 3. Ensure Proper Identification: Verify and record the identity of each donor using a valid form of identification. 4. Complete the chain-of-custody form if required. 5. Pre-Collection Instructions: Do not eat, drink, smoke, chew gum, or brush teeth for at least 30 minutes prior to sample collection. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Ensure each sample is properly sealed and labeled. 9. Documentation: Complete and sign all required documentation, including consent and identification forms. Ensure accurate linkage of sample ID to the donor's identity. 10. Transport to Laboratory: Place all labeled envelopes, consent forms, and chain-of-custody documents in the collection kit or transport bag. Deliver to the laboratory under standard room temperature conditions. Avoid exposure to moisture or heat.
Reported turnaround: 3 Days
Report date: 71-Hours
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 21990.0

name: TB PCR (Fresh Tissue in Saline)
text:
Test code: 1154
Test name: TB PCR (Fresh Tissue in Saline)
Also known as: TB PCR on Fresh Tissue in Saline
Specimen: BLOCKS FOR REVIEW
Description: The TB PCR with INH and RIF Sensitivity (Molecular Drug Resistance Testing) assay detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) DNA in tissue and simultaneously screens for common mutations associated with resistance to Rifampicin (RIF) and Isoniazid (INH)-the two most important first-line anti-TB drugs. It provides rapid results that can guide early treatment decisions, particularly in settings where multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) is a concern. However, molecular assays detect only the most frequent resistance-conferring mutations, so phenotypic culture-based drug susceptibility testing remains essential to confirm results and identify resistance to other drugs. A negative PCR does not exclude TB, and results must be interpreted alongside histology, culture, and clinical findings.
Reported turnaround: After One Week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 7690.0

name: Genetic Test NGS Lung Cancer Panel Liquid Biopsy x50 Markers
text:
Test code: 7805
Test name: Genetic Test NGS Lung Cancer Panel Liquid Biopsy x50 Markers
Also known as: Genetic Testing Lung Cancer Fusion Panel; Genetic Test NGS Lung Cancer Panel x50 Genes
Specimen: Streck tube
Collection instructions: Whole Blood in Streck tube x2 (two tubes of 10 ml each). Contact the laboratory to be supplied the Streck tubes upon request.
Description: The Oncomine Precision Assay is a validated liquid-biopsy next-generation sequencing panel that interrogates 50 cancer-related genes (78 variants) in circulating cell-free/tumour-derived nucleic acids. name: Kinship Studies x3 Individuals
text:
Test code: 7859
Test name: Kinship Studies x3 Individuals
Specimen: Swab
Collection instructions: DNA Kinship Testing Specimen - Buccal Swab (Cotton Swab) or dried blood spot on treated or untreated paper. Buccal Swab Specimen Collection Instructions 1. Prepare the Collection Kit: Ensure the kit contains sterile buccal swabs (minimum 2 per individual), labeled collection envelopes or tubes, gloves, and a consent form. 2. Label each envelope or tube clearly with the individual's full name, date of birth, and collection date. 3. Ensure Proper Identification: Verify and record the identity of each donor using a valid form of identification. 4. Complete the chain-of-custody form if required. 5. Pre-Collection Instructions: Do not eat, drink, smoke, chew gum, or brush teeth for at least 30 minutes prior to sample collection. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Ensure each sample is properly sealed and labeled. 9. Documentation: Complete and sign all required documentation, including consent and identification forms. Ensure accurate linkage of sample ID to the donor's identity. 10. Transport to Laboratory: Place all labeled envelopes, consent forms, and chain-of-custody documents in the collection kit or transport bag. Deliver to the laboratory under standard room temperature conditions. Avoid exposure to moisture or heat.
Description: The DNA Kinship Testing Autosomal STR (Fragment Analysis) uses deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) to accurately determine whether there is a biological relationship between two people. The DNA Kinship Test may be done for legal reasons usually following a court order or legal discussions with lawyers, or it can also be done for peace-of-mind where the parties concerned wish to confirm the their relationship. At DKL it is a requirement to follow strict chain of custody and proper documentation with consent of the relevant parties when collecting the samples for DNA Paternity Test so that the test process and test results are accurate and able to wisthstand scrutiny.

Report date: 71-Hours
Testing days: DAILY-0

name: ANCA (Anti Neutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibodies) By IFA
text:
Test code: 7253
Test name: ANCA (Anti Neutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibodies) By IFA
Also known as: ANCA by IFA
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for ANCA (Anti Neutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibodies) By IFA and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: ANCA by Indirect Immunofluorescence (IFA) is performed using ANCA-L Slides (ImmunoConcepts, USA). These specialized substrate slides contain human neutrophils with lymphocytes, stabilized and fixed directly onto the test wells. The inclusion of lymphocytes enables the detection of antinuclear antibody (ANA) interference, which is commonly encountered with conventional ethanol-fixed ANCA slides. The ANCA-L substrate helps identify such interference through lymphocyte staining patterns, thereby improving result interpretation. For samples showing ANA interference, confirmatory testing with PR3-ANCA and MPO-ANCA assays is recommended. In addition, MPO and PR3 testing is strongly advised for all ANCA-positive patients and is ideally performed on all samples submitted for ANCA testing. ANCA results should always be interpreted in conjunction with the patients clinical findings and other laboratory investigations. Clinical management and treatment decisions should not be based solely on ANCA results. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: JC virus (JCV) PCR Test {Blood}
text:
Test code: 8927
Test name: JC virus (JCV) PCR Test {Blood}
Also known as: JCV; PCR for JC virus (JCV); Test {Blood}
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood or named specimen for JC Virus (JCV) PCR Test \Blood\. Send with the clinical indication and any prior molecular results. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The JC virus (JCV) PCR test on blood is used in the evaluation of patients at risk for JC virus reactivation, particularly those who are immunocompromised due to advanced HIV, post-transplant immunosuppression, or treatment with monoclonal antibody therapies such as natalizumab or rituximab. The assay detects JCV DNA in plasma or whole blood using real-time PCR, providing high specificity and good sensitivity for monitoring systemic viral presence and risk of progression to central nervous system (CNS) disease. A positive result indicates active JC viremia and may support risk stratification for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) in the appropriate clinical context. However, detection in blood does not confirm CNS involvement, and correlation with neurological symptoms and imaging is essential. A negative result reduces but does not fully exclude the possibility of JC virus infection or PML, especially if clinical suspicion remains high. Follow-up testing or CSF analysis may still be warranted in such cases. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 13690.0

Description: The JC virus (JCV) PCR test on urine is primarily used to detect viral shedding in immunocompromised individuals, such as those with advanced HIV, transplant recipients, or patients receiving monoclonal antibody therapies (e.g., natalizumab, rituximab). The assay identifies JCV DNA in urine using real-time PCR, which offers high sensitivity for detecting latent or reactivated infection since the virus commonly reactivates in the kidneys before systemic spread. A positive result indicates urinary shedding of JCV and supports the presence of active or latent infection but does not, by itself, confirm central nervous system (CNS) disease or progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). A negative urine PCR reduces the likelihood of viral reactivation but does not completely rule it out, particularly in patients with ongoing risk factors. Results should always be interpreted in conjunction with blood or CSF testing, neurological assessment, and imaging where clinically indicated. name: Salivary Cortisol (Random)
text:
Test code: 7675
Test name: Salivary Cortisol (Random)
Also known as: Cortisol in Salivary
Specimen: Saliva
Collection instructions: Timing: Collect saliva at specific times depending on indication: late-night (23:00-24:00) for Cushing s screening, or morning/evening for diurnal rhythm assessment. Exact timing must be recorded on the sample. Preparation: Patients should avoid food, drinks (except water), smoking, chewing gum, or brushing teeth for at least 30 minutes before collection. Rinse mouth with water 10 minutes prior. Avoid gingival bleeding to prevent contamination. Collection: Use a salivette with a synthetic swab or direct drooling into the tube. For swabs, hold in the mouth for 1-2 minutes without chewing. Ensure a minimum of 0.5 mL saliva. Labelling and Storage: Label with patient ID, date, and collection time. Store samples at 2-8 \'b0C if delivered within 24 hours, otherwise freeze at -20 \'b0C. Repeated freeze-thaw cycles should be avoided. Transport: Send samples promptly to the lab, ideally within 24-48 hours, and keep cool during transport if delays occur.
Description: Salivary cortisol provides a convenient, non-invasive measure of free cortisol, reflecting the biologically active fraction that diffuses into saliva independent of salivary flow rate. It is particularly useful for assessing diurnal rhythm and late-night cortisol levels in the evaluation of suspected Cushing syndrome, as well as for monitoring adrenal suppression or insufficiency. The Roche Elecsys assay employs an electrochemiluminescence immunoassay (ECLIA) principle with high sensitivity and specificity for cortisol. It is validated for use on salivary samples, minimizing issues of cross-reactivity and interference seen in some earlier immunoassays. Pre-analytical handling remains critical-samples should be collected using synthetic swabs or direct expectoration, ideally at defined times (e.g., late-night 23:00-24:00 for Cushing s screening, or upon waking for diurnal rhythm studies), avoiding contamination from food, beverages, or dental products. Reference intervals are assay-specific and time-dependent. For late-night salivary cortisol, values below the assay cut-off reliably exclude hypercortisolism, whereas consistently elevated levels are highly suggestive and warrant confirmatory testing (e.g., dexamethasone suppression test, 24-hr urinary free cortisol). Interpretation should always be integrated with the clinical context, other biochemical investigations, and, if indicated, imaging findings.

Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour

name: Flow Cytometry Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) Panel (Bone Marrow) x20 Markers
text:
Test code: 8719
Test name: Flow Cytometry Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) Panel (Bone Marrow) x20 Markers
Also known as: ClearLLab Myeloid M1 and M2 Panels x20 markers
Specimen: Bone Marrow Aspirate
Collection instructions: Blood: 4-5ml of whole blood in EDTA and/or Heparin, to reach the lab in less than 6 - 12 hours from collection. Bone Marrow Aspirate: 3-4ml of bone marrow aspirate in EDTA and/or Heparin, to reach the lab in less than 6 - 12 hours from collection. Fluid: CSF, pleural fluid or peritoneal fluid in plain sterile container, to reach the lab in less than 6 - 12 hours from collection. FNA: Cytology aspirate material rinsed in saline/PBS, to reach the lab in less than 6 - 12 hours from collection.

Tests included: Flow Cytometry Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) Panel x20 Markers, Bone Marrow Aspirate (BMA) only Submitted Sample, FBC only (CBC / FHG / TBC)

name: HIAA Urine (5-Hydroxyindoleacetic Acid) 5-HIAA (Random Urine)
text:
Test code: 6273
Test name: HIAA Urine (5-Hydroxyindoleacetic Acid) 5-HIAA (Random Urine)
Also known as: 5HIAA 24-hour urine; HIAA
Specimen: Urine
Collection instructions: Sample Type: 50 mL (10 mL minimum) aliquot of random Urine. Add 50% HCl drop by drop to bring the pH between 1-2. Do not use concentrated HCL. Ship refrigerated at 2-8 degrees centigrade or frozen. Preparation for test: Patient should strictly avoid banana, kiwi, walnut, avocado, brinjal, pineapple, plum, tomato & drugs like Fluorouracil, Melphalan, Paracetamol & Acetaminophen, Heparin, L-dopa, Reserpine, Salicylates, Chlorpromazine, Imipramine, Isoniazid, MAO inhibitors, Phenothiazines, Promethazine, alcoholic beverages, caffeine, tea/coffee, tobacco and strenuous exercise at least 72 hrs before and during specimen collection.
Description: Random urine 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) measures the principal metabolite of serotonin and can support investigation of serotonin-secreting neuroendocrine tumours. A 24-hour urine collection is often preferred for diagnostic evaluation, and diet or medications may affect results.
Tests included: 5 Hiaa (5-Hydroxyindoleacetic Acid)
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks

name: DNA Paternity Test x7 Individuals
text:
Test code: 8346
Test name: DNA Paternity Test x7 Individuals
Also known as: Paternity Test; DNA test (7 persons)
Specimen: Swab
Collection instructions: DNA Paternity Testing Specimen - Buccal Swab (Cotton Swab) or dried blood spot on treated or untreated paper. Buccal Swab Specimen Collection Instructions 1. Prepare the Collection Kit: Ensure the kit contains sterile buccal swabs (minimum 2 per individual), labeled collection envelopes or tubes, gloves, and a consent form. 2. Label each envelope or tube clearly with the individual's full name, date of birth, and collection date. 3. Ensure Proper Identification: Verify and record the identity of each donor using a valid form of identification. 4. Complete the chain-of-custody form if required. 5. Pre-Collection Instructions: Do not eat, drink, smoke, chew gum, or brush teeth for at least 30 minutes prior to sample collection. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Ensure each sample is properly sealed and labeled. 9. Documentation: Complete and sign all required documentation, including consent and identification forms. Ensure accurate linkage of sample ID to the donor's identity. 10. Transport to Laboratory: Place all labeled envelopes, consent forms, and chain-of-custody documents in the collection kit or transport bag. Deliver to the laboratory under standard room temperature conditions. Avoid exposure to moisture or heat.
Description: The DNA Paternity Testing Autosomal STR (Fragment Analysis) uses deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) to accurately determine whether there is a biological relationship between a child and a man (alleged father). The DNA Paternity Test may be done for legal reasons usually following a court order or legal discussions with lawyers, or it can also be done for peace-of-mind where the parties concerned wish to confirm the paternity of a child in relation to the man in question. At DKL it is a requirement to follow strict chain of custody and proper documentation with consent of the relevant parties when collecting the samples for DNA Paternity Test so that the test process and test results are accurate and able to wisthstand scrutiny.
Reported turnaround: After Three Days
Report date: 3-Days
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 109990.0

name: Kinship Studies x8 Individuals
text:
Test code: 8815
Test name: Kinship Studies x8 Individuals
Specimen: Swab,EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: DNA Kinship Testing Specimen - Buccal Swab (Cotton Swab) or dried blood spot on treated or untreated paper. Buccal Swab Specimen Collection Instructions 1. Prepare the Collection Kit: Ensure the kit contains sterile buccal swabs (minimum 2 per individual), labeled collection envelopes or tubes, gloves, and a consent form. 2. Label each envelope or tube clearly with the individual's full name, date of birth, and collection date. 3. Ensure Proper Identification: Verify and record the identity of each donor using a valid form of identification. 4. Complete the chain-of-custody form if required. 5. Pre-Collection Instructions: Do not eat, drink, smoke, chew gum, or brush teeth for at least 30 minutes prior to sample collection. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Ensure each sample is properly sealed and labeled. 9. Documentation: Complete and sign all required documentation, including consent and identification forms. Ensure accurate linkage of sample ID to the donor's identity. 10. Transport to Laboratory: Place all labeled envelopes, consent forms, and chain-of-custody documents in the collection kit or transport bag. Deliver to the laboratory under standard room temperature conditions. Avoid exposure to moisture or heat.
Description: The DNA Kinship Testing Autosomal STR (Fragment Analysis) uses deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) to accurately determine whether there is a biological relationship between two people. The DNA Kinship Test may be done for legal reasons usually following a court order or legal discussions with lawyers, or it can also be done for peace-of-mind where the parties concerned wish to confirm the their relationship. At DKL it is a requirement to follow strict chain of custody and proper documentation with consent of the relevant parties when collecting the samples for DNA Paternity Test so that the test process and test results are accurate and able to wisthstand scrutiny.
Reported turnaround: 3 Days
Report date: 71-Hours
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 124390.0

name: TSH Receptor Antibody (TSHR)
text:
Test code: 6538
Test name: TSH Receptor Antibody (TSHR)
Also known as: Anti TSH Receptor Antibody; Thyrotropin receptor antibody (TRAb); Anti-TSHR;TRAb
Specimen: Serum,Lithium Heparin
Collection instructions: Serum collected using standard sampling tubes or tubes containing separating gel. Li?heparin, K2?EDTA and K3?EDTA plasma.
Description: Anti - TSHR / TRAb antibody testing is carried out in the investigation suspected auto-immune thyroid diseases. e.g. hyperthyroidism (Grave's disease) The TSH Receptor Antibody (TRAb) test is a specialized blood test used to detect the presence of autoantibodies that target the thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) receptor. These antibodies are most commonly associated with Graves disease, an autoimmune condition that causes the thyroid gland to become overactive, resulting in hyperthyroidism. In this condition, the antibodies mimic the action of TSH, overstimulating the thyroid and leading to excessive production of thyroid hormones. The TRAb test is an important tool for confirming a diagnosis of Graves disease, especially in cases where clinical symptoms or imaging results are unclear. It is also used to monitor treatment response, assess the likelihood of disease relapse after therapy, and evaluate the risk of neonatal thyrotoxicosis in pregnant women with current or past Graves disease, as the antibodies can cross the placenta. While the test is highly specific for Graves disease, some patients may not have detectable antibody levels, particularly at early or late stages of the condition. Additionally, results may be influenced by recent treatments such as radioiodine therapy or by interfering substances in the blood. Overall, the TSH Receptor Antibody test provides valuable information in the diagnosis and management of autoimmune thyroid disorders and is most effective when interpreted alongside clinical findings and thyroid function tests.
Reported turnaround: 1 Week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: TUE & FRI
Standard price (KES): 3690.0

name: Anti-Gliadin IgA (Anti-DGP IgA)
text:
Test code: 5071
Test name: Anti-Gliadin IgA (Anti-DGP IgA)
Also known as: ANTI GLIADIN IgA
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Anti-Gliadin IgA (Anti-DGP IgA) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The Deamidated Gliadin IgA test quantitatively measures IgA antibodies against deamidated gliadin peptides (anti-DGP IgA) in human serum or plasma. It aids in the evaluation of celiac disease (CD) and dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhrings disease) when used alongside other clinical and laboratory data. Celiac disease is an autoimmune disorder triggered by gluten in genetically predisposed individuals, primarily linked to HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 genotypes. Gliadin, a gluten protein, undergoes deamidation by tissue transglutaminase (t-TG), forming complexes that activate the immune system, leading to inflammation and potential villous atrophy in the intestines. Serological testing, especially anti-t-TG IgA combined with total IgA measurement, is the recommended first-line approach due to its high sensitivity (96-98%) and specificity (93-95%). Anti-DGP antibodies are highly specific markers for gluten intolerance, with IgA tests showing 86-95% sensitivity and 91-95% specificity, making them particularly useful in children, IgA-deficient individuals, and patients with negative or low anti-t-TG or EMA results. Monitoring anti-DGP and anti-t-TG antibody levels is essential for assessing treatment response in patients adhering to gluten-free diets. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 3390.0

text:

Description: The Deamidated Gliadin IgG test quantitatively measures IgG antibodies against deamidated gliadin peptides (anti-DGP IgG) in serum or plasma. It is used alongside other clinical and laboratory findings to support the diagnosis of celiac disease (CD) and dermatitis herpetiformis. CD is an autoimmune condition triggered by gluten in genetically predisposed individuals, primarily linked to HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 genotypes. Gliadin, a gluten-derived protein, undergoes modification by tissue transglutaminase (t-TG), forming complexes that activate immune responses, leading to intestinal inflammation and potential villous atrophy. Serological testing, particularly anti-t-TG IgA and total IgA, remains the first-line diagnostic approach due to its high sensitivity (96-98%) and specificity (93-95%). Anti-DGP IgG antibodies are highly specific for gluten intolerance and are particularly useful in pediatric patients, as they may appear before anti-t-TG antibodies. The test is also beneficial in patients with negative or low anti-t-TG/EMA levels but clinical suspicion of CD. Antibody levels, including anti-DGP IgG, decrease progressively with adherence to a gluten-free diet, although IgG titers decline more slowly compared to IgA. Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Anti-GBM and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The GBM test quantitatively detection of IgG antibodies against the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) in human serum or plasma, aiding in the diagnosis of Goodpastures syndrome (GP) and differentiating it from other vasculitides. Anti-GBM antibodies are pathogenic markers of rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN) and Goodpastures syndrome, which may involve both kidneys and lungs (haemorrhagic alveolitis). Early detection is crucial due to the rapid and severe progression of GP. While kidney biopsy with linear immunofluorescence remains the diagnostic gold standard, serologic tests like CLIA or ELISA are highly sensitive (94.7-100%) and specific (90.9-100%) alternatives, particularly when biopsy is not feasible. Anti-GBM antibody levels help assess prognosis and treatment response, especially with plasmapheresis. Around 10-38% of patients with anti-GBM antibodies also have ANCA positivity, commonly against MPO, warranting parallel ANCA testing. Persistent antibody negativity is essential before kidney transplantation to prevent recurrence of the disease in the graft. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Flow Cytometry BAL T- Lymphocytes Sub-set
text:
Test code: 7364
Test name: Flow Cytometry BAL T- Lymphocytes Sub-set
Also known as: CD4/CD8 Fluid BAL ratio;Fluid Flow Cytometry Bronchio-Alveolar Lavage
Description: T-lymphocyte subset analysis on bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid is performed using multiparametric flow cytometry to characterize cellular immune populations within the lower respiratory tract. The assay identifies and quantifies T lymphocytes based on surface antigen expression, primarily CD3 (total T cells), CD4 (T-helper cells), and CD8 (cytotoxic T cells). Results are reported as percentages of gated lymphocytes and, where applicable, as absolute counts, providing insight into the local immune milieu of the lung. This test is clinically useful in the evaluation of interstitial lung diseases, sarcoidosis, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, pulmonary infections (including opportunistic infections in immunocompromised patients), and immune-mediated or transplant-related pulmonary conditions. Interpretation should be correlated with clinical findings, radiologic features, microbiological results, and histopathology, as BAL lymphocyte subset distributions reflect localized immune responses rather than systemic immune status.
Reported turnaround: Same Day
Report date: 8-Hours
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 8990.0

Description: Whole Genome Sequencing is a diagnostic blood test designed to provide a comprehensive overview of an individual's genetic composition. name: HLA - Celiac Disease (DQB1-DQA1) Haplotype Association Including DQ2, DQ8
text:
Test code: 5465
Test name: HLA - Celiac Disease (DQB1-DQA1) Haplotype Association Including DQ2, DQ8
Also known as: DQB1-DQA1
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: 5 ml EDTA
Description: This test analyzes specific HLA class II genes (DQA1 and DQB1) to determine the presence of celiac disease-associated haplotypes, particularly HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8. These genetic markers are strongly associated with celiac disease and are present in the majority of affected individuals. The test is performed on a blood sample and uses molecular techniques to accurately identify relevant HLA variants. The presence of HLA-DQ2 and/or HLA-DQ8 supports genetic susceptibility to celiac disease but is not diagnostic on its own. Absence of both haplotypes makes celiac disease highly unlikely. This test is useful in the evaluation of patients with inconclusive serology or histology, those already on a gluten-free diet, and for risk assessment in first-degree relatives of patients with celiac disease. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 16690.0

name: Phosphorylated Tau 217 (pTAU 217)
text:
Test code: 5466
Test name: Phosphorylated Tau 217 (pTAU 217)
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: EDTA Plasma
Description: The Phosphorylated Tau 217 (pTau-217) test measures levels of tau protein phosphorylated at threonine 217, a biomarker closely associated with Alzheimers disease pathology. This test is typically performed on blood or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) using highly sensitive immunoassay techniques to detect abnormal tau phosphorylation linked to amyloid-beta deposition and neurodegeneration. Elevated pTau-217 levels are strongly correlated with Alzheimers disease and can help differentiate it from other causes of cognitive impairment. The test is useful for early detection, diagnostic support in patients with mild cognitive symptoms, and in monitoring disease progression or response to therapy. Results should be interpreted alongside clinical findings, neuroimaging, and other laboratory investigations. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Kinship Studies x4 Individuals
text:
Test code: 8798
Test name: Kinship Studies x4 Individuals
Also known as: Kinship Test; DNA test (4 persons)DNA test (4 people)
Specimen: Swab
Collection instructions: DNA Paternity Testing Specimen - Buccal Swab (Cotton Swab) or dried blood spot on treated or untreated paper. Buccal Swab Specimen Collection Instructions 1. Prepare the Collection Kit: Ensure the kit contains sterile buccal swabs (minimum 2 per individual), labeled collection envelopes or tubes, gloves, and a consent form. 2. Label each envelope or tube clearly with the individual's full name, date of birth, and collection date. 3. Ensure Proper Identification: Verify and record the identity of each donor using a valid form of identification. 4. Complete the chain-of-custody form if required. 5. Pre-Collection Instructions: Do not eat, drink, smoke, chew gum, or brush teeth for at least 30 minutes prior to sample collection. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Ensure each sample is properly sealed and labeled. 9. Documentation: Complete and sign all required documentation, including consent and identification forms. Ensure accurate linkage of sample ID to the donor's identity. 10. Transport to Laboratory: Place all labeled envelopes, consent forms, and chain-of-custody documents in the collection kit or transport bag. Deliver to the laboratory under standard room temperature conditions. Avoid exposure to moisture or heat.
Description: The DNA Paternity Testing Autosomal STR (Fragment Analysis) uses deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) to accurately determine whether there is a biological relationship between a child and a man (alleged father). The DNA Paternity Test may be done for legal reasons usually following a court order or legal discussions with lawyers, or it can also be done for peace-of-mind where the parties concerned wish to confirm the paternity of a child in relation to the man in question. At DKL it is a requirement to follow strict chain of custody and proper documentation with consent of the relevant parties when collecting the samples for DNA Paternity Test so that the test process and test results are accurate and able to wisthstand scrutiny.

Report date: 71-Hours
Testing days: DAILY-0

text:

Collection instructions: Collect 20?30 mL of amniotic fluid where possible; the practical minimum is 10?15 mL, subject to acceptance by the receiving laboratory. Record gestational age, clinical indication and collection time. Transport promptly at room temperature. Consent is required. Confirm the receiving laboratory's exact volume cutoff before collection.

This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Gut health by LC-MS/MS
text:
Test code: 2364
Test name: Gut health by LC-MS/MS
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Gut Health by LC-MS/MS and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: Gut Health by LC-MS/MS is a urine-based metabolic profile that measures selected organic acid biomarkers associated with intestinal microbial metabolism and gut microbiome balance. The assay is performed by liquid chromatographytandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), with results expressed relative to urinary creatinine. The profile includes markers associated with intestinal fungal overgrowth and microbiome dysbiosis, including citramalic acid, tartaric acid, hippuric acid, 4-methylhippuric acid, 2-hydroxyphenylacetic acid, 4-hydroxybenzoic acid, 3-indoleacetic acid, 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid, 3-hydroxybutyric acid, succinic acid, orotic acid, pyroglutamic acid, homovanillic acid and adipic acid. Alterations in these metabolites may reflect changes in microbial metabolism, intestinal dysbiosis, oxidative stress and related metabolic pathways. In particular, the reference laboratory interprets increased succinic and adipic acids as biochemical findings that may be associated with gut dysbiosis and increased oxidative or inflammatory activity. This test is intended as an adjunctive metabolic assessment and should be interpreted alongside the patients clinical presentation, dietary history and other relevant laboratory or gastrointestinal investigations. It does not directly identify or quantify individual microorganisms and should not be used in isolation to diagnose a specific gastrointestinal infection or disease. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Report date: 2-Weeks

The profile includes markers associated with intestinal fungal overgrowth and microbiome dysbiosis, including citramalic acid, tartaric acid, hippuric acid, 4-methylhippuric acid, 2-hydroxyphenylacetic acid, 4-hydroxybenzoic acid, 3-indoleacetic acid, 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid, 3-hydroxybutyric acid, succinic acid, orotic acid, pyroglutamic acid, homovanillic acid and adipic acid. Alterations in these metabolites may reflect changes in microbial metabolism, intestinal dysbiosis, oxidative stress and related metabolic pathways. In particular, the reference laboratory interprets increased succinic and adipic acids as biochemical findings that may be associated with gut dysbiosis and increased oxidative or inflammatory activity. This test is intended as an adjunctive metabolic assessment and should be interpreted alongside the patients clinical presentation, dietary history and other relevant laboratory or gastrointestinal investigations. It does not directly identify or quantify individual microorganisms and should not be used in isolation to diagnose a specific gastrointestinal infection or disease. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Description: The Celiac IgG Panel is a serological test used in the screening and diagnosis of celiac disease by detecting IgA antibodies directed against tissue transglutaminase (tTG IgG) and/or deamidated gliadin peptides (DGP IgG). These antibodies are produced in response to gluten exposure and are highly sensitive markers of gluten-induced intestinal injury. This test is considered the preferred initial screening tool in individuals with normal IgA levels and may also be used to monitor response and adherence to a gluten-free diet.

name: Mixed meal hypoglycemia test
text:

Collection instructions: Symbol; ;;; READ INSTRUCTIONS CAREFULLY! \'B7\*\'B7-150 Patient should fast from 10 pm the previous night and present themselves at 8:00 am on the morming of the test \'B7Patient should bring with them a meal from home or a facility of choice that contains carbohydrates, fats and proteins- preferably a meal similar to one that induces hypoglycemia. \'B7Fasting Glucose, Insulin and C-peptide are collected and labelled clearly as fasting \'B7The meal is ingested - Time zero \'B7Repeat sampling is collected in 30 minute intervals (30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 210, 240, 270 & 300 minutes), samples for Glucose, Insulin and C-peptide are collected. An intravenous cannular may be used to avoid multiple venepucture. \'B7Should symptoms of hypoglycemia occur, collect samples immediately at this point - collect samples for Glucose, Insulin and C-peptide and then correct the hypoglycemia immediately. Symptoms of hypoglycemia include- confusion, shakiness, anxiety, dizzy spells, tremors, loss of conciousness etc. \'B7\*\'B7-150 Have a point of care glucometer to confirm hypoglycemia should symptoms occur. A medical doctor, nurse or clinical officer should be at hand to assist. name: p53 Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
text:
Test code: 6987
Test name: p53 Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
Also known as: p53 IHC;
Description: p53 Immunohistochemistry (IHC) acts as a rapid surrogate for TP53 dysfunction in tumors from suspected Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS) cases (germline TP53 pathogenic variants). In LFS-associated tumors (e.g., early-onset breast cancer, sarcomas, brain tumors, adrenocortical carcinoma), aberrant patterns-strong diffuse nuclear overexpression (>50-80% intense positivity, common with missense variants stabilizing mutant protein) or complete null/absent staining (<1% positivity, typical of truncating/non-missense variants)-strongly suggest TP53 alteration and warrant germline TP53 testing, especially in young patients with LFS-spectrum cancers or family history. A normal/wild-type pattern (scattered weak-moderate nuclear staining in few cells) does not exclude LFS. p53 IHC is not diagnostic of germline status - germline confirmation requires blood-based genetic testing - but aberrant results provide a quick, cost-effective trigger for genetic counseling and surveillance in confirmed carriers.

Description: The Celiac IgG and IgA Panel is a serological test used in the screening and diagnosis of celiac disease by detecting IgG and IgA antibodies directed against tissue transglutaminase (tTG IgG and IgA) and/or deamidated gliadin peptides (DGP IgG and IgA). These antibodies are produced in response to gluten exposure and are highly sensitive markers of gluten-induced intestinal injury. A positive result suggests active celiac disease when the patient is consuming a gluten-containing diet. This test is considered the preferred initial screening tool in individuals with normal IgG and IgA levels and may also be used to monitor response and adherence to a gluten-free diet.

name: JAK2 V617F Gene Mutation Detection (First Line)
text:
Test code: 4737
Test name: JAK2 V617F Gene Mutation Detection (First Line)
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood),Serum
Collection instructions: JAK2 Quantitative RT-PCR for Polycythemia Vera; JAK2 Quantitative RT-PCR for Essential Thrombocythemia; JAK2 Quantitative RT-PCR for Primary Myelofibrosis / MPN;
Description: The JAK2 V617F mutation is a recurrent somatic variant in the JAK2 gene and serves as a key diagnostic marker for myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs). It is present in the majority of patients with polycythemia vera and in a significant proportion of those with essential thrombocythemia and primary myelofibrosis. This test is recommended as a first-line molecular investigation in patients with unexplained erythrocytosis, thrombocytosis, or other clinical features suggestive of an MPN. Detection of the mutation supports a clonal myeloid process and contributes to diagnostic classification in conjunction with clinical and hematologic findings. A positive result is highly indicative of an MPN but should be interpreted alongside full blood count parameters, bone marrow findings, and other relevant investigations. A negative result does not exclude an MPN; in cases with strong clinical suspicion-particularly suspected polycythemia vera-further testing for less common mutations (e.g., JAK2 exon 12) or additional markers (such as CALR or MPL) may be warranted.
Reported turnaround: After Three Days
Report date: 3-Days
Testing days: TUE & FRI
Standard price (KES): 16990.0

name: Paraneoplastic Neurological Syndrome [PNS] Ab Profile x6 (Serum)
text:
Test code: 9896
Test name: Paraneoplastic Neurological Syndrome [PNS] Ab Profile x6 (Serum)
Also known as: Paraneoplastic Encephalitis Antibody Panel; Neuronal Paraneoplastic Antibodies; Onconeural Antibody Profile
Collection instructions: Submit minimum 3 mL serum. Collect blood into a plain or serum separator tube, allow to clot and separate serum promptly. Avoid gross haemolysis. Store and transport refrigerate 2-8 degrees centigrade
Description: Serum IgG autoantibody profile for investigation of suspected paraneoplastic neurological syndromes (PNS), including paraneoplastic encephalitis. The panel detects six classical intracellular/onconeural antibodies: Amphiphysin, CV2.1/CRMP5, PNMA2 (Ma2/Ta), ANNA-1/Hu, ANNA-2/Ri and PCA-1/Yo. Paraneoplastic encephalitis is an immune-mediated neurological syndrome occurring in association with an underlying malignancy, in which the neurological presentation may precede detection of the cancer. It is typically associated with antibodies directed against intracellular neuronal antigens and is therefore diagnostically and biologically distinct from the more common neuronal surface/synaptic antibody-mediated autoimmune encephalitides. This panel should therefore not be used interchangeably with the Autoimmune Encephalitis Panel, which detects antibodies such as NMDA-R, AMPA-R, GABA-B-R, LGI1 and CASPR2. Those antibodies are directed predominantly against neuronal surface or synaptic targets and may occur with or without an associated malignancy. A positive result should be interpreted with the neurological phenotype and should prompt appropriate investigation for an underlying malignancy. A negative result does not exclude paraneoplastic encephalitis/PNS or antibodies not represented in this six-antigen panel. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 16990.0

name: BRAF Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
text:
Test code: 6929
Test name: BRAF Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
Also known as: BRAF IHC;
Specimen: BLOCKS
Description: BRAF V600E Immunohistochemistry (IHC) detects expression of the mutant BRAF V600E protein in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue using a mutation-specific antibody. Positive cytoplasmic staining in tumor cells supports the presence of a BRAF V600E mutation, a clinically significant alteration encountered in several neoplasms including melanoma, colorectal carcinoma, papillary thyroid carcinoma, hairy cell leukemia, and selected central nervous system and histiocytic tumors. Identification of BRAF V600E may assist in diagnosis, prognostic stratification, and selection of targeted therapy where appropriate. A negative result suggests absence of detectable BRAF V600E mutant protein, but does not exclude other BRAF mutations or alternative molecular alterations. Although BRAF V600E IHC shows high concordance with molecular testing, confirmatory molecular analysis may be recommended in selected cases, particularly where therapeutic decisions depend on mutation status.
Reported turnaround: After Five Days
Report date: 5-Days
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 6690.0

name: Beta-2 Microglobulin (B2MG)
text:
Test code: 2345
Test name: Beta-2 Microglobulin (B2MG)
Also known as: B-2 MICROGLOBULIN B2MG
Specimen: Serum,Lithium Heparin,Urine
Collection instructions: Allow specimen to clot completely at room temperature. Separate serum or plasma from cells ASAP or within 2 hours of collection. Transport aat 2-8 degrees celcius
Description: Quantitative determination of Beta 2 microglobulin is used for risk stratification and staging of multiple myeloma, Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, and other lymphoproliferative disorders. In addition it may be used in differentiating glomerular and tubular renal disease. The Beta-2 Microglobulin (B2M) test measures the level of a small protein found on the surface of most cells, particularly those involved in the immune system. B2M is normally present in the body and is filtered out by the kidneys. The test is commonly used to evaluate kidney function, monitor certain cancers such as multiple myeloma and lymphoma, or assess immune system activity in conditions like HIV or autoimmune diseases. Elevated levels may suggest kidney dysfunction, increased cell turnover, or immune system activation. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 2990.0

name: Salivary Cortisol (Morning Sample)
text:
Test code: 7676
Test name: Salivary Cortisol (Morning Sample)
Also known as: Cortisol in Salivary
Specimen: Saliva
Description: The salivary cortisol is measured using the Elecsys Cortisol II assay on the Roche cobas e801 platform, employing a competitive electrochemiluminescence immunoassay (ECLIA). This method quantifies free (biologically active) cortisol in saliva, which correlates closely with the unbound serum fraction and is independent of cortisol-binding globulin. Salivary sampling is non-invasive and particularly suited for assessing circadian cortisol rhythm, with late-night salivary cortisol serving as a sensitive screening test for hypercortisolism (Cushing syndrome). Interpretation is time-dependent and must consider collection timing and pre-analytical factors. Late-night values (23:00-24:00) are expected to be low (<6-7 nmol/L), while morning values (06:00-08:00) are highest (10 - 25 nmol/L) whereby abnormal elevation suggests loss of normal diurnal suppression. Results may be affected by blood contamination (e.g. gum bleeding), recent food intake, stress, or exogenous steroid exposure. Correlation with clinical findings and, where indicated, confirmatory testing (e.g. dexamethasone suppression test or 24-hour urinary free cortisol) is recommended.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: One Hour
Standard price (KES): 2690.0

name: SMAD4 Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
text:
Test code: 1519
Test name: SMAD4 Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
Also known as: SMAD4 IHC;
Specimen: BLOCKS
Description: SMAD4 immunohistochemistry (IHC) is used to assess the integrity of the TGF-\'e2 signaling pathway by evaluating SMAD4 protein expression within tumor cells. In normal tissues, SMAD4 demonstrates diffuse nuclear and cytoplasmic staining, reflecting its role as a central mediator of intracellular signal transduction. In neoplastic contexts, retained (intact) SMAD4 expression is indicated by preserved nuclear staining in tumor cells, comparable to adjacent non-neoplastic elements, which serve as an internal positive control. Loss of SMAD4 expression -defined as complete absence of nuclear staining in tumor cells with retained staining in surrounding stromal, inflammatory, or epithelial cells-is indicative of SMAD4 inactivation, commonly due to gene mutation or deletion. This finding is clinically relevant in several malignancies, particularly pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and colorectal carcinoma, where SMAD4 loss may be associated with more aggressive tumor biology, poorer prognosis, and potential implications for disease progression and therapeutic stratification. Partial or heterogeneous staining patterns should be interpreted with caution and in correlation with morphology and other molecular findings.
Reported turnaround: After Three Days
Report date: 3-Days
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 6690.0

name: Strongyloides Agar Plate Culture Method (APC)
text:
Test code: 7029
Test name: Strongyloides Agar Plate Culture Method (APC)
Also known as: Strongyloides culture (agar method);Larval culture on agar;Stool agar culture for Strongyloides
Specimen: STOOL
Description: Strongyloides agar plate culture is a high-sensitivity stool-based method for the detection of Strongyloides stercoralis larvae. A fresh stool specimen is inoculated onto a nutrient agar plate and incubated, allowing motile larvae to migrate across the surface. As they move, they carry enteric bacteria that proliferate along their path, producing characteristic serpiginous tracks that signal larval presence. Recovered larvae can then be microscopically examined for morphological confirmation of species. This method is considered the most sensitive stool technique for Strongyloides detection and is particularly useful in low parasite burden or intermittent shedding, where routine stool microscopy may be negative. A positive result confirms active infection. However, the test requires fresh samples, controlled incubation conditions, and technical expertise, and may not be routinely available in all laboratories. In clinical practice, it is often used alongside routine microscopy on stool and blood serology testing to improve overall diagnostic yield.
Reported turnaround: After Three Days
Report date: 3-Days
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 5690.0

name: Hepatitis B (HBV) Genotyping (including HBV Viral Load)
text:
Test code: 1322
Test name: Hepatitis B (HBV) Genotyping (including HBV Viral Load)
Also known as: HBV genotype; HBV genotyping; HBV DNA viral load and genotype; HBV Genotype Testing New
Collection instructions: Sample type: EDTA plasma preferred; serum acceptable. Collect 3?5 mL whole blood in an EDTA tube. Centrifuge promptly and separate plasma within 6 hours. Avoid haemolysis and repeated freeze?thaw cycles. Store at room temperature or 2?8 ?C for up to 72 hours, or freeze at -20 ?C or lower. Maintain the cold chain during transport. HBV viral load (HBV DNA) is performed first. Genotyping is carried out reflexively if the viral load is adequate (typically =1,000 IU/mL). Low viral load may result in genotyping failure. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: This assay provides a comprehensive molecular evaluation of hepatitis B virus (HBV), combining quantitative HBV DNA viral load measurement with reflex genotyping by PCR-based sequencing to determine the viral genotype (A?J). The viral load component quantifies circulating HBV DNA and is used for diagnosis, assessment of infectivity, and monitoring of antiviral therapy. Genotyping is performed on samples with sufficient viral load and may inform therapy selection, predicted treatment response (including interferon sensitivity), and prognosis, including risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Accurate genotyping requires adequate circulating viral DNA; low viral loads may fail amplification. The combined workflow is useful when no recent viral load result is available, so that quantification and genotype can be obtained from one referral. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 26990.0

name: Insulin -like growth Factor Binding protein 3 (IGFBP3)
text:
Test code: 3425
Test name: Insulin -like growth Factor Binding protein 3 (IGFBP3)
Also known as: IGFBP3
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Insulin -Like Growth Factor Binding Protein 3 (IGFBP3) and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: Insulin-like Growth Factor Binding Protein 3 (IGFBP-3) is the major carrier protein for insulin-like growth factors (IGF-I and IGF-II) in circulation and reflects growth hormone (GH) activity. Measurement of IGFBP-3 provides a stable and reliable indicator of the GH-IGF axis, as its levels are less affected by short-term physiological fluctuations compared to IGF-1. This makes IGFBP-3 particularly useful in the evaluation of suspected growth hormone deficiency (GHD) and growth hormone excess (e.g., acromegaly or gigantism), especially in pediatric populations. Clinically, IGFBP-3 is used alongside IGF-1 to assess disorders of growth and development, including short stature, delayed puberty, and suspected pituitary dysfunction. Low levels are suggestive of growth hormone deficiency, malnutrition, or chronic systemic illness, while elevated levels may be seen in conditions of GH excess. Interpretation should be age- and sex-specific, and results are best considered in conjunction with clinical findings and other endocrine investigations. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Description: Yellow Fever Serology detects antibodies (IgG) against the Yellow fever virus in serum, using ELISA immunoassay method. Interpretation should consider potential cross-reactivity with other flaviviruses such as dengue. name: Sarcoma Fusion Panel (RNA-based NGS)
text:
Test code: 5277
Test name: Sarcoma Fusion Panel (RNA-based NGS)
Also known as: Comprehensive Sarcoma Fusion Panel (RNA Sequencing); Soft Tissue Tumor Fusion Panel; RNA-Based Gene Fusion Panel for Sarcomas
Specimen: Block (FFPE)
Collection instructions: Submit representative tumour tissue (usually an FFPE block or approved alternative) with the histological diagnosis and estimated tumour content. Provide the clinical indication and any prior molecular or pathology results. Follow current laboratory or referral-laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: This test is a comprehensive RNA-based next-generation sequencing (NGS) assay designed to detect clinically significant gene fusions and selected transcript alterations associated with sarcomas and other soft tissue tumors. The assay is performed on RNA extracted from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor tissue and enables sensitive detection of fusion transcripts involving key genes such as CIC, BCOR, EWSR1, FUS, SS18, FOXO1, among others. These gene rearrangements are critical diagnostic biomarkers that facilitate accurate classification of undifferentiated round cell sarcomas and other fusion-driven mesenchymal neoplasms. The test is particularly valuable in cases with overlapping morphology and immunophenotype, where conventional histopathology and immunohistochemistry are insufficient for definitive diagnosis. Results from this panel support precise tumor classification, prognostication, and therapeutic decision-making, including eligibility for targeted or protocol-based treatments. This assay is recommended for evaluation of suspected Ewing-like sarcomas, CIC-rearranged sarcoma, BCOR-rearranged sarcoma, synovial sarcoma, alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma, and other fusion-associated malignancies. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Report date: 4-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Muscle Biopsy Electron Microscopy
text:
Test code: 8781
Test name: Muscle Biopsy Electron Microscopy
Also known as: Electron Microscopy (Specimen in EM Fixative)
Collection instructions: Submit Muscle tissue biopsies in 3% Buffered Glutaraldehyde solution.
Description: Electron microscopy (EM) of skeletal muscle biopsy is a specialised ultrastructural examination performed to evaluate muscle fibres, neuromuscular junctions and associated cellular organelles at high magnification. It provides detailed assessment of sarcomere architecture, mitochondria, glycogen, lipid droplets, lysosomes, autophagic vacuoles, myofibrils, nuclei and basement membranes, and can identify characteristic ultrastructural abnormalities not visible on routine light microscopy. EM is particularly valuable in the diagnosis and classification of mitochondrial myopathies, congenital myopathies, myofibrillar myopathies, inclusion body myositis, storage disorders, vacuolar myopathies and selected muscular dystrophies. It is performed as an adjunct to routine histology, histochemistry, immunohistochemistry and molecular genetic testing to provide comprehensive clinicopathological correlation. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 3 Weeks
Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 23990.0

name: Coxiella burnetii IgG Antibody Test
text:
Test code: 3128
Test name: Coxiella burnetii IgG Antibody Test
Also known as: Q Fever Serology (IgG); Coxiella burnetii IgG Antibodies; Coxiella IgG Antibody Assay; Phase I & Phase II Coxiella burnetii IgG Antibodies
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Coxiella Burnetii IgG Antibody Test and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The Coxiella burnetii IgG Antibody Test is a serological assay used to detect IgG antibodies directed against Coxiella burnetii, the causative agent of Q fever. The test assists in the evaluation of prior exposure, recent infection, chronic Q fever, or immune response following infection. Depending on the assay methodology and clinical context, antibodies against both Phase I and Phase II antigens may be assessed to help differentiate acute from chronic infection patterns. Q fever is a zoonotic infection commonly associated with exposure to livestock such as cattle, sheep, and goats, particularly through inhalation of contaminated aerosols, animal birth products, dust, or unpasteurized dairy products. Clinical manifestations may range from asymptomatic infection to acute febrile illness, atypical pneumonia, hepatitis, or chronic infections including endocarditis and vascular infection. Serological interpretation should always be correlated with clinical findings, exposure history, imaging, and other laboratory investigations. Early acute infection may yield negative serology prior to seroconversion; repeat testing after 2?3 weeks may be clinically indicated where suspicion remains high. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 1 week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 6990.0

name: Coxiella burnetii IgM Antibody Test
text:
Test code: 3129
Test name: Coxiella burnetii IgM Antibody Test
Also known as: Q Fever Serology (IgM); Coxiella burnetii IgM Antibodies; Coxiella IgM Antibody Assay; Phase I & Phase II Coxiella burnetii IgM Antibodies
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Coxiella Burnetii IgM Antibody Test and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The Coxiella burnetii IgM Antibody Test is a serological assay used to detect IgM antibodies against Coxiella burnetii, the etiologic agent of Q fever. Detection of IgM antibodies may support the diagnosis of recent or acute infection, particularly when interpreted together with clinical presentation and complementary serological findings including IgG antibody patterns. Q fever is a zoonotic infection transmitted primarily through inhalation of aerosols contaminated by infected livestock, especially cattle, sheep, and goats. Acute infection may present with non-specific febrile illness, severe headache, atypical pneumonia, hepatitis, or flu-like symptoms. IgM antibodies generally appear early during infection; however, isolated IgM reactivity should be interpreted cautiously due to the possibility of cross-reactivity or non-specific serological responses. Confirmation with paired acute and convalescent sera demonstrating seroconversion or rising antibody titres may be recommended where clinically indicated. Serological results should be interpreted in conjunction with exposure history, clinical findings, and other laboratory investigations. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 1 week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 6990.0
