name: Hantavirus Detection by RT-PCR
text:
Test code: 9485
Test name: Hantavirus Detection by RT-PCR
Also known as: Hantavirus PCR
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: Collect the approved blood or named specimen for Hantavirus Detection by RT-PCR. Send with the clinical indication and any prior molecular results. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: The Hantavirus RNA Detection by Real-Time RT-PCR assay is a qualitative molecular test used for the detection of Hantavirus viral RNA in clinical specimens. The test assists in the early diagnosis of acute hantavirus infection, including Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) and Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS), particularly during the early viremic phase before antibody seroconversion occurs. Clinical features may include acute febrile illness, thrombocytopenia, renal impairment, respiratory distress, pulmonary edema, hemorrhagic manifestations, and history of rodent exposure. Detection of Hantavirus RNA supports active or recent infection. A negative result does not completely exclude infection and should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings, exposure history, imaging studies, and serological testing (Hantavirus IgM/IgG), especially in late-stage disease or low viral load states. The assay is performed using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) technology on validated clinical specimens including whole blood, plasma, serum, respiratory specimens, or tissue samples. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 1 week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 13990.0

name: Kinship Studies x5 Individuals
text:
Test code: 1789
Test name: Kinship Studies x5 Individuals
Also known as: Kinship Test; DNA test (5 persons)
Specimen: Swab
Collection instructions: DNA Paternity Testing Specimen - Buccal Swab (Cotton Swab) or dried blood spot on treated or untreated paper. Buccal Swab Specimen Collection Instructions 1. Prepare the Collection Kit: Ensure the kit contains sterile buccal swabs (minimum 2 per individual), labeled collection envelopes or tubes, gloves, and a consent form. 2. Label each envelope or tube clearly with the individual's full name, date of birth, and collection date. 3. Ensure Proper Identification: Verify and record the identity of each donor using a valid form of identification. 4. Complete the chain-of-custody form if required. 5. Pre-Collection Instructions: Do not eat, drink, smoke, chew gum, or brush teeth for at least 30 minutes prior to sample collection. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Ensure each sample is properly sealed and labeled. 9. Documentation: Complete and sign all required documentation, including consent and identification forms. Ensure accurate linkage of sample ID to the donor's identity. 10. Transport to Laboratory: Place all labeled envelopes, consent forms, and chain-of-custody documents in the collection kit or transport bag. Deliver to the laboratory under standard room temperature conditions. Avoid exposure to moisture or heat.
Description: The DNA Paternity Testing Autosomal STR (Fragment Analysis) uses deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) to accurately determine whether there is a biological relationship between a child and a man (alleged father). The DNA Paternity Test may be done for legal reasons usually following a court order or legal discussions with lawyers, or it can also be done for peace-of-mind where the parties concerned wish to confirm the paternity of a child in relation to the man in question. At DKL it is a requirement to follow strict chain of custody and proper documentation with consent of the relevant parties when collecting the samples for DNA Paternity Test so that the test process and test results are accurate and able to wisthstand scrutiny.
Reported turnaround: 3 Days
Report date: 71-Hours
Testing days: DAILY-0
Standard price (KES): 80390.0

name: HER2 NGS (ERBB2) Single Gene Mutation Analysis Amplification / Mutation Analysis
text:
Test code: 6466
Test name: HER2 NGS (ERBB2) Single Gene Mutation Analysis Amplification / Mutation Analysis
Also known as: ERBB2
Specimen: FFPE tumour tissue block,Cytology cell block (validated specimens),Plasma cfDNA / liquid biopsy
Collection instructions: Submit representative tumour tissue (usually an FFPE block or approved alternative) with the histological diagnosis and estimated tumour content. Provide the clinical indication and any prior molecular or pathology results. Follow current laboratory or referral-laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: This test performs molecular analysis of the HER2/ERBB2 oncogene using targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) to detect clinically significant genomic alterations including ERBB2 amplification (copy number gain), activating mutations, and selected insertions/deletions/fusions depending on panel design. HER2 alterations are important predictive biomarkers in multiple solid tumours including breast carcinoma, gastric/gastro-oesophageal adenocarcinoma, non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC), colorectal carcinoma, endometrial carcinoma, and other advanced malignancies. The assay assists in identifying patients who may benefit from HER2-targeted therapies such as trastuzumab, pertuzumab, trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), tucatinib, lapatinib, neratinib, and other anti-HER2 agents, as guided by tumour type and current oncology guidelines. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with histopathology, immunohistochemistry (IHC), FISH/ISH findings where applicable, tumour percentage, and overall clinical context. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 3 Weeks
Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 29990.0

name: Adrenal Cortex (ACA) 21-Hydroxylase Antibodies
text:
Test code: 4712
Test name: Adrenal Cortex (ACA) 21-Hydroxylase Antibodies
Also known as: 21-Hydroxylase Antibodies (Anti-21OH / CYP21A2 antibodies); CYP21A2 Antibodies
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Adrenal Cortex (ACA) 21-Hydroxylase Antibodies and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: Detects autoantibodies against 21-hydroxylase (CYP21A2), the major autoantigen in autoimmune adrenalitis. Used in the evaluation of suspected autoimmune primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) and autoimmune polyglandular syndromes. A positive result supports autoimmune adrenal cortical destruction as the cause of adrenal insufficiency. Results should be interpreted together with clinical findings and adrenal hormone studies (cortisol, ACTH, renin, aldosterone, electrolytes) This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Myelin-Associated Glycoprotein (MAG) Antibody
text:
Test code: 7831
Test name: Myelin-Associated Glycoprotein (MAG) Antibody
Also known as: Anti-MAG Antibody IgM;Anti-Myelin Associated Glycoprotein Antibody;Anti-MAG Neuropathy Antibody;
Specimen: Serum
Description: This assay detects IgM autoantibodies directed against myelin-associated glycoprotein (MAG), a component of peripheral nerve myelin involved in Schwann cell-axon interactions and maintenance of myelin integrity. Anti-MAG antibodies are associated with autoimmune demyelinating peripheral neuropathies, particularly distal acquired demyelinating symmetric neuropathy (DADS) and IgM paraproteinaemic neuropathy, commonly occurring in association with monoclonal IgM gammopathies such as IgM MGUS or Waldenstrom macroglobulinaemia. The test is useful in the diagnostic evaluation of patients with chronic slowly progressive sensory or sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy, sensory ataxia, tremor, or demyelinating neuropathy identified on nerve conduction studies. Testing is typically performed using ELISA or immunoblot-based methodologies. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings, electrophysiologic studies, serum protein electrophoresis/immunofixation, serum free light chain analysis, and other relevant neurologic and haematologic investigations
Reported turnaround: After Five Days
Report date: 5-Days
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 11990.0

name: POLD1 Mutation Analysis by NGS (Solid Single Gene Assay)
text:
Test code: 9528
Test name: POLD1 Mutation Analysis by NGS (Solid Single Gene Assay)
Also known as: POLD1 Gene Mutation Test; POLD1 NGS Analysis; DNA Polymerase Delta 1 Mutation Analysis; POLD1 Exonuclease Domain Mutation Analysis; POLD1 Single Gene NGS Assay
Specimen: BLOCK / TISSUE
Collection instructions: Submit representative tumour tissue (usually an FFPE block or approved alternative) with the histological diagnosis and estimated tumour content. Provide the clinical indication and any prior molecular or pathology results. Follow current laboratory or referral-laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: POLD1 Gene Mutation Test; POLD1 NGS Analysis; DNA Polymerase Delta 1 Mutation Analysis; POLD1 Exonuclease Domain Mutation Analysis; POLD1 Single Gene NGS Assay LIS Test Description: POLD1 Mutation Analysis by Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) is a targeted solid tumour molecular assay designed to detect clinically significant pathogenic variants in the POLD1 (DNA polymerase delta 1 catalytic subunit) gene, particularly within the exonuclease proofreading domain. The assay is performed as a focused single-gene NGS test on DNA extracted from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumour tissue or other validated solid tumour specimens. Pathogenic POLD1 mutations are associated with defective DNA proofreading and genomic hypermutation, contributing to tumourigenesis in selected solid tumours including colorectal, endometrial, and other malignancies. Alterations in POLD1 may be associated with elevated tumour mutational burden and may have potential prognostic and predictive significance, including possible relevance to immune checkpoint inhibitor responsiveness in selected clinical contexts. Germline POLD1 mutations are additionally associated with hereditary polymerase proofreading-associated cancer predisposition syndromes. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with histopathology, clinical findings, family history, MMR/MSI status, and other relevant molecular and genomic studies. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 3 Weeks
Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 53690.0

name: NGS RAS/RAF/PIK3C Extended 6-gene Panel
text:
Test code: 9691
Test name: NGS RAS/RAF/PIK3C Extended 6-gene Panel
Also known as: NGS 6-gene panel KRAS NRAS HRAS BRAF PIK3CA TP53; RAS/RAF Mutation Analysis by NGS; Extended RAS Pathway Somatic Mutation Panel; Targeted Solid Tumor Hotspot NGS Panel
Collection instructions: Submit representative tumour tissue (usually an FFPE block or approved alternative) with the histological diagnosis and estimated tumour content. Provide the clinical indication and any prior molecular or pathology results. Follow current laboratory or referral-laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: The RAS/RAF Extended NGS Panel is a focused targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) assay for detection of clinically significant somatic mutations in selected solid tumors using formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor tissue. The assay specifically evaluates hotspot regions and coding sequences within six clinically important cancer-associated genes: KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, and TP53. This panel is primarily designed to assess alterations involving the RAS/MAPK signaling pathway together with selected PI3K pathway and tumor suppressor genes relevant to oncogenesis, prognosis, targeted therapy selection, resistance profiling, and eligibility for precision oncology protocols. The assay detects single nucleotide variants (SNVs), small insertions/deletions (indels), and selected copy number alterations where technically feasible using massively parallel sequencing technology. Clinically relevant applications include molecular characterization of colorectal carcinoma, endometrial carcinoma, lung carcinoma, melanoma, thyroid carcinoma, pancreatic carcinoma, and other solid tumors in which RAS/RAF pathway alterations may influence therapeutic decision-making. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with histopathological findings, tumor type, clinical context, and other relevant molecular or immunohistochemical studies. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Report date: 4-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: PIK3CA Gene Mutation Analysis by NGS
text:
Test code: 9692
Test name: PIK3CA Gene Mutation Analysis by NGS
Also known as: PIK3CA Mutation Detection by NGS; PIK3CA Hotspot Mutation Analysis; PIK3CA Targeted NGS Assay
Specimen: BLOCK / TISSUE
Collection instructions: Submit representative tumour tissue (usually an FFPE block or approved alternative) with the histological diagnosis and estimated tumour content. Provide the clinical indication and any prior molecular or pathology results. Follow current laboratory or referral-laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: This assay detects clinically significant mutations in the PIK3CA gene (Phosphatidylinositol-4,5-Bisphosphate 3-Kinase Catalytic Subunit Alpha) using targeted Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) technology on DNA extracted from tumour tissue or other validated specimen types. The test interrogates key hotspot regions and coding exons of the PIK3CA gene associated with oncogenic activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling pathway. Common actionable mutations include variants involving codons E542K, E545K, Q546K, H1047R, and H1047L, among others. PIK3CA mutations are encountered in multiple solid tumours including breast carcinoma, colorectal carcinoma, endometrial carcinoma, cervical carcinoma, ovarian carcinoma, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, and other malignancies. Detection of a PIK3CA mutation may provide diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive therapeutic information, including potential eligibility for targeted therapies such as PI3K inhibitors where clinically indicated. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with tumour histology, clinical findings, radiologic features, and other molecular or cytogenetic investigations. This assay is intended for clinical diagnostic use and does not exclude the presence of mutations outside the regions analysed. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 3 Weeks
Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

text:
Test code: 4465
Test name: Brivaracetam Drug Level
Also known as: Brivaracetam Therapeutic Drug Monitoring (TDM); Brivaracetam Quantitative Assay; Brivaracetam Serum Level; Briviact TDM
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect at the time specified by the clinician (usually a trough immediately before the next dose unless a peak or protocol time is requested). Record collection time, dose, route, and time of the last dose. Follow current laboratory collection requirements. Confirm the referral laboratory's current specimen and transport requirements before collection.
Description: Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) assay for quantitative measurement of Brivaracetam concentration in plasma or serum using high-sensitivity liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Brivaracetam is a selective synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A) antiepileptic agent indicated primarily for management of focal-onset seizures. Measurement of brivaracetam levels may assist in assessment of therapeutic compliance, dose optimization, toxicity evaluation, pharmacokinetic variability, suspected drug interactions, refractory seizure management, and special clinical situations including hepatic impairment or pediatric therapy monitoring. Trough specimen collection immediately prior to the next scheduled dose is preferred for therapeutic interpretation. Clinical correlation with seizure control, concurrent antiepileptic medications, and patient symptoms is recommended. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: CMV (Cytomegalovirus) RT-PCR
text:
Test code: 2156
Test name: CMV (Cytomegalovirus) RT-PCR
Also known as: Cytomegalovirus qualitative & Quantitative PCR
Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood),CSF
Description: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) DNA PCR is a real-time polymerase chain reaction assay used for the qualitative and/or quantitative detection of CMV viral DNA in clinical specimens, commonly EDTA plasma, whole blood, cerebrospinal fluid, or urine depending on clinical indication. The test targets conserved regions of the CMV genome and provides a sensitive and specific method for detecting active viral replication. Quantitative results, typically reported in IU/mL or copies/mL depending on assay calibration, allow assessment of viral load and are useful for monitoring disease progression and response to antiviral therapy. CMV PCR is primarily indicated for the diagnosis and monitoring of CMV infection in immunocompromised patients, including transplant recipients and individuals with HIV, as well as for evaluation of suspected congenital CMV infection in neonates. The assay plays a critical role in guiding initiation and adjustment of antiviral treatment. Proper specimen collection in EDTA tubes and timely transport under appropriate conditions are essential to ensure sample integrity and reliable amplification results.

Testing days: DAILY-0

Description: Calcitonin is tested to aid in the diagnosis and management of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) and other thyroid or parathyroid disorders. It is a peptide hormone secreted by the parafollicular C cells of the thyroid in response to elevated serum calcium. Calcitonin lowers blood calcium and phosphate levels by inhibiting bone resorption and promoting renal excretion. text:

Description: The BRCA somatic testing checks for presence in tumor cells of mutations in two genes called BRCA1 and BRCA2. The BRCA1 and BRCA2 are known as tumour suppressor genes - they prevent cells from growing too rapidly or in an uncontrolled way. BRCA somatic testing on tissue biopsies having cancer cells helps to identify patients with cancer, particularly advanced ovarian cancer and also prostate cancer, who may benefit from PARP inhibitors depending on presence of BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes. Unlike germline mutation testing that looks for inherited mutations, the somatic mutations are not hereditary mutations but are acquired mutations confined to the tumor cells / tissues. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Alpha Galactosidase A (a-Gal A) Enzyme Activity for Fabry Disease
text:
Test code: 1392
Test name: Alpha Galactosidase A (a-Gal A) Enzyme Activity for Fabry Disease
Also known as: Alpha-Galactosidase A Activity; GLA Enzyme Activity : Fabry Disease Enzyme Assay: Fabry Screening Test
Specimen: Lithium Heparin
Collection instructions: Collect the laboratory-approved specimen for Alpha Galactosidase A (a-Gal A) Enzyme Activity for Fabry Disease and label it with patient identity and collection time. Send any relevant clinical information needed to interpret this test. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.
Description: dá-Galactosidase A (á-Gal A) Enzyme Activity is the primary biochemical test used in the evaluation of Fabry disease, an X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency of the á-galactosidase A enzyme. Reduced enzyme activity results in progressive accumulation of globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) and related glycosphingolipids within multiple organs, particularly the kidneys, heart, nervous system, skin, and eyes. This assay measures á-galactosidase A enzyme activity in peripheral blood and is highly sensitive for identifying affected males. In females, normal enzyme activity does not exclude Fabry disease because of variable X-chromosome inactivation; therefore, molecular confirmation by GLA gene analysis may be required where clinical suspicion remains high. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings, family history, and, where available, complementary tests such as Lyso-Gb3 and GLA gene mutation analysis. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 17390.0

text:
Test code: 9602
Test name: AST for Yeast ID & Sensitivity - Submitted Culture Isolate (Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing)
Also known as: Automated MIC & Antibiotic Susceptibility Testing;AST by VITEK® 2 (Submitted Isolate);
Collection instructions: Sample Type: Pure fungal isolate on culture plate (non-mixed culture) or pure subculture submitted on appropriate microbiological agar. Turnaround Time (TAT): 24-48 hours from receipt of a suitable pure isolate (may be extended if subculture or purity confirmation is required).
Description: This test performs automated antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) on a previously isolated yeast organism using the bioM\'e9rieux VITEK\'ae 2 system. A standardized yeast suspension prepared from a pure culture is inoculated into organism-specific AST cards containing multiple antimicrobial agents at defined concentrations. The system determines minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) and categorizes results as Susceptible (S), Intermediate/Susceptible Increased Exposure (I), or Resistant (R) according to current CLSI or EUCAST interpretive criteria, as configured by the laboratory. Testing is performed only on pure yeast isolates. Mixed cultures or unsuitable isolates require re-isolation and purification before AST can proceed. The report includes MIC values (where applicable), interpretive susceptibility categories, and may identify important resistance phenotypes or mechanisms supported by the VITEK\'ae 2 Advanced Expert System to assist clinicians in selecting appropriate antimicrobial therapy

text:

Collection instructions: DNA Paternity Testing Specimen - Buccal Swab (Cotton Swab) or dried blood spot on treated or untreated paper. Buccal Swab Specimen Collection Instructions 1. Prepare the Collection Kit: Ensure the kit contains sterile buccal swabs (minimum 2 per individual), labeled collection envelopes or tubes, gloves, and a consent form. 2. Label each envelope or tube clearly with the individual's full name, date of birth, and collection date. 3. Ensure Proper Identification: Verify and record the identity of each donor using a valid form of identification. 4. Complete the chain-of-custody form if required. 5. Pre-Collection Instructions: Do not eat, drink, smoke, chew gum, or brush teeth for at least 30 minutes prior to sample collection. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Ensure each sample is properly sealed and labeled. 9. Documentation: Complete and sign all required documentation, including consent and identification forms. Ensure accurate linkage of sample ID to the donor's identity. 10. Transport to Laboratory: Place all labeled envelopes, consent forms, and chain-of-custody documents in the collection kit or transport bag. Deliver to the laboratory under standard room temperature conditions. Avoid exposure to moisture or heat.

Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: 3?5 mL whole blood in K2 EDTA or 2 mL bone marrow. Indicate the date and time of sample collection on the test request form.
Description: A molecular test used to assess the proportion of donor-derived and recipient-derived hematopoietic cells following hematopoietic stem cell or bone marrow transplantation. Chimerism analysis supports post-transplant monitoring by evaluating engraftment status, detecting mixed chimerism, identifying possible graft failure, and assisting in the early recognition of disease relapse or transplant complications. Results should be interpreted together with the patients transplant history, clinical findings, hematologic status, and other relevant laboratory investigations. name: Amylase Isoenzymes
text:
Test code: 7478
Test name: Amylase Isoenzymes
Also known as: Amylase Isoenzyme Analysis; Pancreatic & Salivary Amylase Isoenzymes; Amylase Fractionation
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Turnaround Time (TAT) Approximately 3 weeks after the 1st day of the testing month (batched referral test). Collect 3 mL of serum (minimum 1 mL) in a single SST (Serum Separator Tube). Allow the blood to clot completely before centrifugation, separate the serum promptly, and avoid haemolysis. Store and transport the specimen refrigerated (2-8?C). This is a batched referral assay. Specimens should be collected during the first week of the month and must reach the referral laboratory on or before the 1st day of the designated testing month to be included in that months analytical run.
Description: Amylase isoenzyme analysis measures total serum amylase and differentiates the pancreatic and salivary isoenzyme fractions to identify the source of an elevated serum amylase concentration. It is primarily used in the evaluation of persistent or unexplained hyperamylasaemia when the cause cannot be determined by routine serum amylase testing alone. The test helps distinguish pancreatic disorders from non-pancreatic causes of elevated amylase, including salivary gland disease, macroamylasaemia, impaired renal clearance, and ectopic amylase production. Results should be interpreted alongside the clinical presentation, serum lipase, imaging findings, and other relevant laboratory investigations. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

name: Prothrombin Time (PT) INR
text:
Test code: 1404
Test name: Prothrombin Time (PT) INR
Also known as: PT;Prothrombin Time;International Normalized Ratio (INR);INR
Specimen: Citrated
Description: A coagulation assay performed using the transmission turbidity method to assess the extrinsic and common coagulation pathways, including coagulation factors I (fibrinogen), II, V, VII, and X. The sample is mixed with excess tissue factor and calcium ions, triggering conversion of fibrinogen to insoluble fibrin. The resulting change in absorbance is measured, and the clotting time is reported as Prothrombin Time (PT) and International Normalized Ratio (INR). The test is used to screen for coagulation factor deficiencies and to monitor oral anticoagulant therapy with warfarin.
Tests included: International Normalized ratio (INR), Prothrombin Index, Prothrombin Time (PT)

name: Thrombin Time (TT)
text:
Test code: 1405
Test name: Thrombin Time (TT)
Also known as: TT
Specimen: Citrated
Description: A coagulation assay performed using the transmission turbidity method to assess the final stage of the coagulation cascade. The sample is mixed with an appropriate amount of thrombin, which converts fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin. The resulting change in absorbance is measured, and the time taken for fibrin formation is reported as the Thrombin Time. The test is used to evaluate fibrinogen function and detect abnormalities such as hypofibrinogenemia, dysfibrinogenemia, increased fibrin degradation products, or the presence of thrombin inhibitors including heparin and direct thrombin inhibitors.

text:
Test code: 7263
Test name: Y-Chromosome STR (Yfiler™ Plus) Paternal Lineage Analysis x2 Individuals
Also known as: Yfiler™ Plus Y-STR Analysis; Y-STR Kinship Test; Paternal Lineage DNA Test; Male Lineage DNA Analysis; Male Kinship DNA Test.
Specimen: Swab,EDTA (Whole Blood)
Collection instructions: DNA Paternity Testing Specimen - Buccal Swab (Cotton Swab) or dried blood spot on treated or untreated paper. Buccal Swab Specimen Collection Instructions 1. Prepare the Collection Kit: Ensure the kit contains sterile buccal swabs (minimum 2 per individual), labeled collection envelopes or tubes, gloves, and a consent form. 2. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Description: Y-Chromosome Short Tandem Repeat (Y-STR) analysis is a molecular genetic test used to evaluate biological relationships through the paternal lineage by analysing polymorphic short tandem repeat (STR) markers located on the male-specific Y chromosome. Using the Thermo Fisher Scientific Yfiler\'99 Plus PCR Amplification Kit, the assay amplifies 27 Y-STR loci following DNA extraction, with subsequent capillary electrophoresis, allele calling, Y-haplotype generation and statistical kinship analysis. Buccal (oral) swabs are the preferred specimen, although EDTA whole blood is also suitable. The expected turnaround time is *3 working days* from receipt of an adequate specimen. The test is primarily indicated for paternal lineage verification, including father-son, paternal grandfather-grandson, brother-to-brother and paternal uncle-nephew relationship testing, as well as forensic human identification, missing persons investigations, disaster victim identification and complex kinship cases where the alleged father is unavailable or deceased. Matching Y-STR haplotypes are consistent with a shared paternal lineage but do not independently establish a specific biological relationship, since males from the same paternal family generally share identical or highly similar Y-chromosome profiles. Conversely, non-matching haplotypes effectively exclude a shared recent paternal lineage, except in the rare event of a Y-STR mutation. As this assay evaluates only the paternal lineage, it cannot distinguish between closely related males within the same paternal family or assess maternal relationships. It should not replace autosomal STR analysis for routine paternity testing when the alleged father is available. Reports include specimen details, the Y-STR haplotype, comparison of tested individuals, an interpretation of whether the findings are consistent with or exclude a shared paternal lineage, and an interpretive comment outlining the limitations of Y-STR analysis together with recommendations for complementary autosomal STR testing where appropriate.

Pre-Collection Instructions: Do not eat, drink, smoke, chew gum, or brush teeth for at least 30 minutes prior to sample collection. Rinse the mouth with clean water and wait 10 minutes before swabbing. 6. Swab Collection Procedure: Wear gloves throughout the procedure. Using one sterile swab, firmly rub the inside of the cheek in a back-and-forth motion for 30-60 seconds to collect epithelial cells. Repeat with a second swab on the opposite cheek. Allow swabs to air dry for at least 15-20 minutes. Do not blow on or touch the swab head. 7. Packaging the Samples: Place the dried swabs into the labeled paper envelope or specimen tube (do not use plastic bags or airtight containers). 8. Ensure each sample is properly sealed and labeled. 9. Documentation: Complete and sign all required documentation, including consent and identification forms. Ensure accurate linkage of sample ID to the donor's identity. 10. Deliver to the laboratory under standard room temperature conditions. Avoid exposure to moisture or heat.
Description: Y-Chromosome Short Tandem Repeat (Y-STR) analysis is a molecular genetic test used to evaluate biological relationships through the paternal lineage by analysing polymorphic short tandem repeat (STR) markers located on the male-specific Y chromosome. Using the Thermo Fisher Scientific Yfiler\'99 Plus PCR Amplification Kit, the assay amplifies 27 Y-STR loci following DNA extraction, with subsequent capillary electrophoresis, allele calling, Y-haplotype generation and statistical kinship analysis. Buccal (oral) swabs are the preferred specimen, although EDTA whole blood is also suitable. The expected turnaround time is *3 working days* from receipt of an adequate specimen. The test is primarily indicated for paternal lineage verification, including father-son, paternal grandfather-grandson, brother-to-brother and paternal uncle-nephew relationship testing, as well as forensic human identification, missing persons investigations, disaster victim identification and complex kinship cases where the alleged father is unavailable or deceased. Matching Y-STR haplotypes are consistent with a shared paternal lineage but do not independently establish a specific biological relationship, since males from the same paternal family generally share identical or highly similar Y-chromosome profiles. Conversely, non-matching haplotypes effectively exclude a shared recent paternal lineage, except in the rare event of a Y-STR mutation. As this assay evaluates only the paternal lineage, it cannot distinguish between closely related males within the same paternal family or assess maternal relationships. It should not replace autosomal STR analysis for routine paternity testing when the alleged father is available. Reports include specimen details, the Y-STR haplotype, comparison of tested individuals, an interpretation of whether the findings are consistent with or exclude a shared paternal lineage, and an interpretive comment outlining the limitations of Y-STR analysis together with recommendations for complementary autosomal STR testing where appropriate.

name: Ascitic Fluid Urea & Creatinine – Uroperitoneum Evaluation
text:
Test code: 7272
Test name: Ascitic Fluid Urea & Creatinine – Uroperitoneum Evaluation
Specimen: ASCITIC FLUID,Serum
Collection instructions: Collect 1 2 mL of ascitic/peritoneal fluid in a sterile, leak-proof plain container. A paired serum sample should be collected at approximately the same time for measurement and comparison of serum urea and creatinine levels. Clearly label the fluid specimen as ascitic/peritoneal fluid and provide relevant clinical details, including suspected uroperitoneum or urinary tract leakage. Transport promptly to the laboratory.
Description: Measurement of urea and creatinine in ascitic/peritoneal fluid, with comparison to corresponding serum levels, to aid in the evaluation of suspected uroperitoneum (urinary ascites) resulting from urinary tract leakage or rupture. Ascitic fluid creatinine levels higher than the corresponding serum creatinine, particularly an elevated fluid-to-serum creatinine ratio, may support the presence of urine within the peritoneal cavity. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings and appropriate imaging studies.
Reported turnaround: One Hour
Report date: 1-Hour
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 2990.0

name: ERG (ETS-Related Gene) Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
text:
Test code: 6741
Test name: ERG (ETS-Related Gene) Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
Also known as: ERG Clone EP111 IHC
Specimen: BLOCKS
Collection instructions: Specimen Instructions Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue block (preferred), together with the histopathology report.
Description: ERG (ETS-Related Gene) is a nuclear immunohistochemical marker used in the evaluation of selected neoplasms. It is a highly sensitive marker of endothelial differentiation and is useful in confirming vascular tumours such as angiosarcoma, epithelioid hemangioendothelioma and Kaposi sarcoma. ERG is also expressed in approximately 40-60% of prostate adenocarcinomas due to TMPRSS2-ERG gene fusion and may support a prostatic origin when interpreted alongside morphology and other prostate markers (e.g. NKX3.1, PSA and PSMA). Results should always be interpreted in conjunction with the histopathological findings and the full immunohistochemical panel. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

text:

Also known as: CD4/CD8 Pleaural Fluid ratio;Fluid Flow Cytometry Pleural fluid

Description: Flow Cytometry Pleural Fluid T-Lymphocyte Subset analysis is performed to identify and quantify T-cell populations within pleural fluid, including CD3+ total T lymphocytes, CD4+ helper T cells, and CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, with determination of the CD4/CD8 ratio. The test may support the clinical evaluation of pleural effusions where assessment of local immune cell populations is indicated, including selected inflammatory, infectious, immunological, and lymphoproliferative conditions. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with the patient's clinical findings, pleural fluid characteristics, cytology, microbiology, and other relevant laboratory investigations.

text:

Description: Therapeutic venesection is the planned removal of a prescribed volume of whole blood to reduce iron stores or red-cell mass. It may be used in the management of conditions such as hereditary haemochromatosis, polycythaemia vera and selected cases of secondary erythrocytosis, following assessment and authorisation by the responsible clinician. The procedure record documents the clinical indication, prescribed and actual volume removed, relevant pre-procedure haemoglobin or haematocrit, patient observations, tolerance and any adverse events. Blood collected during therapeutic venesection is not intended for transfusion and will be managed in accordance with local policy unless collected through an approved blood-donation pathway.

name: TB PCR (Tissue in Formalin)
text:
Test code: 7132
Test name: TB PCR (Tissue in Formalin)
Also known as: PCR for TB; (Tissue in Formalin)
Collection instructions: Submit the formalin-fixed tissue specimen required for TB PCR (Tissue in Formalin), clearly labelled with the tissue site and relevant clinical information. Confirm current referral-laboratory acceptance and processing requirements.
Description: The TB PCR with INH and RIF Sensitivity (Molecular Drug Resistance Testing) assay detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) DNA in tissue and simultaneously screens for common mutations associated with resistance to Rifampicin (RIF) and Isoniazid (INH)-the two most important first-line anti-TB drugs. It provides rapid results that can guide early treatment decisions, particularly in settings where multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) is a concern. However, molecular assays detect only the most frequent resistance-conferring mutations, so phenotypic culture-based drug susceptibility testing remains essential to confirm results and identify resistance to other drugs. A negative PCR does not exclude TB, and results must be interpreted alongside histology, culture, and clinical findings. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks
Report date: 2-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) Platelet Factor 4 (PF4) Antibody (Anti-PF4/Heparin IgG)
text:
Test code: 6437
Test name: Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) Platelet Factor 4 (PF4) Antibody (Anti-PF4/Heparin IgG)
Also known as: PF4-Heparin Antibody; Anti-PF4/Heparin IgG; PF4-H Antibody; Heparin-PF4 IgG Antibody; HIT Immunoassay
Specimen: Platelet-Poor Plasma (PPP)
Collection instructions: Sample Type Platelet-Poor Plasma (PPP) prepared from sodium citrate whole blood. Sample Collection Instructions - Collect 3-5 mL whole blood into one Blue Top (3.2% sodium citrate) tube - Mix gently but thoroughly by 5-10 inversions immediately after collection. - Prepare platelet-poor plasma (PPP) within 1 hour of collection by double centrifugation (or according to validated laboratory protocol). - Overnight fasting is preferred. - Clinical history is mandatory, including: - Heparin exposure (UFH or LMWH) - Date of heparin initiation - Platelet count trend - Clinical suspicion/4Ts score (if available) - Presence of thrombosis or other HIT-related features
Description: The Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) Antibody (Anti-PF4/Heparin IgG), Quantitative assay detects IgG antibodies directed against complexes of platelet factor 4 (PF4) and heparin. It is used in the evaluation of suspected immune-mediated heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), a potentially life-threatening complication of unfractionated or low-molecular-weight heparin characterised by thrombocytopenia with an increased risk of arterial and venous thrombosis. This quantitative CLIA assay should always be interpreted in conjunction with the patient's clinical probability (e.g. 4Ts score), timing of heparin exposure, platelet count trend, and evidence of thrombosis. A positive result indicates the presence of anti-PF4/heparin IgG antibodies but does not by itself confirm clinically significant HIT. Where indicated, confirmation with a functional platelet activation assay may be recommended. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 22990.0

name: Factor XIII Activity Assay (FXIII:C)
text:
Test code: 6438
Test name: Factor XIII Activity Assay (FXIII:C)
Also known as: Factor XIII Functional Assay; Coagulation Factor XIII Activity; Factor XIII (13) Activity
Specimen: Platelet-poor Citrated Plasma
Collection instructions: Sample Instructions: Collect 3 mL whole blood in one Blue Top (3.2% sodium citrate) tube. Mix gently by inversion immediately after collection. Centrifuge within 1 hour of collection to prepare platelet-poor plasma (PPP). Transfer plasma into a properly labelled plastic transport tube and freeze if transport to the reference laboratory will be delayed. Avoid haemolysed, lipaemic or clotted specimens. Clinical history, including bleeding manifestations, family history, recent surgery or trauma, and any recent plasma products or Factor XIII replacement therapy, should accompany the request.
Description: The Factor XIII Activity Assay (FXIII:C) is a quantitative functional assay used to evaluate the activity of coagulation Factor XIII, the enzyme responsible for stabilising fibrin clots by cross-linking fibrin strands after clot formation. Factor XIII deficiency is a rare but important cause of bleeding in patients with normal PT/INR and APTT results, as routine coagulation tests do not assess Factor XIII function. This assay is indicated in patients with unexplained delayed postoperative or post-traumatic bleeding, recurrent soft tissue or intracranial haemorrhage, umbilical stump bleeding in neonates, poor wound healing, recurrent pregnancy loss, or suspected congenital or acquired Factor XIII deficiency. Reduced activity may require follow-up testing with Factor XIII antigen assays, Factor XIII inhibitor studies, and, where clinically indicated, F13A1/F13B genetic testing This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 7990.0

A negative result does not completely exclude infection, particularly when the bacterial load is low, sampling is performed late in the illness, or antibiotics have already been administered. name: Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH), CSF
text:
Test code: 7281
Test name: Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH), CSF
Also known as: CSF LDH; LDH CSF; Lactate Dehydrogenase CSF; Cerebrospinal Fluid LDH; LDH – Cerebrospinal Fluid
Specimen: CSF
Description: Cerebrospinal fluid lactate dehydrogenase (CSF LDH) measures the activity of the intracellular enzyme lactate dehydrogenase within cerebrospinal fluid. LDH may be released into CSF following cellular injury, inflammation or increased cellular turnover within the central nervous system. Increased CSF LDH concentrations have been described in association with central nervous system infections, particularly bacterial meningitis, intracranial haemorrhage, malignant involvement of the central nervous system and other conditions causing tissue or cellular injury. CSF LDH is a non-specific biochemical marker and should not be used independently to establish a diagnosis. Results should be interpreted together with the patient's clinical presentation and other CSF investigations, particularly total and differential cell counts, protein, glucose, Gram stain/culture or molecular microbiological investigations, and cytology or flow cytometry where malignancy is suspected. Blood contamination of CSF may increase LDH activity and should be considered when interpreting an elevated result. Testing is performed by a kinetic photometric enzymatic method based on the IFCC principle using the Roche cobas c 503 clinical chemistry system. The cobas c 503 platform accommodates CSF specimens; however, the Roche LDHI2 reagent manufacturer's stated intended specimen types are serum and plasma. Use of the assay for CSF should therefore be supported by the laboratory's documented verification of the alternative specimen application and locally verified or appropriately adopted reference values.
Reported turnaround: DAILY
Report date: 8-Hours
Testing days: DAILY
Standard price (KES): 990.0

name: NGS KRAS/NRAS/HRAS/BRAF/PIK3CA/TP53 Extended 6-Gene Panel
text:
Test code: 6450
Test name: NGS KRAS/NRAS/HRAS/BRAF/PIK3CA/TP53 Extended 6-Gene Panel
Also known as: NGS 6-Gene Solid Tumour Panel; RAS/RAF/PIK3CA Extended NGS Panel Extended RAS/RAF Mutation Panel; Colorectal Cancer 6-Gene NGS Panel
Specimen: BLOCKS
Collection instructions: Submit a representative FFPE tumour tissue block or unstained sections from a histologically confirmed tumour. Where possible, the specimen should contain adequate viable tumour for molecular analysis. A corresponding H&E-stained slide and histopathology report should accompany the specimen where available. Tumour-rich areas may be selected or macrodissected where required to optimise tumour content.
Description: The NGS KRAS/NRAS/HRAS/BRAF/PIK3CA/TP53 Extended 6-Gene Panel is a targeted next-generation sequencing assay for detection of clinically relevant somatic mutations in KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA and TP53 in solid tumours. The panel evaluates key molecular alterations involving the RAS/MAPK and PI3K signalling pathways together with TP53 tumour-suppressor abnormalities, which may have diagnostic, prognostic, predictive or therapeutic significance depending on the tumour type and clinical context. The assay is particularly useful in the molecular characterisation of colorectal carcinoma, including extended RAS and BRAF assessment, and may also be applicable to other solid tumours such as lung, pancreatic, thyroid and endometrial carcinomas, melanoma, and other malignancies in which alterations involving these genes may influence targeted therapy selection, treatment response, resistance profiling or tumour classification. The assay primarily detects single nucleotide variants (SNVs) and small insertions/deletions (indels) within the targeted genomic regions analysed. Results should be interpreted together with the histopathological diagnosis, tumour type, tumour cellularity, clinical context and other relevant molecular or immunohistochemical findings. This is a focused six-gene targeted panel and does not constitute comprehensive genomic profiling. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 4 Weeks
Report date: 4-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 53990.0

name: MYO (Myoglobin)
text:
Test code: 7289
Test name: MYO (Myoglobin)
Also known as: Myoglobin
Specimen: Serum,Lithium Heparin
Description: Myoglobin is a small oxygen-binding protein (17.8 kDa) found in cardiac and skeletal muscle, measured in serum or plasma to aid in the early diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). It is rapidly released into the bloodstream within ~2 hours of myocardial injury and peaks within 3 hours, especially after reperfusion therapy. Because of its quick rise and elimination (via kidneys within 24 hours), it serves as an early but non-specific marker for myocardial damage. Elevated levels can also result from skeletal muscle injury or renal impairment.
Reported turnaround: One Hour

text:
Test code: 3554 Test name: Dengue Fever PCR (Part of Tropical Fever Panel by PCR) Also known as: Dengue Fever PCR (Part of Tropical Fever Panel by PCR) Specimen: EDTA (Whole Blood) Collection instructions:

Collect the approved blood or named specimen for Dengue Fever PCR (Part of Tropical Fever Panel by PCR). Send with the clinical indication and any prior molecular results. Confirm the current referral-laboratory requirement if this test is sent out.

Description:

The Tropical Fever Panel is a real-time PCR-based molecular test designed to rapidly detect common infectious causes of acute febrile illness in tropical regions. name: Electron Microscopy (Tissue)
text:
Test code: 9061
Test name: Electron Microscopy (Tissue)
Also known as: Electron Microscopy (Specimen in EM Fixative)
Specimen: TISSUE
Collection instructions: Submit tissue biopsies immediately in 3% buffered glutaraldehyde solution. Ensure the specimen is fully immersed in fixative and appropriately labelled. Do not place tissue intended for electron microscopy in formalin.
Description: Electron microscopy (EM) is a specialized ultrastructural examination used to assess cellular and subcellular morphology at high resolution. It may be performed on appropriately collected tissue or cellular specimens where detailed evaluation of organelles, membranes, inclusions, deposits, cilia or other ultrastructural features may assist in diagnosis. Findings are interpreted in conjunction with the clinical information, light microscopy, immunohistochemistry and other relevant laboratory investigations. Diagnostic yield depends on appropriate specimen selection, fixation and preservation. EM is particularly valuable in the diagnosis and classification of mitochondrial myopathies, congenital myopathies, myofibrillar myopathies, inclusion body myositis, storage disorders, vacuolar myopathies and selected muscular dystrophies. It is performed as an adjunct to routine histology, histochemistry, immunohistochemistry and molecular genetic testing to provide comprehensive clinicopathological correlation.
Reported turnaround: 3 Weeks
Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 23990.0

name: Urine Beta-2 microglobulin (B2MG)
text:
Test code: 7241
Test name: Urine Beta-2 microglobulin (B2MG)
Also known as: Beta-2 microglobulin (B2MG) UrineB2MG Urine
Specimen: Urine
Description: Urine beta-2 microglobulin test measures the level of a protein called beta-2 microglobulin in the urine, which is primarily used as an indicator of kidney damage, particularly damage to the proximal tubules in the kidney, as elevated levels suggest that the kidneys are not properly reabsorbing this protein, which should normally be filtered out but mostly reabsorbed back into the bloodstream; therefore, a high level in the urine indicates potential kidney dysfunction. Increased urine beta-2 microglobulin levels reflect tubular disorders of the kidney. In such cases, serum beta2 microglobulin levels are usually normal, since the dysfunction is in tubular reabsorption.
Reported turnaround: 2 Weeks

text:
Test code: 4598
Test name: Methionine Quantitative, Plasma
Also known as: Plasma methionine; Quantitative plasma methionine; Methionine level;
Specimen: EDTA (Plasma)
Collection instructions: Collect blood in an EDTA tube and separate sufficient plasma to provide 3 mL. Transfer into a labelled aliquot tube. Confirm patient preparation, processing, storage and transport requirements with the reference laboratory before collection.
Description: Quantitative plasma methionine supports the investigation of suspected disorders of methionine metabolism, including hypermethioninaemia and homocystinuria, and biochemical monitoring of patients with an established diagnosis. Methionine and homocysteine are separate measurements; their combined pattern helps guide further metabolic and genetic investigations. In confirmed metabolic disease, serial measurements support specialist assessment of treatment response and adjustment of dietary methionine restriction or other prescribed therapy. Description: Quantitative urine methionine assesses urinary methionine excretion and may support investigation of amino-acid metabolism or renal tubular transport disorders. name: Drug Allergy Antibiotics Panel x28 Drugs
text:
Test code: 1137
Test name: Drug Allergy Antibiotics Panel x28 Drugs
Also known as: Antibiotic Allergy Panel; Drug-Specific IgE Panel; 28-Drug Allergy Panel; Antibiotic Hypersensitivity Panel; Antibiotic IgE Allergy Testing;
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect blood in 2 Serum Separator Tubes (SSTs) to obtain a minimum of 5 mL serum. Allow blood to clot, centrifuge and separate serum into appropriately labelled containers. Avoid haemolysed or contaminated specimens.
Description: The Drug Allergy Antibiotics Panel (28 Drugs) is a serum-based enzyme immunoassay (EIA) that measures drug-specific immunoglobulin E (IgE) antibodies against 28 antibiotic and related drug antigens. The panel includes penicillins, cephalosporins, macrolides, tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, sulfonamides and other antimicrobial agents. Results are reported quantitatively in IU/mL and classified into seven IgE reactivity classes (0 6), ranging from clinically insignificant to extremely high according to the reference laboratory's assay-specific thresholds. The test is intended as an adjunct in the evaluation of suspected IgE-mediated antibiotic hypersensitivity, particularly in patients with a history of allergic reactions following antibiotic exposure. Results require correlation with the implicated medication, clinical presentation, timing and severity of the reaction, and previous drug exposures. A positive result indicates detectable IgE reactivity but does not independently confirm clinical drug allergy, while a negative result does not exclude drug hypersensitivity, including non-IgE-mediated reactions. The clinical diagnostic performance of individual drug assays may be limited or inadequately validated. Specialist allergy assessment, including validated skin testing or supervised drug provocation where appropriate, may be necessary to establish the diagnosis and guide safe antibiotic selection. Test is performed at our reference lab network. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After One Week
Report date: 1-Week
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU

name: Drug Allergy Panel x7 Drugs (Antibiotics & Paracetamol)
text:
Test code: 1138
Test name: Drug Allergy Panel x7 Drugs (Antibiotics & Paracetamol)
Also known as: Drug Allergy Panel – 7 Parameters; Drug-Specific IgE Panel; Antibiotic and Paracetamol Allergy Panel; Medication Hypersensitivity Panel; Drug Allergy Screen;
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect blood in a Serum Separator Tube (SST). Allow blood to clot, centrifuge and separate serum into an appropriately labelled container. Avoid haemolysed or contaminated specimens. The minimum serum volume and storage/transport conditions should be confirmed with the reference laboratory.
Description: The Drug Allergy Panel (7 Drugs) is a serum-based immunoassay panel that measures drug-specific immunoglobulin E (IgE) antibodies against seven medications: Penicillin G, Penicillin V, Ampicillin, Amoxicillin, Neomycin, Gentamicin and Paracetamol. The panel additionally includes total serum IgE measurement. Drug-specific IgE antibodies are measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), while total IgE is measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA). Results are reported quantitatively in IU/mL, with drug-specific IgE concentrations classified into seven reactivity classes (0 6) according to the reference laboratory's assay-specific thresholds. The panel is intended as an adjunct in evaluating suspected immediate, IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reactions to selected antibiotics and paracetamol. Clinical indications include suspected medication-related urticaria, angioedema, anaphylaxis or other immediate allergic reactions. Results must be interpreted alongside the patient's medication exposure history, timing and nature of symptoms, and previous allergic reactions. A positive result indicates detectable IgE reactivity but does not independently establish clinical drug allergy, while a negative result does not exclude drug hypersensitivity, including delayed or non-IgE-mediated reactions. Total IgE is a nonspecific marker and cannot independently diagnose drug allergy. Specialist allergy assessment and validated testing may be required to confirm the diagnosis and guide safe medication selection. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.

Avoid haemolysed or contaminated specimens. The minimum serum volume and storage/transport conditions should be confirmed with the reference laboratory.
Description: The Drug Allergy Panel (10 Drugs) is a serum-based immunoassay panel that measures drug-specific immunoglobulin E (IgE) antibodies against ten commonly used antibiotics and analgesic/antipyretic medications. The panel includes six antibiotics (Amoxicillin, Ciprofloxacin, Ampicillin, Cloxacillin, Erythromycin and Ofloxacin) and four analgesic/antipyretic agents (Ibuprofen, Diclofenac, Paracetamol and Aspirin). Total serum IgE measurement is also included. Drug-specific IgE antibodies are measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), while total IgE is measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA). Results are reported quantitatively in IU/mL, with drug-specific IgE concentrations classified into seven reactivity classes (0 6) according to the reference laboratory's assay-specific thresholds. The panel is intended as an adjunct in evaluating suspected immediate drug hypersensitivity reactions, including urticaria, angioedema, anaphylaxis and other symptoms occurring after exposure to the listed medications. It covers selected antibiotic and analgesic agents, although aspirin and other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) hypersensitivity reactions are frequently mediated by non-IgE mechanisms and cannot be reliably diagnosed or excluded using serum-specific IgE testing. Results require careful correlation with the clinical history, implicated medication and timing of symptoms. A positive result does not independently confirm clinical allergy, while a negative result does not exclude drug hypersensitivity. Specialist allergy assessment, including validated skin testing or supervised drug provocation where appropriate, may be required to establish the diagnosis and guide safe medication selection. name: Histoplasma Antibody (Immunodiffusion)
text:
Test code: 1140
Test name: Histoplasma Antibody (Immunodiffusion)
Also known as: Histoplasma capsulatum Antibody; Histoplasmosis Serology; Histoplasma Antibodies; Histoplasma Immunodiffusion (ID); Histoplasma H and M Antibodies.
Specimen: Serum
Collection instructions: Collect 1 2 mL of serum from a serum separator tube (SST). Allow blood to clot, centrifuge and separate serum. Refrigerate at 2 8\'b0C pending dispatch. Avoid haemolysed or contaminated samples. TAT: Samples submitted during the first week of each month. Results available 2 3 weeks after submission to the reference laboratory.
Description: The Histoplasma Antibody test uses immunodiffusion to detect antibodies against Histoplasma capsulatum, the causative organism of histoplasmosis. It is indicated in patients with suspected pulmonary or disseminated histoplasmosis, particularly those presenting with persistent respiratory symptoms, pulmonary nodules, granulomatous lung lesions or relevant environmental exposure. Detection of H and/or M precipitin bands supports exposure or infection, with H-band antibodies more suggestive of active disease and M-band antibodies potentially persisting following previous infection. A positive result should be interpreted alongside clinical presentation, radiological findings and other laboratory investigations, as seropositivity alone does not establish active infection. A negative result does not exclude histoplasmosis, particularly in early infection, immunocompromised patients or localised disease. Where clinical suspicion persists, additional investigations such as Histoplasma urine or serum antigen testing, fungal culture, molecular testing or tissue biopsy with histopathological examination may be necessary to establish the diagnosis and guide antifungal treatment decisions. This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: 2-3 Weeks
Report date: 3-Weeks
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 17990.0

metadata.description: This Inhalation Allergy Panel by Line Immunoassay on EUROBLOTOne includes specific IgE testing against Bermuda grass, Timothy grass, cultivated rye, cultivated wheat, ox-eye daisy, wall pellitory (P. officinalis and P. judaica), weed mix, alder, birch, oak, olive tree, white pine, cypress, tree mix, Penicillium notatum, Cladosporium herbarum, Aspergillus fumigatus, Candida albicans, Alternaria alternata, house-dust mites (Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus and D. farinae), cat, dog, horse, chicken feathers, animal hair mix, cage bird mix, latex, honey bee venom, common wasp venom, German cockroach and mosquito. It provides a comprehensive assessment of sensitisation to seasonal pollens, perennial indoor allergens, moulds, animals, insects and other relevant environmental triggers. The panel supports the investigation of suspected IgE-mediated conditions such as allergic rhinitis, conjunctivitis and allergic asthma.

name: LIN-28 Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
text:
Test code: 7203
Test name: LIN-28 Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
Also known as: LIN-28 IHC; LIN28 IHC; LIN28A
Collection instructions: Submit a representative FFPE block containing viable tumour. Ensure the block identifiers match those on the request form. Include the relevant histopathology report and clinical indication.
Description: IHC-LIN-28 detects LIN-28 protein expression in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumour tissue. The stain can support the diagnosis of selected germ cell tumours and, in the paediatric central nervous system, embryonal tumour with multilayered rosettes (ETMR). Interpret staining in conjunction with tumour morphology, the anatomical site and other immunohistochemical findings. Molecular testing may be required for definitive tumour classification This test is referred to a partner reference laboratory when it is not available in-house at DKL.
Reported turnaround: After 10 Days
Report date: 10-Days
Testing days: SUN, TUE & THU
Standard price (KES): 6690.0
